# Chart

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add chart` or `dx components add chart --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `table`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::chart::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

Charts drawn as SVG in Rust, coloured from theme tokens. No JavaScript chart library.

- `BarChart`, `LineChart`, `AreaChart`: give `data: Vec<ChartDatum>` for one series, or `categories: Vec<String>` and `series: Vec<ChartSeries>` for several. Bars sit side by side or, with `stacked: true`, on top of each other; areas overlap translucently or stack.
- `PieChart`: shares of a total from `data`. `donut: true` cuts a hole, with `center` and `center_caption` text inside it.
- `RadarChart`: one axis per category around a circle and one closed shape per series, for comparing profiles across the same measures. Takes `data`, or `categories` and `series`, like `LineChart`; `max` sets the value at the outer ring (otherwise a round number above the largest value).
- `RadialChart`: one `value` out of `max` (default 100) as a ring, with the percentage (or `center`) in the middle and an optional `caption`.
- `ChartLegend`: the colour key. Charts with two or more series, and pie charts, show one; `legend: false` hides it, `legend: Some(true)` forces it.
- `table: true` adds a "Show data" disclosure with the numbers as a table.
- `keyboard: true` (bar, line, area, pie and radar charts) makes the chart one tab stop: the arrow keys move between points, and the point under the cursor is outlined and named in a status line under the chart ("Feb: 305. 2 of 6."). Off by default, so a page full of charts doesn't fill the tab order; turn it on for charts people need to read point by point.

```rust
AreaChart {
    categories: vec!["Jan".into(), "Feb".into(), "Mar".into()],
    series: vec![
        ChartSeries::new("Desktop", [186.0, 305.0, 237.0]),
        ChartSeries::new("Mobile", [80.0, 200.0, 120.0]),
    ],
    stacked: true,
    table: true,
    label: "Visitors by device, January to March",
}
PieChart { data: plans, donut: true, center: "42", center_caption: "Customers", label: "Customers by plan" }
RadarChart {
    categories: vec!["Speed".into(), "Battery".into(), "Camera".into()],
    series: vec![ChartSeries::new("Phone A", [8.0, 6.0, 9.0]), ChartSeries::new("Phone B", [6.0, 9.0, 6.0])],
    max: 10.0,
    keyboard: true,
    label: "Two phones scored out of 10",
}
RadialChart { value: 89.6, max: 100.0, caption: "of target", label: "Q3 revenue against target" }
```

## Colours

Series 1 uses `--chart-1` when you set it and the accent (`--accent-color`) otherwise; series 2 to 5 use `--chart-2` … `--chart-5` from `theme.css`, and a sixth series starts again at 1. Every shipped colour keeps 3:1 against the page in light and dark. Set the tokens on `:root` or on any container to recolour charts:

```css
.sales { --chart-1: #2563eb; --chart-2: #f59e0b; }
```

## Accessibility

- Role and name: each chart is `role="img"` named by `label`, with a `<desc>` that lists every value (`describe`, `describe_series`, `describe_shares`). Radial charts read "64 of 100 (64%)" (`UiStrings::value_of_max`).
- Hover: each bar, point and slice has a `<title>` with its value; line and area charts also show every series' value for the column under the pointer.
- Not by colour alone: line and area series also differ by dash pattern, matched in the legend; `table: true` gives a keyboard-reachable table of the numbers.
- Focus: without `keyboard` a chart is a static image, not a tab stop. With it, the chart is a `role="group"` named by `label` and described by a hint ("Use the arrow keys to move between points.", `UiStrings::chart_keys_hint`); the cursor starts on the first point when focus arrives, and a `role="status"` line reads the point (`UiStrings::chart_point`). The keys are in the table below. The "Show data" toggle is a native `<summary>` (Enter or Space).
- Reduced motion: bars grow, areas, lines, radar shapes and slices fade in, and the radial ring slides to a new value only under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.

## Stability

Experimental; see `docs/STABILITY.md` in the kit repository.

## Keyboard and accessibility

Pattern: Chart with keyboard point navigation (no APG pattern). Roles: `group`, `img`, `status`. Works on native (Blitz): partly.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tab | Before the chart | Focuses the chart; the cursor starts on the first point, which is announced. | not yet |
| ArrowRight | On the chart | Moves to the next category's point. | yes |
| ArrowLeft | On the chart | Moves to the previous category's point; stops at the first. | yes |
| ArrowDown | On the chart | Moves to the next series at the same category (with one series, the next point). | yes |
| ArrowUp | On the chart | Moves to the previous series at the same category (with one series, the previous point). | yes |
| Home | On the chart | Moves to the first category. | yes |
| End | On the chart | Moves to the last category. | yes |

States:

- `exploring`: The chart has focus: the point under the cursor is outlined and named in the status line.

Native: Tabbing into the chart does not start the cursor on Blitz yet (the status line stays empty); the arrow keys work once it has focus.

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
/// One point, bar or slice.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub struct ChartDatum {
    pub label: String,
    pub value: f32,
}

/// One named series for a multi-series chart: one value per category, in the order of the
/// chart's `categories`. Missing values count as zero.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub struct ChartSeries {
    pub name: String,
    pub values: Vec<f32>,
}

/// How a [`ChartLegend`] draws each entry's marker.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub enum LegendMarker {
    /// A filled square, for bars and slices.
    #[default]
    Square,
    /// A short line in the series' dash pattern, for line and area charts.
    Line,
}

/// Round `max` up to a "nice" axis limit (1, 2, 5 or 10 times a power of ten).
/// Non-positive and non-finite input gives 1, so an empty chart still has an axis.
pub fn nice_max(max: f32) -> f32

/// A plain-language summary for screen readers, since an SVG chart has no text structure.
pub fn describe(data: &[ChartDatum]) -> String

/// [`describe`] for several series: `Desktop: Jan 186, Feb 305. Mobile: Jan 80, Feb 200.`
pub fn describe_series(categories: &[String], series: &[ChartSeries]) -> String

/// Whole-number percentages of the total for each datum (negative and non-finite values count
/// as zero). An all-zero list gives zeros.
pub fn shares(data: &[ChartDatum]) -> Vec<f32>

/// [`describe`] for a pie or donut: each value with its share, `Free: 12 (40%), Pro: 18 (60%)`.
pub fn describe_shares(data: &[ChartDatum]) -> String

/// A move of the keyboard cursor in a chart with `keyboard: true`.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub enum ChartKey {
    /// Right arrow: the next category (bar, point, slice or axis).
    Next,
    /// Left arrow.
    Previous,
    /// Down arrow: the next series in legend order. With one series, the next category.
    NextSeries,
    /// Up arrow.
    PreviousSeries,
    /// Home: the first category.
    First,
    /// End: the last category.
    Last,
}

/// The mark under the keyboard cursor: a category (column, slice or radar axis) and a series.
/// Pure, so the moves are tested without a browser.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub struct ChartCursor {
    pub category: usize,
    pub series: usize,
}

/// The colour key for a multi-series chart, or for the slices of a pie. A list of names, each
/// with a marker in its series' colour (and, for [`LegendMarker::Line`], its dash pattern).
/// Charts render one themselves; use this to place a key elsewhere.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn ChartLegend(items: Vec<String>, #[props(default)] marker: LegendMarker) -> Element {
    rsx!

/// A bar chart drawn as SVG. Give it `data` for one series, or `categories` and `series` for
/// several: side by side, or `stacked`. `label` is read by screen readers along with a summary
/// of every value; hovering a bar shows its value. A legend appears when there are two or
/// more series; `table: true` adds a "Show data" table.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn BarChart(
    #[props(default)] data: Vec<ChartDatum>,
    #[props(default)] categories: Vec<String>,
    #[props(default)] series: Vec<ChartSeries>,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(default = 200.0)] height: f32,
    #[props(default)] stacked: bool,
    #[props(default)] legend: Option<bool>,
    #[props(default)] table: bool,
    /// One tab stop for the chart; the arrow keys then move between its marks (Left/Right
    /// across categories, Up/Down across series, Home/End), and the one under the cursor is
    /// highlighted and announced.
    #[props(default)]
    keyboard: bool,
) -> Element

/// A line chart drawn as SVG with theme colours: `data` for one line, `categories` and
/// `series` for several (each in its own colour and dash pattern). Same accessibility
/// contract as [`BarChart`].
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn LineChart(
    #[props(default)] data: Vec<ChartDatum>,
    #[props(default)] categories: Vec<String>,
    #[props(default)] series: Vec<ChartSeries>,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(default = 200.0)] height: f32,
    #[props(default)] legend: Option<bool>,
    #[props(default)] table: bool,
    /// One tab stop for the chart; the arrow keys then move between its marks (Left/Right
    /// across categories, Up/Down across series, Home/End), and the one under the cursor is
    /// highlighted and announced.
    #[props(default)]
    keyboard: bool,
) -> Element

/// An area chart: lines with the region below them filled. Several series overlap
/// translucently, or sit on top of each other with `stacked`. Same props and accessibility
/// contract as [`LineChart`].
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn AreaChart(
    #[props(default)] data: Vec<ChartDatum>,
    #[props(default)] categories: Vec<String>,
    #[props(default)] series: Vec<ChartSeries>,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(default = 200.0)] height: f32,
    #[props(default)] stacked: bool,
    #[props(default)] legend: Option<bool>,
    #[props(default)] table: bool,
    /// One tab stop for the chart; the arrow keys then move between its marks (Left/Right
    /// across categories, Up/Down across series, Home/End), and the one under the cursor is
    /// highlighted and announced.
    #[props(default)]
    keyboard: bool,
) -> Element

/// A pie chart, or with `donut: true` a ring with an optional `center` value and
/// `center_caption` in the hole. Each slice is a share of the total; hovering a slice shows
/// its value and percentage, the legend names the slices and `table: true` adds a
/// "Show data" table. `size` caps the width in CSS pixels.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn PieChart(
    data: Vec<ChartDatum>,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(default)] donut: bool,
    #[props(default, into)] center: Option<String>,
    #[props(default, into)] center_caption: Option<String>,
    #[props(default = true)] legend: bool,
    #[props(default)] table: bool,
    #[props(default = 200.0)] size: f32,
    /// One tab stop; the arrow keys, Home and End then move between the slices.
    #[props(default)]
    keyboard: bool,
) -> Element

/// A radar (spider) chart: one axis per category, all starting at the centre, and one closed
/// shape per series through its values. Good for comparing a few profiles across the same
/// measures. Give it `data` for one shape, or `categories` and `series` for several (each in
/// its own colour and dash pattern). The axis limit is `max`, or a round number above the
/// largest value. Same accessibility contract as [`LineChart`]; `size` caps the width in CSS
/// pixels.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn RadarChart(
    #[props(default)] data: Vec<ChartDatum>,
    #[props(default)] categories: Vec<String>,
    #[props(default)] series: Vec<ChartSeries>,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    /// The value at the outer ring. Defaults to a round number above the largest value.
    #[props(default)]
    max: Option<f32>,
    #[props(default)] legend: Option<bool>,
    #[props(default)] table: bool,
    #[props(default = 300.0)] size: f32,
    /// One tab stop; Left/Right then move between the axes, Up/Down between the series.
    #[props(default)]
    keyboard: bool,
) -> Element

/// Fraction of `max` that `value` reaches, between 0 and 1 (0 for a non-positive `max`).
pub fn progress(value: f32, max: f32) -> f32

/// A radial (ring) chart for one value out of `max`: a goal, a quota, a score. The centre shows
/// the percentage unless `center` gives other text; `caption` goes under it. Changes animate
/// along the ring, except under reduced motion.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn RadialChart(
    value: f32,
    #[props(default = 100.0)] max: f32,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(default, into)] center: Option<String>,
    #[props(default, into)] caption: Option<String>,
    #[props(default = 160.0)] size: f32,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonSize, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::chart::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

fn monthly() -> Vec<ChartDatum> {
    [
        ("Jan", 186.0),
        ("Feb", 305.0),
        ("Mar", 237.0),
        ("Apr", 73.0),
        ("May", 209.0),
        ("Jun", 214.0),
    ]
    .into_iter()
    .map(|(label, value)| ChartDatum::new(label, value))
    .collect()
}

fn months() -> Vec<String> {
    ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"]
        .map(String::from)
        .to_vec()
}

fn devices() -> Vec<ChartSeries> {
    vec![
        ChartSeries::new("Desktop", [186.0, 305.0, 237.0, 73.0, 209.0, 214.0]),
        ChartSeries::new("Mobile", [80.0, 200.0, 120.0, 190.0, 130.0, 140.0]),
    ]
}

fn browsers() -> Vec<ChartDatum> {
    [
        ("Chrome", 275.0),
        ("Safari", 200.0),
        ("Firefox", 187.0),
        ("Edge", 173.0),
        ("Other", 90.0),
    ]
    .into_iter()
    .map(|(label, value)| ChartDatum::new(label, value))
    .collect()
}

fn skills() -> Vec<String> {
    ["Speed", "Battery", "Camera", "Screen", "Price", "Storage"]
        .map(String::from)
        .to_vec()
}

fn phones() -> Vec<ChartSeries> {
    vec![
        ChartSeries::new("Phone A", [8.0, 6.0, 9.0, 7.0, 4.0, 8.0]),
        ChartSeries::new("Phone B", [6.0, 9.0, 6.0, 8.0, 8.0, 5.0]),
    ]
}

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut goal = use_signal(|| 64.0_f32);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 2rem; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(16rem, 1fr));",
            BarChart { data: monthly(), keyboard: true, label: "Visitors per month, January to June" }
            LineChart { data: monthly(), label: "Visitors per month, January to June (line)" }
            AreaChart {
                categories: months(),
                series: devices(),
                stacked: true,
                table: true,
                label: "Visitors by device, January to June, stacked",
            }
            BarChart { categories: months(), series: devices(), label: "Visitors by device, January to June" }
            LineChart { categories: months(), series: devices(), keyboard: true, label: "Visitors by device, January to June (lines)" }
            RadarChart {
                categories: skills(),
                series: phones(),
                max: 10.0,
                keyboard: true,
                table: true,
                label: "Two phones scored out of 10",
            }
            PieChart {
                data: browsers(),
                donut: true,
                center: "935",
                center_caption: "Visitors",
                table: true,
                label: "Visitors by browser",
            }
            PieChart { data: browsers(), keyboard: true, label: "Visitors by browser (pie)" }
            div { style: "display: grid; gap: 0.75rem; justify-items: center;",
                RadialChart { value: goal(), label: "Monthly goal reached", caption: "of goal" }
                Button {
                    variant: ButtonVariant::Outline,
                    size: ButtonSize::Sm,
                    onclick: move |_| goal.set(if goal() >= 100.0 { 12.0 } else { (goal() + 22.0).min(100.0) }),
                    "Add progress"
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Chat

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add chat` or `dx components add chat --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::chat::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A conversation view for chat and agent apps: `ChatLog` (the scrolling log), `ChatMessage`
(one message, named by its author), `StreamingText` (a reply that arrives a piece at a time)
and `TypingIndicator`. Pair it with [`ChatComposer`](chat_composer) for input and
[`ToolCall`](tool_call) for an agent's tool calls.

```rust
ChatLog { label: "Conversation with Ada", style: "height: 24rem",
    ChatMessage { author: "You", from: ChatRole::User, hide_author: true, "Hi!" }
    ChatMessage { author: "Ada",
        StreamingText { text: reply(), streaming: streaming() }
    }
    if typing() { TypingIndicator { author: "Ada" } }
}
```

## Scrolling

The log follows new content while the reader is at the end, and stops the moment they
scroll up; a "Jump to latest" button then appears (it says "New messages below" once
something arrives) and takes them back, keeping focus in the log. Following is measured, not
event-driven: it re-checks after each render of the log and whenever its content changes
size (a `ResizeObserver` on the web), so streamed text that grows inside a child component is
followed too. On the native renderer, which sends no scroll events, a scroll offset that moved
up since the last follow counts as the reader scrolling away.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: the log is `role="log"` with a required `label` (a compile error without one).
  Each message is an `article` named by its required `author`, so screen reader users can
  move between messages and hear who wrote each. `hide_author` hides the name visually only.
- Live regions: the log is deliberately `aria-live="off"`. A streamed reply changes many times
  a second and would be read in fragments. Instead the log owns a polite announcer:
  `StreamingText` announces "Author: whole reply" once when `streaming` turns off, and
  `TypingIndicator` announces "Author is typing" when it appears. Call
  `use_chat_announcer()` inside the log to announce anything else. Turn `announce` off on
  text the reader sent themselves.
- `StreamingText` sets `aria-busy` while streaming; its caret is decorative.
- The log is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) so it can be scrolled from the keyboard.
- Reduced motion: the caret stops blinking, the typing dots stop bouncing (and stay visible),
  and messages and the jump button appear without rising.

## Source

Original to this repo. The "announce whole messages, not the stream" approach follows
WAI-ARIA's `aria-busy` guidance and common screen reader behaviour with chat logs.

## Stability

Experimental: new on 2026-10-30, and the props may change once a real agent app uses them (docs/STABILITY.md).

## Keyboard and accessibility

Pattern: Log. Roles: `log`. Works on native (Blitz): yes.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | In the message box | Sends the message; it appears at the end of the conversation and focus stays in the box. | yes |

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
/// Says things to screen readers on behalf of a [`ChatLog`].
///
/// The log itself is not a live region: a streamed reply changes dozens of times a second, and
/// screen readers would read every fragment. The log announces whole messages through this
/// instead: [`StreamingText`] says the finished reply, [`TypingIndicator`] says who is typing.
/// Call [`announce`](Self::announce) for anything else worth hearing (a failed tool call, a new
/// message from someone else).
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub struct ChatAnnouncer {
    /// Two polite regions, used in turn, so saying the same text twice is still heard.
    slots: Signal<[String; 2]>,
}

/// The announcer of the enclosing [`ChatLog`], if there is one.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub fn use_chat_announcer() -> Option<ChatAnnouncer>

/// A scrolling conversation. It follows new messages while the reader is at the end, stops
/// when they scroll up, and then shows a "Jump to latest" button (which says "New messages
/// below" once something arrives). Size it with `style` or a class; it fills its parent's
/// height by default.
///
/// `label` is required: the log is a named region (`role="log"`), and a page with an unnamed
/// one gives screen reader users no way to tell conversations apart.
///
/// ```
/// # use dioxus::prelude::*;
/// # use ui::prelude::*;
/// # fn app() -> Element {
/// rsx! {
///     ChatLog { label: "Conversation with Ada",
///         ChatMessage { author: "Ada", from: ChatRole::Assistant, "Hello!" }
///     }
/// }
/// # }
/// ```
///
/// Leaving `label` out is a compile error:
///
/// ```compile_fail,E0061
/// # use dioxus::prelude::*;
/// # use ui::prelude::*;
/// # fn app() -> Element {
/// rsx! { ChatLog { ChatMessage { author: "Ada", "Hello!" } } }
/// # }
/// ```
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn ChatLog(
    /// The conversation's accessible name ("Conversation with Ada").
    #[props(into)]
    label: String,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// Who wrote a [`ChatMessage`]. Sets its alignment and look.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub enum ChatRole {
    /// The person using the app: right-aligned bubble.
    User,
    /// The assistant or another participant: full-width text.
    #[default]
    Assistant,
    /// Notices from the app ("Conversation started"): centred and muted.
    System,
}

/// One message in a [`ChatLog`]: an `article` named by its author, so screen reader users can
/// move from message to message and hear who wrote each.
///
/// `author` is required for the same reason; `hide_author` hides it visually (for the
/// user's own messages, say) while it is still read.
///
/// ```compile_fail,E0061
/// # use dioxus::prelude::*;
/// # use ui::prelude::*;
/// # fn app() -> Element {
/// rsx! { ChatMessage { from: ChatRole::User, "Hi" } }
/// # }
/// ```
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn ChatMessage(
    /// Who wrote it ("You", "Assistant", "Ada").
    #[props(into)]
    author: String,
    #[props(default)] from: ChatRole,
    /// Hide the author's name visually; screen readers still read it.
    #[props(default)]
    hide_author: bool,
    /// When it was sent, as the app wants it shown ("10:42").
    #[props(into)]
    time: Option<String>,
    /// Shown beside the message, decorative (the author's name is the label).
    avatar: Option<Element>,
    /// Buttons under the message (copy, retry). Give each a name.
    actions: Option<Element>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// Text that arrives a piece at a time (a model's reply). Shows a caret while `streaming`,
/// keeps line breaks, and when streaming ends announces the whole text once, with its
/// author, through the [`ChatLog`]'s announcer. Screen readers never hear the fragments.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn StreamingText(
    /// Everything received so far.
    #[props(into)]
    text: String,
    /// More text is still coming.
    #[props(default)]
    streaming: bool,
    /// Announce the finished text (default). Turn off for text the reader has just sent.
    #[props(default = true)]
    announce: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element

/// Three pulsing dots for "someone is writing". The dots are decorative; the text
/// ("Assistant is typing") is read, and announced once when it appears inside a [`ChatLog`].
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn TypingIndicator(
    /// Who is typing. Fills [`UiStrings::typing`](crate::components::ui_strings::UiStrings).
    #[props(into)]
    author: String,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::chat::*;
use crate::components::chat_composer::*;
use crate::components::tool_call::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;
use dioxus_sdk_time::sleep;
use std::time::Duration;

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
enum Item {
    System(String),
    User(String),
    Tool {
        name: &'static str,
        summary: String,
        status: ToolStatus,
    },
    Reply {
        text: String,
        streaming: bool,
    },
}

const ANSWER: &str = "Keep the log pinned to the end while the reader is there, and let go as soon as they scroll up. ChatLog measures instead of listening for scroll events, so this works on the native renderer too. Screen readers hear each reply once, when it is complete, not every fragment as it streams in.";

fn reply_to(question: &str) -> String {
    format!("You asked: “{question}”. {ANSWER}")
}

/// A pretend agent: the reply streams in word by word after a tool call. Nothing leaves the
/// page.
#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut items = use_signal(|| {
        vec![
            Item::System("Conversation started".into()),
            Item::User("How do I keep a chat scrolled to the newest message?".into()),
            Item::Tool {
                name: "search_docs",
                summary: "“scroll to latest”, 3 results".into(),
                status: ToolStatus::Succeeded,
            },
            Item::Reply {
                text: ANSWER.into(),
                streaming: false,
            },
        ]
    });
    let mut busy = use_signal(|| false);
    let mut typing = use_signal(|| false);
    let mut stop = use_signal(|| false);

    let ask = move |question: String| {
        items.write().push(Item::User(question.clone()));
        busy.set(true);
        stop.set(false);
        typing.set(true);
        spawn(async move {
            sleep(Duration::from_millis(500)).await;
            items.write().push(Item::Tool {
                name: "search_docs",
                summary: format!("“{question}”"),
                status: ToolStatus::Running,
            });
            sleep(Duration::from_millis(700)).await;
            if let Some(Item::Tool { status, summary, .. }) = items.write().last_mut() {
                *status = ToolStatus::Succeeded;
                summary.push_str(", 3 results");
            }
            typing.set(false);
            items.write().push(Item::Reply {
                text: String::new(),
                streaming: true,
            });
            for word in reply_to(&question).split_inclusive(' ') {
                if stop() {
                    break;
                }
                sleep(Duration::from_millis(45)).await;
                if let Some(Item::Reply { text, .. }) = items.write().last_mut() {
                    text.push_str(word);
                }
            }
            if let Some(Item::Reply { streaming, .. }) = items.write().last_mut() {
                *streaming = false;
            }
            busy.set(false);
        });
    };

    rsx! {
        div {
            display: "flex",
            flex_direction: "column",
            gap: "0.75rem",
            height: "28rem",
            max_width: "40rem",
            ChatLog { label: "Conversation with the docs assistant",
                for (i, item) in items().into_iter().enumerate() {
                    match item {
                        Item::System(text) => rsx! {
                            ChatMessage { key: "{i}", author: "System", from: ChatRole::System, hide_author: true, "{text}" }
                        },
                        Item::User(text) => rsx! {
                            ChatMessage { key: "{i}", author: "You", from: ChatRole::User, hide_author: true, "{text}" }
                        },
                        Item::Tool { name, summary, status } => rsx! {
                            ToolCall { key: "{i}", name, summary, status,
                                pre { "{{ \"query\": \"scroll to latest\", \"limit\": 3 }}" }
                            }
                        },
                        Item::Reply { text, streaming } => rsx! {
                            ChatMessage { key: "{i}", author: "Assistant",
                                StreamingText { text, streaming }
                            }
                        },
                    }
                }
                if typing() {
                    TypingIndicator { author: "Assistant" }
                }
            }
            ChatComposer {
                label: "Message the docs assistant",
                placeholder: "Ask about the kit…",
                busy: busy(),
                onsend: ask,
                onstop: move |_| stop.set(true),
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Chat composer

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add chat_composer` or `dx components add chat_composer --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `button`, `icons`, `textarea`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::chat_composer::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The message box of a chat. It grows with the text (CSS `field-sizing`, through
[`Textarea`](textarea)'s `autosize`), sends with Enter, adds a line with Shift+Enter, and
turns Send into Stop while a reply is `busy` (Escape stops too). Sending trims the text,
ignores an empty message, empties the box and keeps focus in it. Extra controls (attach, a
model picker) go in its children.

```rust
ChatComposer {
    label: "Message",
    busy: streaming(),
    onsend: move |text: String| ask(text),
    onstop: move |_| cancel(),
}
```

Pass `value: Signal<String>` to hold the draft yourself.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: a text box named by the required `label` (a compile error without one);
  how to send is read after it (`aria-describedby`), and `aria-keyshortcuts="Enter"`.
- IME: Enter that confirms a composition (Japanese, Chinese, Korean input) picks the
  characters and never sends. `composer_key` holds the rule and is unit-tested.
- The send button stays focusable while there is nothing to send (`aria-disabled`, not
  `disabled`), so its name is still found.
- Escape stops a running reply only while `busy`; it is left out of the contract because this
  demo is never busy, and is checked in the browser by `tests/e2e/chat.mjs`.
- Reduced motion: the focus ring appears without a transition.

## Source

Original to this repo.

## Stability

Experimental: new on 2026-10-30, and the props may change once a real agent app uses them (docs/STABILITY.md).

## Keyboard and accessibility

Pattern: Text box with a send button. Works on native (Blitz): yes.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | In the message box | Sends the message, empties the box and keeps focus in it. Does nothing while the box is empty. | yes |
| Shift + Enter | In the message box | Starts a new line instead of sending. | yes |
| Space | On the send button | Sends the message. | yes |

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
/// What a key press in the composer does. Kept apart from the component so the rules are
/// tested on their own (`tests/components/chat_composer.rs`).
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub enum ComposerKey {
    /// Send the message (and keep the newline out of the box).
    Send,
    /// Stop the reply that is streaming.
    Stop,
    /// Let the text box handle it (type, add a line, move the caret).
    Default,
}

/// Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, Escape stops a running reply. Enter that confirms an
/// IME composition (Japanese, Chinese, Korean input) never sends: it picks the characters.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub fn composer_key(key: &Key, shift: bool, composing: bool, busy: bool) -> ComposerKey

/// The message box of a chat: grows with the text, sends on Enter (Shift+Enter for a new
/// line), and turns its send button into Stop while a reply is `busy`. Sending trims the text,
/// ignores an empty message, clears the box and keeps focus in it.
///
/// `label` is required: it is the text box's only accessible name (the placeholder is not
/// one). How to send is read after it.
///
/// ```
/// # use dioxus::prelude::*;
/// # use ui::prelude::*;
/// # fn app() -> Element {
/// rsx! { ChatComposer { label: "Message", onsend: move |text: String| println!("{text}") } }
/// # }
/// ```
///
/// Leaving `label` out is a compile error:
///
/// ```compile_fail,E0061
/// # use dioxus::prelude::*;
/// # use ui::prelude::*;
/// # fn app() -> Element {
/// rsx! { ChatComposer { onsend: move |_: String| {} } }
/// # }
/// ```
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn ChatComposer(
    /// The text box's accessible name ("Message", "Ask the agent").
    #[props(into)]
    label: String,
    /// Called with the trimmed text when the reader sends.
    onsend: EventHandler<String>,
    #[props(into)] placeholder: Option<String>,
    /// A reply is streaming: sending waits, and Stop (with `onstop`) replaces Send.
    #[props(default)]
    busy: bool,
    /// Called by the Stop button and by Escape while `busy`.
    onstop: Option<EventHandler<()>>,
    #[props(default)] disabled: bool,
    /// Hold the draft yourself (to keep it across routes, or fill it from a suggestion).
    /// Without it the composer keeps its own.
    value: Option<Signal<String>>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    /// Extra controls left of the send button (attach, model picker). Name each one.
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{ButtonVariant, IconButton, IconButtonSize};
use crate::components::chat_composer::*;
use crate::components::icons::Paperclip;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut sent = use_signal(Vec::<String>::new);
    rsx! {
        div { display: "flex", flex_direction: "column", gap: "0.75rem", max_width: "32rem",
            ChatComposer {
                label: "Message",
                placeholder: "Write a message…",
                onsend: move |text| sent.write().push(text),
                IconButton {
                    label: "Attach a file",
                    variant: ButtonVariant::Ghost,
                    size: IconButtonSize::Sm,
                    r#type: "button",
                    Paperclip { size: "1rem" }
                }
            }
            if sent().is_empty() {
                p { "data-slot": "sent", style: "margin: 0; color: var(--secondary-color-5); font-size: 0.875rem;",
                    "Nothing sent yet."
                }
            } else {
                ul { "data-slot": "sent", style: "margin: 0; padding-inline-start: 1.25rem; font-size: 0.875rem;",
                    for (i, text) in sent().into_iter().enumerate() {
                        li { key: "{i}", style: "white-space: pre-wrap;", "{text}" }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Checkbox

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add checkbox` or `dx components add checkbox --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`).
- Import: `use crate::components::checkbox::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Checkbox component is used to create an accessible checkbox input.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The checkbox component creates a checkbox button
Checkbox {
    // The checkbox indicator is a child component which will only be visible when the checkbox is checked.
    CheckboxIndicator {
        // The content of the checkbox indicator, typically an icon or image.
        {children}
    }
}
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Checkbox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/checkbox/) pattern. Roles: `checkbox`. Works on native (Blitz): yes.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Space | On the checkbox | Checks or unchecks it. | yes |

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
pub use dioxus_primitives::checkbox::CheckboxState;

#[component]
pub fn Checkbox(props: CheckboxProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::checkbox::*;
use crate::components::label::Label;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem;",
            Checkbox { id: "terms", name: "terms" }
            Label { html_for: "terms", "Accept terms" }
        }
    }
}
```

# Chips

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add chips` or `dx components add chips --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`).
- Import: `use crate::components::chips::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A row of on/off chips for filters and multi-choice tags. Each chip is a native checkbox inside its label; a check mark appears when it is on.

```rust
Chips { label: "Filter by status",
    Chip { default_checked: true, "Open" }
    Chip { "In review" }
    Chip { checked: done(), on_change: move |v| done.set(v), "Done" }
}
```

For one choice out of several, use `ToggleGroup` or `RadioGroup` instead.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: `role="group"` named by `label`; each chip is a native checkbox named by its text
- Keyboard: Tab moves between chips, Space toggles
- State: announced as checked or not checked, and shown with a check mark as well as colour; forced-colors mode outlines the selected chip
- Reduced motion: the check mark and colour change without transition

## Source

Idea from Rust/UI `chips.rs` (rust-ui/ui@43ddc65, MIT). Rewritten: upstream hides the checkbox with `display: none` (unreachable by keyboard and screen readers) and styles with Tailwind; here the checkbox stays focusable and the styles use theme tokens.

## API

```rust
/// A labelled group of [`Chip`]s, for filters and multi-choice tags.
#[component]
pub fn Chips(
    /// Names the group for screen readers, e.g. "Filter by status".
    #[props(into)]
    label: String,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// One on/off chip: a native checkbox inside its label, so Tab reaches it, Space toggles it
/// and screen readers announce "checked". A check mark shows the state as well as the colour.
///
/// Uncontrolled with `default_checked`, or controlled with `checked` plus `on_change`.
#[component]
pub fn Chip(
    /// Controlled state. Leave unset to let the chip keep its own.
    checked: Option<bool>,
    /// Starting state when uncontrolled.
    #[props(default)]
    default_checked: bool,
    #[props(default)] disabled: bool,
    /// Form field name and value, when the chips sit in a `<form>`.
    #[props(into)]
    name: Option<String>,
    #[props(into)] value: Option<String>,
    #[props(default)] on_change: EventHandler<bool>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::chips::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut done = use_signal(|| false);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.75rem;",
            Chips { label: "Filter by status",
                Chip { default_checked: true, "Open" }
                Chip { "In review" }
                Chip { checked: done(), on_change: move |v| done.set(v), "Done" }
                Chip { disabled: true, "Archived" }
            }
            p { style: "margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--secondary-color-5);",
                if done() { "Showing done tasks." } else { "Hiding done tasks." }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Collapsible

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add collapsible` or `dx components add collapsible --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`).
- Import: `use crate::components::collapsible::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The `Collapsible` component allows users to create expandable sections that can be toggled open or closed. This is useful for displaying content in a compact manner, such as FAQs, menus, or any content that benefits from being hidden until needed.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The collapsible component must wrap all collapsible items.
Collapsible {
    // The trigger is used to expand or collapse the item.
    CollapsibleTrigger {}
    // The content that is shown when the item is expanded.
    CollapsibleContent {}
}
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Disclosure (Show/Hide)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/) pattern. Works on native (Blitz): yes.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | On the trigger | Shows or hides the content. | yes |
| Space | On the trigger | Shows or hides the content. | yes |

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Collapsible(props: CollapsibleProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CollapsibleTrigger(props: CollapsibleTriggerProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CollapsibleContent(props: CollapsibleContentProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CollapsibleItem(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn CollapsibleList(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::collapsible::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        Collapsible {
            CollapsibleTrigger {
                b { "Recent Activity" }
            }
            CollapsibleList {
                CollapsibleItem { "Added a new feature to the collapsible component" }
                CollapsibleContent {
                    CollapsibleItem { "Fixed a bug in the collapsible component" }
                    CollapsibleItem { "Updated the documentation for the collapsible component" }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Color picker

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add color_picker` or `dx components add color_picker --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `input`).
- Import: `use crate::components::color_picker::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

Color picker used when the user needs to make a customized color selection.

## Component Structure

```rust
ColorPicker {
    // The currently selected color in the color picker.
    color,
    on_color_change: move |c: Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>| {
        // This callback is triggered when a color is selected in the popover.
        // The HSV parameter contains the selected color.
    },

    // Optional label on the trigger button.
    label: "Pick",
}
```

### Custom Popover

`ColorPicker` renders the default trigger and `ColorPickerSelect` content. If you
want to fully replace the default popover UI, compose the picker from
`ColorPickerRoot`, `ColorPickerTrigger`, and `ColorPickerPopover`:

```rust
ColorPickerRoot {
    color,
    on_color_change: move |c: Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>| { /* ... */ },

    ColorPickerTrigger {
        label: "Pick",
    }

    ColorPickerPopover {
        div {
            "Custom color picker content"
        }
    }
}
```

If you only need to add content after the default controls, pass children to
`ColorPicker`; they will be appended inside the default popover.

## API

```rust
/// The props for the [`ColorPickerRoot`] component.
pub struct ColorPickerRootProps {
    /// The selected color
    #[props(default)]
    pub color: ReadSignal<Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>>,

    /// Callback when color changes
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_color_change: Callback<Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>>,

    /// Whether the color picker is disabled
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// The controlled open state of the popover.
    pub open: ReadSignal<Option<bool>>,

    /// The default open state when uncontrolled.
    #[props(default)]
    pub default_open: bool,

    /// Callback fired when the open state changes.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_open_change: Callback<bool>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the color picker element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The children of the color picker element
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn ColorPickerRoot(props: ColorPickerRootProps) -> Element

/// The props for the [`ColorPicker`] component.
pub struct ColorPickerProps {
    /// The selected color
    #[props(default)]
    pub color: ReadSignal<Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>>,

    /// Callback when color changes
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_color_change: Callback<Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>>,

    /// Whether the color picker is disabled
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// Optional label on the trigger button
    #[props(default)]
    pub label: Option<String>,

    /// The controlled open state of the popover.
    pub open: ReadSignal<Option<bool>>,

    /// The default open state when uncontrolled.
    #[props(default)]
    pub default_open: bool,

    /// Callback fired when the open state changes.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_open_change: Callback<bool>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the color picker element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// Additional content to append to the default color picker popover
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn ColorPicker(props: ColorPickerProps) -> Element

/// The props for the [`ColorPickerTrigger`] component.
pub struct ColorPickerTriggerProps {
    /// Optional label on the trigger button
    #[props(default)]
    pub label: Option<String>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the trigger button
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// Additional content to render inside the trigger button
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn ColorPickerTrigger(props: ColorPickerTriggerProps) -> Element

/// The props for the [`ColorPickerPopover`] component.
pub struct ColorPickerPopoverProps {
    /// Additional attributes to extend the popover content
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The children of the color picker popover
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn ColorPickerPopover(props: ColorPickerPopoverProps) -> Element

/// The props for the [`ColorField`] component.
pub struct ColorFieldProps {
    /// Optional label above the input field
    #[props(default)]
    pub label: Option<String>,

    /// Optional props for the text description element
    #[props(default)]
    pub description: Option<String>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the color field element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The children of the color field element
    pub children: Element,
}

/// The props for the [`ColorSwatch`] component.
pub struct ColorSwatchProps {
    /// The selected color
    #[props(default)]
    pub color: ReadSignal<Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64>>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the color swatch element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The children of the color swatch element
    pub children: Element,
}

/// The props for the [`ColorSlider`] component.
pub struct ColorSliderProps {
    pub title: ReadSignal<String>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the color slider element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The children of the color slider element
    pub children: Element,
}

/// The props for the [`ColorPickerSelect`] component.
pub struct ColorPickerSelectProps {
    /// Additional attributes to extend the color picker select element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]

    /// The children of the color picker select element

```

## Example

```rust
use dioxus::prelude::*;

use crate::components::color_picker::*;
use dioxus_primitives::color_picker::Color;
use palette::{encoding, Hsv, IntoColor};

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut color = use_signal(|| -> Hsv<encoding::Srgb, f64> {
        Color::new(155, 128, 255).into_format::<f64>().into_color()
    });

    rsx! {
        ColorPicker {
            label: "Pick a color",
            color: color(),
            on_color_change: move |c| {
                tracing::info!("Color changed: {:?}", c);
                color.set(c);
            },
        }
    }
}
```

# Combobox

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add combobox` or `dx components add combobox --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`).
- Import: `use crate::components::combobox::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Combobox component is an autocomplete input with a filterable popup list.

Filtering preserves the order defined by the rendered `ComboboxOption` elements and their `index`
props. If you want query-dependent ranking, control `query`, sort your item data in user code,
render the options in that sorted order, and assign indexes from the sorted list.

## Component Structure

```rust
let mut value = use_signal(|| None::<String>);
let mut query = use_signal(String::new);

Combobox::<String> {
    value: Some(value.into()),
    on_value_change: move |next: Option<String>| {
        value.set(next);
    },
    query: Some(query()),
    on_query_change: move |next| query.set(next),
    placeholder: "Select framework...",
    aria_label: "Select framework",
    list_aria_label: "Frameworks",
    ComboboxEmpty { "No framework found." }
    ComboboxOption::<String> {
        index: 0usize,
        value: "next".to_string(),
        text_value: "Next.js",
        "Next.js"
    }
}
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Combobox (list autocomplete)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/) pattern. Roles: `combobox`, `listbox`, `option`. Works on native (Blitz): yes.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| ArrowDown | In the input | Opens the list. | yes |
| d | In the input | Typing opens the list and filters it to the matching options. | yes |
| Enter | On a highlighted option | Picks the option and closes the list; focus stays in the input. | yes |
| Escape | In the open list | Closes the list; focus stays in the input. | yes |

States:

- `open`: The list of options is shown.
- `closed`: Only the input is shown.

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
pub struct ComboboxProps<T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static = String> {
    #[props(default)]
    pub value: Option<ReadSignal<Option<T>>>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub default_value: Option<T>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub on_value_change: Callback<Option<T>>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub open: ReadSignal<Option<bool>>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub default_open: ReadSignal<bool>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub on_open_change: Callback<bool>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub query: ReadSignal<Option<String>>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub default_query: ReadSignal<String>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub on_query_change: Callback<String>,

    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(true)))]
    pub roving_loop: ReadSignal<bool>,

    #[props(default = Callback::new(|(q, t): (String, String)| default_combobox_filter(&q, &t)))]
    pub filter: Callback<(String, String), bool>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub placeholder: ReadSignal<String>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub aria_label: Option<String>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub list_aria_label: Option<String>,

    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn Combobox<T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static>(props: ComboboxProps<T>) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ComboboxEmpty(props: ComboboxEmptyProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ComboboxOption<T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static>(props: ComboboxOptionProps<T>) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::combobox::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut query = use_signal(String::new);
    let frameworks: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
        ("next", "Next.js"),
        ("svelte", "SvelteKit"),
        ("nuxt", "Nuxt.js"),
        ("remix", "Remix"),
        ("astro", "Astro"),
        ("solid", "SolidStart"),
        ("dioxus", "Dioxus"),
    ];

    rsx! {
        Combobox::<String> {
            query: Some(query()),
            on_query_change: move |next| query.set(next),
            placeholder: "Select framework...",
            aria_label: "Select framework",
            list_aria_label: "Frameworks",
            ComboboxEmpty { "No framework found." }
            for (i , (value , label)) in frameworks.iter().enumerate() {
                ComboboxOption::<String> {
                    index: i,
                    value: value.to_string(),
                    text_value: label.to_string(),
                    {*label}
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Command

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add command` or `dx components add command --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `dialog`, `hooks`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::command::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A command palette: a search box over a filtered list, inside a dialog. `filter_items` and `step_active` are pure helpers.

Pass `hotkey: "k"` to open it with Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on macOS); it uses `use_hotkey` from the `hooks` item, which `rust-ui add command` installs with it. That works on the web only, so keep a visible button too.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: a `combobox` input controlling a labelled `listbox`, with `aria-activedescendant` on the highlighted option
- Reduced motion: none

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Dialog (Modal) with a Combobox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/) pattern. Roles: `dialog`, `combobox`, `listbox`. Works on native (Blitz): not yet.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | On the button that opens it | Opens the palette with focus in the search input. | not yet |
| Control + k | Anywhere on the page, with hotkey set (web only) | Opens the palette. | not yet |
| z | In the search input | Typing filters the commands. | not yet |
| Escape | In the palette | Closes it and returns focus to the button that opened it. | not yet |

States:

- `open`: The palette is shown and the search input has focus.
- `closed`: Only the trigger is shown.

Native: The search input does not get focus when the palette opens, typing does not filter, and focus is not returned after Escape. Ctrl+K is web only.

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
/// One entry in a command palette.
pub struct CommandItem {
    pub id: String,
    pub label: String,
    /// Shown as a heading above consecutive items that share it.
    pub group: Option<String>,
    /// Display-only hint such as `Ctrl K`.
    pub shortcut: Option<String>,
}

/// Indices of the items that match `query`: every whitespace-separated word must appear in
/// the label, ignoring case. An empty query matches everything. Order is preserved.
pub fn filter_items(items: &[CommandItem], query: &str) -> Vec<usize>

/// Move the highlighted row by `delta`, wrapping at both ends. `len == 0` yields 0.
pub fn step_active(current: usize, delta: isize, len: usize) -> usize

/// Where the highlight goes after `key` in a list of `len` rows, or `None` if the key
/// doesn't move it. Arrows wrap; Home and End jump to the ends.
pub fn command_nav(key: &Key, active: usize, len: usize) -> Option<usize>

/// A searchable list of actions in a modal dialog. Type to filter, arrow keys to move,
/// Enter to choose, Escape to close. Focus stays in the input; the highlighted row is
/// exposed through `aria-activedescendant`.
#[component]
pub fn CommandDialog(
    open: bool,
    on_open_change: EventHandler<bool>,
    items: Vec<CommandItem>,
    on_select: EventHandler<String>,
    /// Defaults to "Search commands..." ([`UiStrings`](crate::components::ui_strings::UiStrings)).
    #[props(into)]
    placeholder: Option<String>,
    /// Open with Ctrl+`hotkey` (Cmd on macOS) anywhere on the page, e.g. `hotkey: "k"`.
    /// Web only ([`use_hotkey`]); keep a visible button that opens it too. Read once, on mount.
    hotkey: Option<&'static str>,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::command::*;
use crate::components::kbd::{Kbd, KbdGroup};
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut open = use_signal(|| false);
    let mut last = use_signal(|| None::<String>);
    let items = vec![
        CommandItem::new("new-file", "New file")
            .group("File")
            .shortcut("Ctrl N"),
        CommandItem::new("open-file", "Open file")
            .group("File")
            .shortcut("Ctrl O"),
        CommandItem::new("save-file", "Save file")
            .group("File")
            .shortcut("Ctrl S"),
        CommandItem::new("toggle-theme", "Toggle theme").group("View"),
        CommandItem::new("zoom-in", "Zoom in")
            .group("View")
            .shortcut("Ctrl +"),
        CommandItem::new("zoom-out", "Zoom out")
            .group("View")
            .shortcut("Ctrl -"),
    ];
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1rem; flex-wrap: wrap;",
            Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, onclick: move |_| open.set(true),
                "Open command palette"
                KbdGroup {
                    Kbd { "Ctrl" }
                    Kbd { "K" }
                }
            }
            if let Some(id) = last() {
                span { style: "font-size: 0.875rem;", "Ran: {id}" }
            }
        }
        CommandDialog {
            open: open(),
            on_open_change: move |v| open.set(v),
            items,
            on_select: move |id| last.set(Some(id)),
            // Ctrl+K (Cmd+K) anywhere on the page; the button does the same off the web.
            hotkey: "k",
        }
    }
}
```

# Context menu

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add context_menu` or `dx components add context_menu --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::context_menu::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The context menu component can be used to define a context menu that is displayed when the user right-clicks on an element. It can contain various menu items that the user can interact with.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The context menu component must wrap all context menu items.
ContextMenu {
    // The context menu trigger is the element that will display the context menu when right-clicked.
    ContextMenuTrigger {
        // The content of the trigger
        {children}
    }
    // The context menu content contains all the items that will be displayed in the context menu.
    ContextMenuContent {
        // Each context menu item represents an individual action in the context menu. Items are displayed in order based on the order of the index property.
        ContextMenuItem {
            // The index of the item, used to determine the order in which items are displayed.
            index: 0,
            // The value of the item which will be passed to the on_select callback when the item is selected.
            value: "",
            on_select: |value: String| {
                // This callback is triggered when the item is selected.
                // The value parameter contains the value of the selected item.
            },
        }
    }
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn ContextMenu(props: ContextMenuProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ContextMenuTrigger(props: ContextMenuTriggerProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ContextMenuContent(props: ContextMenuContentProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ContextMenuItem(props: ContextMenuItemProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::context_menu::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;
#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut selected_item = use_signal(|| None);

    rsx! {
        ContextMenu {
            ContextMenuTrigger { "right click here" }
            ContextMenuContent {
                ContextMenuItem {
                    value: "edit".to_string(),
                    index: 0usize,
                    on_select: move |value| {
                        selected_item.set(Some(value));
                    },
                    "Edit"
                }
                ContextMenuItem {
                    value: "undo".to_string(),
                    index: 1usize,
                    disabled: true,
                    on_select: move |value| {
                        selected_item.set(Some(value));
                    },
                    "Undo"
                }
                ContextMenuItem {
                    value: "duplicate".to_string(),
                    index: 2usize,
                    on_select: move |value| {
                        selected_item.set(Some(value));
                    },
                    "Duplicate"
                }
                ContextMenuItem {
                    value: "delete".to_string(),
                    index: 3usize,
                    on_select: move |value| {
                        selected_item.set(Some(value));
                    },
                    "Delete"
                }
            }
        }

        if let Some(item) = selected_item() {
            span { margin_left: "10px", "Selected: {item}" }
        }
    }
}
```

# DataTable

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add data_table` or `dx components add data_table --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `button`, `input`, `table`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::data_table::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A table with sorting, a filter box, pagination and optional row selection, built on `Table`.

```rust
DataTable {
    columns: vec![DataColumn::new("Name").sortable(), DataColumn::new("Salary").sortable().numeric()],
    rows: vec![vec!["Ada".into(), "$142,000".into()]],
    caption: "Team directory",
    page_size: 10,
    selectable: true,
    on_select: move |indices| { /* original row indices */ },
}
```

Cells are text. For custom content (a badge, a link, a row menu) pass `render_cell: move |(row, col)| rsx! { ... }`; `row` is the index into `rows`, and the text in `rows` is still what filtering and sorting use. For a different layout altogether, compose `Table` yourself and call `table_view(...)` for the filter, sort and page logic; it is a pure function.

Outside filters or actions (a date range, a status select, an "Export" button) go in `toolbar: rsx! { ... }`; they sit in the same row as the filter box and wrap on narrow screens.

Paging and selection are kept as row indices, so both reset when `rows` changes (an outside filter, an insert or a delete).

## Accessibility

- Role and name: a native `<table>` with a `<caption>`; sortable headers are buttons inside `<th scope="col" aria-sort>`; the filter has an `aria-label`; each row checkbox is named after the row's first cell, and the header checkbox is "Select all rows on this page".
- Keyboard: everything is a native control (Tab, Space, Enter).
- Status: "Showing 1–5 of 14 rows" and the selected count are in a `role="status"` region, so filter results are announced.
- Reduced motion: no animation.

## Source

Original to this repo (sorting headers come from our `Table`). The feature set follows Rust/UI's `data_table` / `data_grid`, which were not copied.

## Stability

Experimental. The column API and the `toolbar` slot are new and may change in any release; see `docs/STABILITY.md` in the kit repository.

## API

```rust
/// One column: its header and how it behaves.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub struct DataColumn {
    pub header: String,
    pub sortable: bool,
    /// Right-aligned, and sorted as numbers (`$1,200`, `45%` and `3.5` all parse).
    pub numeric: bool,
}

/// What the table shows for a given query, sort and page. Pure, so it is easy to test.
pub struct TableView {
    /// Original row indices on the current page, in display order.
    pub rows: Vec<usize>,
    /// Rows that match the filter, across all pages.
    pub matched: usize,
    pub pages: usize,
    /// The current page, clamped into range (zero-based).
    pub page: usize,
}

/// Filter (every whitespace-separated term must appear in some cell, ignoring case), sort
/// (stable; unparsable numbers last) and paginate (`page_size` 0 shows everything).
pub fn table_view(
    columns: &[DataColumn],
    rows: &[Vec<String>],
    query: &str,
    sort: Option<(usize, SortDirection)>,
    page: usize,
    page_size: usize,
) -> TableView

/// A table with sorting, a filter box, pagination and optional row selection. Cells are text
/// unless `render_cell` is given; `toolbar` adds controls beside the filter box. For a different
/// layout compose `Table` yourself and reuse [`table_view`].
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn DataTable(
    columns: Vec<DataColumn>,
    rows: Vec<Vec<String>>,
    /// Describes the table to assistive tech and is shown below it.
    #[props(into)]
    caption: String,
    /// Rows per page; `0` shows all rows.
    #[props(default = 10)]
    page_size: usize,
    #[props(default = true)] filterable: bool,
    #[props(default)] selectable: bool,
    /// Called with the original indices of the selected rows whenever the selection changes.
    #[props(default)]
    on_select: Callback<Vec<usize>>,
    /// Custom cell content: called with `(row, column)` (original row index) and rendered
    /// instead of the text. The text in `rows` is still what filtering and sorting use.
    #[props(default)]
    render_cell: Option<Callback<(usize, usize), Element>>,
    /// Extra controls (outside filters, actions) shown in the toolbar beside the filter box.
    #[props(default)]
    toolbar: Option<Element>,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::data_table::*;
use crate::components::toggle::Toggle;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

const PEOPLE: [(&str, &str, &str, &str); 14] = [
    ("Ada Lovelace", "Engineering", "London", "$142,000"),
    ("Grace Hopper", "Engineering", "New York", "$151,500"),
    ("Alan Turing", "Research", "Manchester", "$138,250"),
    ("Katherine Johnson", "Research", "Hampton", "$129,900"),
    ("Margaret Hamilton", "Engineering", "Boston", "$147,300"),
    ("Linus Torvalds", "Platform", "Portland", "$160,000"),
    ("Barbara Liskov", "Research", "Cambridge", "$155,750"),
    ("Dennis Ritchie", "Platform", "Murray Hill", "$133,400"),
    ("Hedy Lamarr", "Design", "Vienna", "$98,000"),
    ("Tim Berners-Lee", "Platform", "Geneva", "$149,000"),
    ("Radia Perlman", "Platform", "Redmond", "$144,800"),
    ("Donald Knuth", "Research", "Stanford", "$170,000"),
    ("Frances Allen", "Engineering", "Yorktown", "$140,100"),
    ("Edsger Dijkstra", "Research", "Eindhoven", "$137,600"),
];

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    // An outside filter, shown in the table's toolbar beside its own filter box.
    let mut research_only = use_signal(|| false);
    let rows: Vec<Vec<String>> = PEOPLE
        .iter()
        .filter(|(_, team, _, _)| !research_only() || *team == "Research")
        .map(|(a, b, c, d)| vec![a.to_string(), b.to_string(), c.to_string(), d.to_string()])
        .collect();
    let columns = vec![
        DataColumn::new("Name").sortable(),
        DataColumn::new("Team").sortable(),
        DataColumn::new("Office"),
        DataColumn::new("Salary").sortable().numeric(),
    ];
    let mut picked = use_signal(Vec::<usize>::new);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 0.75rem;",
            DataTable {
                columns,
                rows,
                caption: "Team directory",
                page_size: 5,
                selectable: true,
                on_select: move |s| picked.set(s),
                toolbar: rsx! {
                    Toggle {
                        pressed: research_only(),
                        on_pressed_change: move |on| research_only.set(on),
                        "Research only"
                    }
                },
            }
            p { style: "margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem;", "Selected rows: {picked().len()}" }
        }
    }
}
```
