# Date picker

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add date_picker` or `dx components add date_picker --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `calendar`, `form`, `icons`, `popover`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::date_picker::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The DatePicker component is used to display a date input and a Calendar popover, allowing users to enter or select a date value.

## Component Structure

```rust
DatePicker {
    // The currently selected date in the date picker (if any).
    selected_date,
    on_value_change: move |v: Option<Date>| {
        // This callback is triggered when a date is selected in the
        // calendar or the user entered it from the keyboard.
        // The date parameter contains the selected date.
    },
    // Optional number of pre-composed calendar months to show in the popover.
    month_count: 1,
    // Optional placeholder formatters for the input fields.
    on_format_day_placeholder: || "D",
    on_format_month_placeholder: || "M",
    on_format_year_placeholder: || "Y",
}
```

The styled `DatePicker` and `DateRangePicker` render the input, trigger, popover content, and calendar by default.

## Naming

Name a picker from its visible label: `DateRangePicker { aria_labelledby: "dates-label", .. }` (or `aria_label`). The picker's group then carries that name; the English "Date" / "Date Range" is only used when you pass none. The segments are named "year", "month" and "day" inside it, and a segment moves on to the next once it holds all its digits ("01" for January).

## In a form

`DateRangeField` (in the form component) binds a `DateRangePicker` to a `use_form` field, labelled, described and validated like the other fields. Its value is `2026-10-15/2026-10-20`; `format_iso_date_range` and `parse_iso_date_range` write and read that, and `format_iso_date` / `parse_iso_date` do the same for one date (`2026-10-15`, the `<input type="date">` format).

## API

```rust
pub use dioxus_primitives::calendar::DateRange;

pub use time::{Date, Month};

/// `"2026-10-15"`: the format of `<input type="date">`.
pub fn format_iso_date(date: Date) -> String

/// Reads `"2026-10-15"`; anything else (including a date that doesn't exist) is `None`.
pub fn parse_iso_date(text: &str) -> Option<Date>

/// `"2026-10-15/2026-10-20"`: an ISO 8601 interval of two dates, the format
/// [`DateRangeField`](crate::components::form::DateRangeField) keeps in a form field.
pub fn format_iso_date_range(range: DateRange) -> String

/// Reads `"2026-10-15/2026-10-20"`. The dates may come in either order; the range is always
/// start to end.
pub fn parse_iso_date_range(text: &str) -> Option<DateRange>

pub struct DatePickerProps {
    /// Callback when value changes
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_value_change: Callback<Option<Date>>,

    /// The selected date
    #[props(default)]
    pub selected_date: ReadSignal<Option<Date>>,

    /// Whether the date picker is disabled
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// Whether the date picker is enable user input
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(false)))]
    pub read_only: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// Lower limit of the range of available dates
    #[props(default = fixed_date(1925, Month::January, 1))]
    pub min_date: Date,

    /// Upper limit of the range of available dates
    #[props(default = fixed_date(2050, Month::December, 31))]
    pub max_date: Date,

    /// Callback when display day placeholder
    #[props(default = Callback::new(|_| "D".to_string()))]
    pub on_format_day_placeholder: Callback<(), String>,

    /// Callback when display month placeholder
    #[props(default = Callback::new(|_| "M".to_string()))]
    pub on_format_month_placeholder: Callback<(), String>,

    /// Callback when display year placeholder
    #[props(default = Callback::new(|_| "Y".to_string()))]
    pub on_format_year_placeholder: Callback<(), String>,

    /// Specify how many months are visible at once
    #[props(default = 1)]
    pub month_count: u8,

    /// Unavailable dates
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled_ranges: ReadSignal<Vec<DateRange>>,

    /// Whether focus should loop around when reaching the end.
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(false)))]
    pub roving_loop: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the date picker element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
}

pub struct DateRangePickerProps {
    /// Callback when value changes
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_range_change: Callback<Option<DateRange>>,

    /// The selected date
    #[props(default)]
    pub selected_range: ReadSignal<Option<DateRange>>,

    /// Whether the date picker is disabled
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// Whether the date picker is enable user input
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(false)))]
    pub read_only: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// Lower limit of the range of available dates
    #[props(default = fixed_date(1925, Month::January, 1))]
    pub min_date: Date,

    /// Upper limit of the range of available dates
    #[props(default = fixed_date(2050, Month::December, 31))]
    pub max_date: Date,

    /// Callback when display day placeholder
    #[props(default = Callback::new(|_| "D".to_string()))]
    pub on_format_day_placeholder: Callback<(), String>,

    /// Callback when display month placeholder
    #[props(default = Callback::new(|_| "M".to_string()))]
    pub on_format_month_placeholder: Callback<(), String>,

    /// Callback when display year placeholder
    #[props(default = Callback::new(|_| "Y".to_string()))]
    pub on_format_year_placeholder: Callback<(), String>,

    /// Specify how many months are visible at once
    #[props(default = 1)]
    pub month_count: u8,

    /// Unavailable dates
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled_ranges: ReadSignal<Vec<DateRange>>,

    /// Whether focus should loop around when reaching the end.
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(false)))]
    pub roving_loop: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// Additional attributes to extend the date picker element
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
}

#[component]
pub fn DatePicker(props: DatePickerProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn DateRangePicker(props: DateRangePickerProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::Button;
use crate::components::date_picker::*;
use crate::components::form::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

use time::Date;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut selected_date = use_signal(|| None::<Date>);
    let mut selected_range = use_signal(|| None::<DateRange>);
    let form = use_form();
    let stay = form.field(vec![
        custom(|v| {
            if v.is_empty() {
                Err("Choose your dates.".to_string())
            } else {
                Ok(())
            }
        }),
        days_between(Some(2), Some(14), "Stays are 2 to 14 nights."),
    ]);
    let mut booked = use_signal(|| None::<String>);

    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 1rem; justify-items: start;",
            DatePicker {
                selected_date: selected_date(),
                on_value_change: move |v| {
                    tracing::info!("Selected date changed: {:?}", v);
                    selected_date.set(v);
                },
            }
            DateRangePicker {
                selected_range: selected_range(),
                on_range_change: move |r| selected_range.set(r),
            }
            Form {
                state: form,
                on_valid: move |_| booked.set(Some(stay.value())),
                DateRangeField {
                    field: stay,
                    label: "Stay",
                    description: "Check-in and check-out, 2 to 14 nights.",
                }
                Button { r#type: "submit", "Check availability" }
            }
            if let Some(range) = booked() {
                p { role: "status", style: "margin: 0;", "Looking for {range}" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# DateTimePicker

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add date_time_picker` or `dx components add date_time_picker --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `date_picker`, `form`, `time_picker`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::date_time_picker::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A `DatePicker` and a `TimePicker` that edit one value, for bookings, reminders and anything scheduled.

```rust
let mut when = use_signal(|| None::<PrimitiveDateTime>);
rsx! {
    DateTimePicker {
        label: "Departure",
        value: when(),
        on_value_change: move |v| when.set(v),
        default_time: Time::from_hms(9, 0, 0).ok(), // filled in when a date is picked first
        hour_cycle: HourCycle::H12,
        min_date: today,
    }
}
```

`value` is `Option<PrimitiveDateTime>` (`time`, re-exported): `Some` once both a date and a time are entered. The date half takes `min_date`, `max_date` and `disabled_ranges` like `DatePicker`; the time half takes `hour_cycle`, `seconds` and `minute_step` like `TimePicker`. `name` submits it with a native `<form>` as `2026-10-15T14:05`; `format_iso_date_time` and `parse_iso_date_time` write and read that format (`<input type="datetime-local">`'s).

In a `use_form` form, use `DateTimeField { field, label: "Departure" }`: the field holds `2026-10-15T14:05`, empty until both halves are filled.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: a `role="group"` named by `label` (default "Date and time") or by a visible label through `labelled_by`, with the description and error in `aria-describedby`. Inside are the date picker's group and the time picker's group; see their docs.
- Keyboard: as `DatePicker` and `TimePicker`; Tab moves from the date segments to the calendar button to the time segments.
- `DateTimeField` validates when focus leaves the whole picker, calendar included, and a failed submit focuses the hours (the date segments come from dioxus-primitives and cannot be focused from outside).
- Reduced motion: the calendar popover's fade follows `DatePicker`.

## Source

Original to this repo; composes the kit's `DatePicker` and `TimePicker`.

## Stability

Experimental. New on 2026-10-15; see `docs/STABILITY.md` in the kit repository.

## API

```rust
pub use time::PrimitiveDateTime;

/// `"2026-10-15T14:05"` (with `:09` seconds when asked): the format of
/// `<input type="datetime-local">`, used by
/// [`DateTimeField`](crate::components::form::DateTimeField) to keep a value in a form field.
pub fn format_iso_date_time(value: PrimitiveDateTime, seconds: bool) -> String

/// Reads `"2026-10-15T14:05"` or `"2026-10-15T14:05:09"` (a space works in place of `T`).
pub fn parse_iso_date_time(text: &str) -> Option<PrimitiveDateTime>

/// A [`DatePicker`] and a [`TimePicker`] that edit one value. The value is `Some` once both a
/// date and a time are entered.
///
/// ```rust,ignore
/// let mut when = use_signal(|| None::<PrimitiveDateTime>);
/// DateTimePicker { value: when(), on_value_change: move |v| when.set(v), hour_cycle: HourCycle::H12 }
/// ```
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn DateTimePicker(
    #[props(default)] value: ReadSignal<Option<PrimitiveDateTime>>,
    #[props(default)] on_value_change: Callback<Option<PrimitiveDateTime>>,
    #[props(default)] hour_cycle: HourCycle,
    #[props(default)] seconds: bool,
    #[props(default = 1)] minute_step: u8,
    /// Filled in when a date is picked while the time is still empty, for example 09:00.
    #[props(default)]
    default_time: Option<Time>,
    #[props(default = Date::from_calendar_date(1925, Month::January, 1).expect("valid date"))]
    min_date: Date,
    #[props(default = Date::from_calendar_date(2050, Month::December, 31).expect("valid date"))]
    max_date: Date,
    /// Dates that can't be picked.
    #[props(default)]
    disabled_ranges: ReadSignal<Vec<DateRange>>,
    #[props(default)] disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,
    #[props(default)] read_only: ReadSignal<bool>,
    /// Accessible name of the group when no visible label is linked with `labelled_by`.
    /// Defaults to "Date and time" from `UiStrings`.
    #[props(into, default)]
    label: Option<String>,
    /// Id of a visible label for the whole picker.
    #[props(into, default)]
    labelled_by: Option<String>,
    /// Id for the time's first segment, so a `<label for>` can point at it.
    #[props(into, default)]
    time_segment_id: Option<String>,
    #[props(default)] invalid: bool,
    /// Ids of a description and error message for the group.
    #[props(into, default)]
    described_by: Option<String>,
    /// Submit the value with a native `<form>` under this name, as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`.
    #[props(into, default)]
    name: Option<String>,
    /// Called when focus leaves the picker, its calendar included.
    #[props(default)]
    on_blur: Callback<()>,
    /// The time's first segment, once mounted.
    #[props(default)]
    on_mounted: Callback<MountedEvent>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::Button;
use crate::components::date_time_picker::*;
use crate::components::form::*;
use crate::components::time_picker::{HourCycle, Time};
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let form = use_form();
    let departure = form.field(vec![custom(|v| {
        if v.is_empty() {
            Err("Pick a date and a time.".to_string())
        } else {
            Ok(())
        }
    })]);
    let mut saved = use_signal(|| None::<String>);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 1rem; justify-items: start;",
            Form {
                state: form,
                on_valid: move |_| saved.set(Some(departure.value())),
                DateTimeField {
                    field: departure,
                    label: "Departure",
                    description: "Picking a date fills in 09:00.",
                    default_time: Time::from_hms(9, 0, 0).ok(),
                    minute_step: 5,
                }
                Button { r#type: "submit", "Book" }
            }
            if let Some(value) = saved() {
                p { role: "status", style: "margin: 0;", "Departure: {value}" }
            }
            DateTimePicker { label: "Return", hour_cycle: HourCycle::H12 }
        }
    }
}
```

# Dialog

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add dialog` or `dx components add dialog --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::dialog::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The dialog component can be used to display additional information or actions related to an item. It is a simple modal dialog that can be opened and closed by the user.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The dialog component must wrap all dialog elements.
Dialog {
    // The open prop determines if the dialog is currently open or closed.
    open: open(),
    // Required: the heading and the dialog's accessible name. Leaving it out is a compile error.
    title: "Item information",
    // Optional: one line read after the title.
    description: "Here is some additional information about the item.",
    // The content follows the title and description.
    p { "..." }
}
```

## Accessibility

- `title` is a required prop, so a dialog without a name doesn't compile (the error names the missing field: "Missing required field title"). Radix and shadcn only warn about this at runtime.
- `hide_title: true` hides the title and `description` visually but keeps them for screen readers, for dialogs whose content already makes the purpose clear (the command palette uses it).
- For a description with links or formatting, put a `DialogDescription` in the children instead of `description` (not both).

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Dialog (Modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/) pattern. Roles: `dialog`. Works on native (Blitz): partly.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | On the button that opens it | Opens the dialog and moves focus into it. | yes |
| Space | On the button that opens it | Opens the dialog and moves focus into it. | yes |
| Tab | Inside the dialog | Moves to the next control; from the last one it wraps to the first, so focus stays in the dialog. | yes |
| Shift + Tab | Inside the dialog | Moves to the previous control, wrapping from the first to the last. | yes |
| Escape | Inside the dialog | Closes the dialog and returns focus to the button that opened it. | not yet |

States:

- `open`: The dialog is shown over the page.
- `closed`: Only the trigger is shown.

Native: Closing works, but focus is left on the removed content instead of going back to the trigger.

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
/// The props for [`Dialog`].
///
/// `title` is required: a dialog without a name is announced as just "dialog". Hide it with
/// `hide_title` when the content already makes the purpose clear to sighted users.
///
/// ```
/// # use dioxus::prelude::*;
/// # use ui::prelude::*;
/// # fn app() -> Element {
/// rsx! { Dialog { open: true, title: "Rename file", p { "…" } } }
/// # }
/// ```
///
/// Leaving `title` out is a compile error ("Missing required field title"):
///
/// ```compile_fail,E0061
/// # use dioxus::prelude::*;
/// # use ui::prelude::*;
/// # fn app() -> Element {
/// rsx! { Dialog { open: true, p { "…" } } }
/// # }
/// ```
pub struct DialogProps {
    /// The dialog's heading, and its accessible name (`aria-labelledby`).
    #[props(into)]
    pub title: String,

    /// One line read after the title (`aria-describedby`). For richer text, put a
    /// [`DialogDescription`] in the children instead (not both).
    #[props(default, into)]
    pub description: Option<String>,

    /// Hide the title and `description` visually; screen readers still read them.
    #[props(default)]
    pub hide_title: bool,

    /// The ID of the dialog root element.
    pub id: ReadSignal<Option<String>>,

    /// Whether the dialog is modal. If true, it will trap focus within the dialog when open.
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(true)))]
    pub is_modal: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// The controlled `open` state of the dialog.
    pub open: ReadSignal<Option<bool>>,

    /// The default `open` state of the dialog if it is not controlled.
    #[props(default)]
    pub default_open: bool,

    /// Called when the open state changes.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_open_change: Callback<bool>,

    /// Attributes for the dialog panel.
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The dialog's content, shown below the title.
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn Dialog(props: DialogProps) -> Element

/// A longer description for a [`Dialog`] (links, formatting). For one line of text, use the
/// dialog's `description` prop instead.
#[component]
pub fn DialogDescription(props: DialogDescriptionProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::dialog::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut open = use_signal(|| false);
    rsx! {
        Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, onclick: move |_| open.set(true), "Open dialog" }
        Dialog {
            open: open(),
            on_open_change: move |v| open.set(v),
            title: "Are you sure?",
            description: "This action cannot be undone.",
            div { style: "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem; justify-content: flex-end; margin-top: 1rem;",
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, onclick: move |_| open.set(false), "Cancel" }
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Destructive, onclick: move |_| open.set(false), "Delete" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Drag and drop list

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add drag_and_drop_list` or `dx components add drag_and_drop_list --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::drag_and_drop_list::*;` after copying, or `use ui::components::drag_and_drop_list::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

Allows users to create vertically sortable lists supporting drag and drop, touch or keyboard input.

## Component Structure

```rust
DragAndDropList {
    // Items to be rendered
    items
    // Whether the list items should be removable
    is_removable
}
```

## API

```rust
pub struct DragAndDropListProps {
    /// Items (labels) to be rendered.
    pub items: Vec<Element>,

    /// Set if the list items should be removable
    #[props(default)]
    pub is_removable: bool,

    /// Accessible label for the list
    #[props(default)]
    pub aria_label: Option<String>,

    /// Additional attributes to apply to the list element.
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The children of the list component.
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn DragAndDropList(props: DragAndDropListProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn DragAndDropListItem(props: DragAndDropListItemProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn DragAndDropListItems(props: DragAndDropListItemsProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn DragAndDropDropIndicator(props: DragAndDropDropIndicatorProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn RemoveButton(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::avatar::{AvatarImageSize, ImageAvatar};
use crate::components::drag_and_drop_list::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

const INLINE_STYLE: &str = r#".dx-tasks-demo {
  width: 100%;
  max-width: 460px;
  margin: 0 auto;
}

.dx-tasks-header {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  justify-content: space-between;
  padding: 0 2px 14px;
  gap: 16px;
}

.dx-tasks-title {
  margin: 0;

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct TaskView {
    code: &'static str,
    title: &'static str,
    status: &'static str,
    assignee: &'static str,
    avatar: &'static str,
    due: &'static str,
    urgent: bool,
}

// Placeholder avatars (inline SVG, no network).
const AVATARS: &[&str] = &[
    crate::demos::avatar::DEMO_AVATAR_SRC,
    crate::demos::avatar::DEMO_AVATAR_SRC,
    crate::demos::avatar::DEMO_AVATAR_SRC,
];

const TASKS: &[TaskView] = &[
    TaskView {

    },
    TaskView {

    },

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let items: Vec<Element> = TASKS.iter().map(|t| task_item(*t)).collect();

    rsx! {
        style { {INLINE_STYLE} }
        div { class: "dx-tasks-demo",
            div { class: "dx-tasks-header",
                div {
                    h3 { class: "dx-tasks-title", "Launch priorities" }
                    p { class: "dx-tasks-subtitle",
                        "Drag to reorder - top is highest priority"
                    }
                }
                span { class: "dx-tasks-count", "6 active" }
            }
            div {
                DragAndDropList { items }
            }
        }
    }
}

fn task_item(t: TaskView) -> Element {
    let urgent_attr = if t.urgent { "true" } else { "false" };
    let avatar_label = format!("Assigned to {}", t.assignee);

    rsx! {
        div { key: "{t.code}", class: "dx-task-card",
            div { class: "dx-task-body",
                div { class: "dx-task-title", "{t.title}" }
                div { class: "dx-task-meta",
                    span { class: "dx-task-code", "{t.code}" }
                    span { class: "dx-task-sep", "aria-hidden": "true" }
                    span { "{t.status}" }
                    span { class: "dx-task-sep", "aria-hidden": "true" }
                    span {
                        class: "dx-task-due",
                        "data-urgent": "{urgent_attr}",
                        "{t.due}"
                    }
                }
            }
            ImageAvatar {
                size: AvatarImageSize::Small,
                aria_label: "{avatar_label}",
                style: "user-select: none;",
                src: "{t.avatar}",
                alt: "{avatar_label}",
                "{t.assignee}"
            }
        }
    }
}

# Drawer

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add drawer` or `dx components add drawer --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::drawer::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A panel that slides up from the bottom and can be dragged down to dismiss.

```rust
Drawer {
    open: open(),
    on_open_change: move |v| open.set(v),
    title: "Move goal", // required
    description: "Set your daily goal.",
    DrawerClose { "Close" }
}
```

It is built on the dialog primitive plus the motion layer's vertical `SwipeDismiss` (`vertical` and `one_way`): pull down far enough, or flick, and it springs away; release early and it springs back.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: a modal `dialog` named by its `title` (a required prop: leaving it out is a compile error; `hide_title` hides it visually) and described by `description` or a `DrawerDescription` child; the handle is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Keyboard: focus is trapped inside; Escape closes; the Close button always works, so dragging is never required.
- Reduced motion: the slide-in is removed and the drag release becomes a near-instant tween.

## Source

Original to this repo, on `dioxus-primitives` dialog and `crates/motion`. Rust/UI's `drawer.rs` was only used to see the feature set.

## API

```rust
/// The props for [`Drawer`].
///
/// `title` is required: a drawer is a modal dialog, and one without a name is announced as just
/// "dialog". Hide it with `hide_title` when the content makes the purpose clear to sighted users.
///
/// ```
/// # use dioxus::prelude::*;
/// # use ui::prelude::*;
/// # fn app() -> Element {
/// rsx! { Drawer { open: true, title: "Rename file", p { "…" } } }
/// # }
/// ```
///
/// Leaving `title` out is a compile error ("Missing required field title"):
///
/// ```compile_fail,E0061
/// # use dioxus::prelude::*;
/// # use ui::prelude::*;
/// # fn app() -> Element {
/// rsx! { Drawer { open: true, p { "…" } } }
/// # }
/// ```
pub struct DrawerProps {
    /// The drawer's heading, and its accessible name (`aria-labelledby`).
    #[props(into)]
    pub title: String,

    /// One line read after the title (`aria-describedby`), shown under it. For richer text, put
    /// a [`DrawerDescription`] in the children instead (not both).
    #[props(default, into)]
    pub description: Option<String>,

    /// Hide the title and `description` visually; screen readers still read them.
    #[props(default)]
    pub hide_title: bool,

    /// The ID of the dialog root element.
    pub id: ReadSignal<Option<String>>,

    /// Whether the drawer is modal. If true, it will trap focus within the drawer when open.
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(true)))]
    pub is_modal: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// The controlled `open` state of the drawer.
    pub open: ReadSignal<Option<bool>>,

    /// The default `open` state of the drawer if it is not controlled.
    #[props(default)]
    pub default_open: bool,

    /// Called when the open state changes, including after a drag dismisses it.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_open_change: Callback<bool>,

    /// Attributes for the drawer panel.
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The drawer's content, shown below the title.
    pub children: Element,
}

/// A panel that slides up from the bottom of the screen and can be dragged down to dismiss.
///
/// It is a modal dialog underneath (focus is trapped, Escape closes, the page behind is inert),
/// named by its required `title`. Dragging is an extra: the Close button and Escape always work.
#[component]
pub fn Drawer(props: DrawerProps) -> Element

/// A longer description for a [`Drawer`] (links, formatting). For one line of text, use the
/// drawer's `description` prop instead.
#[component]
pub fn DrawerDescription(props: DialogDescriptionProps) -> Element

/// A button that closes the drawer.
#[component]
pub fn DrawerClose(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::Button;
use crate::components::drawer::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut open = use_signal(|| false);
    rsx! {
        Button { onclick: move |_| open.set(true), "Open drawer" }
        Drawer {
            open: open(),
            on_open_change: move |v| open.set(v),
            title: "Move goal",
            description: "Set your daily activity goal. Drag the handle down, or press Escape, to close.",
            p { style: "margin: 0.5rem 0;", "Pick a number that feels realistic for this week." }
            DrawerClose { "Close" }
        }
    }
}
```

# Dropdown menu

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add dropdown_menu` or `dx components add dropdown_menu --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::dropdown_menu::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The DropdownMenu component is used to create a dropdown menu that can be triggered by a button click. It allows users to select an option from a list of items.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The dropdown menu component must wrap all dropdown items.
DropdownMenu {
    // The dropdown menu trigger is the button that will display the dropdown menu when clicked.
    DropdownMenuTrigger {
        // The content of the trigger to display inside the button.
        {children}
    }
    // The dropdown menu content contains all the items that will be displayed in the dropdown menu.
    DropdownMenuContent {
        // Each dropdown menu item represents an individual option in the dropdown menu. Items are displayed in order based on the order of the index property.
        DropdownMenuItem {
            // The index of the item, used to determine the order in which items are displayed.
            index: 0,
            // The value of the item which will be passed to the on_select callback when the item is selected.
            value: "",
            on_select: |value: String| {
                // This callback is triggered when the item is selected.
                // The value parameter contains the value of the selected item.
            },
        }
    }
}
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Menu Button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/) pattern. Roles: `listbox`, `option`. Works on native (Blitz): partly.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | On the trigger | Opens the menu; focus stays on the trigger until an arrow key moves it in (the APG moves it to the first item at once). | yes |
| Space | On the trigger | Opens the menu, as Enter does. | yes |
| ArrowDown | In the open menu | Moves focus to the first item, then to the next one. | yes |
| ArrowUp | In the open menu | Moves focus to the previous item, wrapping from the first to the last. | yes |
| Enter | On an item | Chooses the item, closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. | not yet |
| Escape | In the open menu | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. | yes |

States:

- `open`: The list of actions is shown.
- `closed`: Only the trigger is shown.

Known gaps:

- The items are a `listbox` of `option`s, not a `menu` of `menuitem`s (upstream markup).
- Opening does not move focus to the first item; the first arrow key does.

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn DropdownMenu(props: DropdownMenuProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn DropdownMenuTrigger(props: DropdownMenuTriggerProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn DropdownMenuContent(props: DropdownMenuContentProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn DropdownMenuItem<T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static>(
    props: DropdownMenuItemProps<T>,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::dropdown_menu::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut picked = use_signal(|| None::<&'static str>);
    let actions = ["Edit", "Duplicate", "Archive", "Delete"];
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem;",
            DropdownMenu { default_open: false,
                DropdownMenuTrigger { "Actions" }
                DropdownMenuContent {
                    for (i, a) in actions.into_iter().enumerate() {
                        DropdownMenuItem::<&'static str> {
                            value: a,
                            index: i,
                            on_select: move |v| picked.set(Some(v)),
                            {a}
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            if let Some(a) = picked() {
                span { style: "font-size: 0.875rem;", "Selected: {a}" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Dropzone

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add dropzone` or `dx components add dropzone --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::dropzone::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A file picker you can also drop files onto.

```rust
Dropzone { accept: "image/*,.pdf", multiple: true, max_size: 5 * 1024 * 1024,
           on_files: move |files| upload(files) }
```

The control is a native `<input type="file">` inside the label, so it behaves like any file input. Dropped files are checked against `accept` (`.ext`, `type/*`, `type/subtype`) and `max_size`; rejected files produce a message and are not passed on. `accepts()` and `format_size()` are public helpers.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: the label text is the input's name; the selected files are a labelled list; rejection messages are `role="alert"`.
- Keyboard: Tab to the (visually hidden) input, Space or Enter opens the file picker. Drag and drop is an extra, never the only way.
- Reduced motion: no animation.

## Source

Original to this repo. Rust/UI's `dropzone.rs` (498 lines, wasm-bindgen based) was used only to see the feature set.

## API

```rust
/// Does a file match an `accept` list such as `.png,image/*,application/pdf`? An empty list
/// accepts everything. Matching ignores case.
pub fn accepts(accept: &str, name: &str, content_type: &str) -> bool

/// "1.5 MB" style size.
pub fn format_size(bytes: u64) -> String

/// A file picker you can also drop files onto. The real control is a native
/// `<input type="file">` inside the label, so keyboard and screen readers work as they do for
/// any file input; dropped files are checked against `accept` and `max_size` too.
#[component]
pub fn Dropzone(
    /// Visible instructions, for example "Drop files here or browse".
    /// Defaults to "Drop files here or click to browse" ([`UiStrings`](crate::components::ui_strings::UiStrings)).
    #[props(into)]
    prompt: Option<String>,
    /// Comma-separated: `.png`, `image/*`, `application/pdf`. Empty accepts anything.
    #[props(into, default)]
    accept: String,
    #[props(default)] multiple: bool,
    /// Largest file in bytes (0 for no limit).
    #[props(default)]
    max_size: u64,
    #[props(default)] disabled: bool,
    /// Called with the accepted files after every drop or pick.
    #[props(default)]
    on_files: Callback<Vec<FileData>>,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::dropzone::*;
use dioxus::html::FileData;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut count = use_signal(|| 0_usize);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 0.75rem; max-width: 28rem;",
            Dropzone {
                accept: "image/*,.pdf",
                multiple: true,
                max_size: 5 * 1024 * 1024,
                on_files: move |files: Vec<FileData>| count.set(count() + files.len()),
            }
            p { style: "margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem;", role: "status", "Files received: {count()}" }
        }
    }
}
```

# Empty

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add empty` or `dx components add empty --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::empty::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

Placeholder for a list, table or page with nothing in it, with optional icon, text and actions. Compose `Empty`, `EmptyHeader`, `EmptyMedia`, `EmptyTitle`, `EmptyDescription`, `EmptyContent`.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: `EmptyTitle` is `role="heading"` with a configurable `level`; the media is `aria-hidden`.
- Keyboard: actions are normal buttons
- Reduced motion: none

## Source

Structure and API adapted from Rust/UI (`empty.rs`, rust-ui/ui commit 43ddc65, MIT); styling rewritten in plain CSS with this kit's tokens. Behaviour and accessibility were reworked here.

## API

```rust
/// A placeholder for a list, table or page with nothing in it yet.
/// Compose with `EmptyHeader`, `EmptyMedia`, `EmptyTitle`, `EmptyDescription` and `EmptyContent`.
#[component]
pub fn Empty(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn EmptyHeader(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// Decorative media (an icon or illustration). Hidden from assistive tech.
#[component]
pub fn EmptyMedia(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// The heading. `level` is the heading level (default 3); pick the one that fits the page outline.
#[component]
pub fn EmptyTitle(
    #[props(default = 3)] level: u8,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn EmptyDescription(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// Actions, usually one or two buttons.
#[component]
pub fn EmptyContent(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::empty::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "max-width: 32rem;",
            Empty {
                EmptyHeader {
                    EmptyMedia {
                        svg {
                            view_box: "0 0 24 24",
                            fill: "none",
                            stroke: "currentColor",
                            stroke_width: "2",
                            path { d: "M3 7a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h4l2 2h8a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v8a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H5a2 2 0 0 1-2-2z" }
                        }
                    }
                    EmptyTitle { "No projects yet" }
                    EmptyDescription { "Create your first project to see it here." }
                }
                EmptyContent {
                    Button { "Create project" }
                    Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, "Import" }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Field

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add field` or `dx components add field --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::field::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

Wires a label, description and error to a control with matching ids. `use_field_ids()` returns the ids; for most forms use `TextField` from `form`.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: the control gets `aria-describedby` pointing at the description and error; `FieldError` renders `role="alert"` only when there is a message
- Keyboard: none of its own
- Reduced motion: none

## API

```rust
/// DOM ids that tie a control to its description and error message, so assistive
/// technology reads them together. Create with [`use_field_ids`].
pub struct FieldIds {
    pub control: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub error: String,
}

/// Stable, unique ids for one field.
pub fn use_field_ids() -> FieldIds

/// Groups a label, a control, a description and an error message.
///
/// ```ignore
/// let ids = use_field_ids();
/// Field { invalid: error().is_some(),
///     FieldLabel { html_for: ids.control.clone(), "Email" }
///     Input { id: ids.control.clone(), aria_invalid: error().is_some(),
///             aria_describedby: ids.described_by(error().is_some()) }
///     FieldDescription { id: ids.description.clone(), "We never share it." }
///     FieldError { id: ids.error.clone(), message: error() }
/// }
/// ```
#[component]
pub fn Field(
    #[props(default)] invalid: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn FieldLabel(
    #[props(into)] html_for: String,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn FieldDescription(
    #[props(into)] id: String,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// Renders nothing until there is a message, then announces it (`role="alert"`).
#[component]
pub fn FieldError(#[props(into)] id: String, #[props(default)] message: Option<String>) -> Element {
    match message
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::Button;
use crate::components::field::*;
use crate::components::input::Input;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let email_ids = use_field_ids();
    let password_ids = use_field_ids();
    let mut email = use_signal(String::new);
    let mut password = use_signal(String::new);
    let mut email_error = use_signal(|| None::<String>);
    let mut password_error = use_signal(|| None::<String>);
    let mut done = use_signal(|| false);

    let submit = move |event: FormEvent| {
        event.prevent_default();
        email_error.set(
            validate::required(&email.read())
                .and_then(|_| validate::email(&email.read()))
                .err(),
        );
        password_error.set(validate::min_len(&password.read(), 8).err());
        done.set(email_error.read().is_none() && password_error.read().is_none());
    };

    rsx! {
        form { style: "display: grid; gap: 1rem; max-width: 20rem;", onsubmit: submit, novalidate: true,
            Field { invalid: email_error().is_some(),
                FieldLabel { html_for: email_ids.control.clone(), "Email" }
                Input {
                    id: email_ids.control.clone(),
                    r#type: "email",
                    placeholder: "you@example.com",
                    value: email,
                    aria_invalid: email_error().is_some().then_some("true"),
                    aria_describedby: email_ids.described_by(email_error().is_some()),
                    oninput: move |e: FormEvent| email.set(e.value()),
                }
                FieldDescription { id: email_ids.description.clone(), "We never share it." }
                FieldError { id: email_ids.error.clone(), message: email_error() }
            }
            Field { invalid: password_error().is_some(),
                FieldLabel { html_for: password_ids.control.clone(), "Password" }
                Input {
                    id: password_ids.control.clone(),
                    r#type: "password",
                    value: password,
                    aria_invalid: password_error().is_some().then_some("true"),
                    aria_describedby: password_ids.described_by(password_error().is_some()),
                    oninput: move |e: FormEvent| password.set(e.value()),
                }
                FieldDescription { id: password_ids.description.clone(), "At least 8 characters." }
                FieldError { id: password_ids.error.clone(), message: password_error() }
            }
            Button { r#type: "submit", "Create account" }
            if done() {
                p { role: "status", style: "margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem;", "Looks good. Account created." }
            }
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use crate::components::field::validate::*;

    #[test]
    fn required_rejects_blank() {
        assert!(required("").is_err());
        assert!(required("   ").is_err());
        assert!(required("x").is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn min_len_counts_characters_not_bytes() {
        assert!(min_len("ééééééé", 8).is_err());
        assert!(min_len("éééééééé", 8).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn email_accepts_and_rejects() {
        for ok in ["a@b.co", "first.last@example.com"] {
            assert!(email(ok).is_ok(), "{ok}");
        }
        for bad in [
            "", "a", "a@", "@b.co", "a@b", "a@b.", "a b@c.de", "a@@b.co", "a@b@c.de",
        ] {
            assert!(email(bad).is_err(), "{bad}");
        }
    }
}
```

---

# Form

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add form` or `dx components add form --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `checkbox`, `combobox`, `date_picker`, `date_time_picker`, `field`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `time_picker`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::form::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

Validation state for a form, with the accessibility wiring done for you. `use_form()` creates the state, `form.field(vec![required(), email()])` declares each field (call it like a hook), and `Form` / `TextField` render a native `<form novalidate>` and fully labelled inputs.

```rust
let form = use_form();
let email = form.field(vec![required(), email()]);
rsx! {
    Form { state: form, on_valid: move |_| save(email.value()),
        TextField { field: email, label: "Email", r#type: "email" }
        Button { r#type: "submit", "Save" }
    }
}
```

Start a field with a value with `form.field_with("Acme", rules)`; `reset()` returns to it. To load a record into the form (an edit sheet), call `field.load(value)`: it sets the value, makes it the one `reset()` returns to, and clears the error. Both `set` and `load` are safe to call from an effect.

`SelectField` and `ComboboxField` bind a `Select` or a searchable `Combobox` to a field the same way, so they can be required, show their error and get focus on a failed submit:

```rust
let plan = form.field(vec![required()]);
let zone = form.field_with("UTC", vec![required()]);
rsx! {
    SelectField { field: plan, label: "Plan", placeholder: "Choose a plan",
        options: vec![FieldOption::new("free", "Free"), FieldOption::new("pro", "Pro")] }
    ComboboxField { field: zone, label: "Time zone", options: vec!["UTC".into(), "Asia/Tokyo".into()] }
}
```

The field holds the option's `value` (empty while nothing is chosen). They validate when the list closes, as a text field does on blur.

`TextareaField` is the multi-line `TextField`. `CheckboxField` puts a checkbox and its label on one line; the field holds `"true"` while it is ticked, so a rule makes it mandatory ("accept the terms") and it is focused on a failed submit like the rest:

```rust
let notes = form.field(vec![max_len(300)]);
let terms = form.field(vec![custom(|v| if v == "true" { Ok(()) } else { Err("Accept the terms.".into()) })]);
rsx! {
    TextareaField { field: notes, label: "Notes", maxlength: "300" }
    CheckboxField { field: terms, label: "I accept the terms" }
}
```

`TimeField` and `DateTimeField` bind a `TimePicker` or `DateTimePicker`. The field holds `14:05` or `2026-10-15T14:05` (the formats of `<input type="time">` and `datetime-local`), empty until every part is entered; they validate when focus leaves the picker:

```rust
let start = form.field(vec![required()]);
let departure = form.field(vec![required()]);
rsx! {
    TimeField { field: start, label: "Start", hour_cycle: HourCycle::H12, minute_step: 5 }
    DateTimeField { field: departure, label: "Departure", default_time: Time::from_hms(9, 0, 0).ok() }
}
```

`TimeField` also takes `min` and `max`; it then adds a range rule itself ("Choose a time from 9:00 to 17:00."). `DateRangeField` binds a `DateRangePicker`: the field holds `2026-10-15/2026-10-20` (an ISO 8601 interval, read back with `parse_iso_date_range`), empty until both dates are picked, and `days_between(min, max, message)` limits the length of the stay:

```rust
let stay = form.field(vec![required(), days_between(Some(2), Some(14), "Stays are 2 to 14 nights.")]);
rsx! {
    DateRangeField { field: stay, label: "Stay", min_date: today, disabled_ranges: booked() }
}
```

A failed submit focuses the range picker's group, which is read with its label and error.

`TextField` and `TextareaField` pass any other attribute to their control (`inputmode: "numeric"`, `maxlength`, `pattern`, `rows`); the field's own `id`, `value` and ARIA wiring win over them.

Rules: `required()`, `email()`, `min_len(n)`, `max_len(n)`, `time_between(min, max, message)`, `days_between(min, max, message)`, or `custom(|v| ...)` returning `Err(message)`. The first failing rule shows. A field validates when it loses focus, then on every change until it is valid.

## Derive a form from a struct

`#[derive(Form)]` (in `ui::prelude`) turns a struct into the same fields, so the rules and messages live next to the types:

```rust
#[derive(Form, Clone, PartialEq)]
struct SignUp {
    #[form(required, min_len = 3, autocomplete = "username")]
    user_name: String,
    #[form(required, email, description = "We never share it.")]
    email: String,
    #[form(min = 18)]
    age: u32,
    #[form(select = plans, placeholder = "Choose a plan")]
    plan: Option<String>,
    #[form(required = "Accept the terms to continue.", label = "I accept the terms")]
    terms: bool,
}

let form = SignUp::use_form(); // or SignUp::use_form_with(&saved)
rsx! {
    Form { state: form, on_valid: move |_| if let Some(v) = form.value() { save(v) },
        {form.fields()}
        Button { r#type: "submit", "Sign up" }
    }
}
```

It generates `SignUpForm`, with one public `FormField` per struct field (`form.email`), plus `fields()` (every field, rendered in order), `value()` (the typed struct, `None` while a field does not parse), `load(&value)`, `reset()`, `validate()` and `state()`. Render a field yourself to lay it out differently: `TextField { field: form.email, label: "Email" }`.

The type picks the control and the base rules:

- `String`: a `TextField`. `Option<String>`: the same, optional (empty is `None`).
- `bool`: a `CheckboxField`; `required` means it must be ticked.
- Numbers and any other `FromStr + Display` type: a `TextField` (`inputmode` numeric or decimal for numbers) that must parse, so it is required. `Option<T>` makes it optional.

Attributes, all inside `#[form(...)]`:

- `label = "..."` (default: the field name, `user_name` becomes "User name"), `description`, `placeholder`, `autocomplete`, `input = "password"` (the input `type`; `email` sets `type="email"` itself).
- `required` or `required = "message"`. The default message names the field ("Email is required."), since an error is announced on its own.
- `email`, `min_len = n`, `max_len = n` for text; `min = n`, `max = n` and `invalid = "message"` (when it doesn't parse) for parsed types; `validate = my_rule` (any `fn(&str) -> Result<(), String>`, repeatable).
- `textarea`, `select = options_fn` or `combobox = options_fn` (a `fn() -> Vec<FieldOption>`) to change the control.

Rules run in that order and the first failure shows. On an optional field the rules only check what was typed. Required fields get `aria-required`, and the errors use the same `aria-invalid` / `aria-describedby` / `role="alert"` wiring as the hand-written fields. Unknown attributes, and ones that don't fit the type (`email` on a number, `required` on an `Option`), are compile errors.

The generated code names the kit as `::ui`. If you copied the form component into your app (`rust-ui add form`), add the `rust-ui-form-derive` crate and point it at your copy: `#[form(path = "crate::components::form")]` on the struct.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: each control has a `<label>`; invalid controls get `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby` pointing at the description and the error. The error is `role="alert"` so it is announced.
- Keyboard: on a failed submit focus moves to the first invalid field. Enter submits as usual.
- Reduced motion: no animation.

Use `FormField` directly (value, error, ids, set, load, blur, mounted) to wire your own controls. Pass the control's `onmounted` to `field.mounted(e)` so a failed submit can focus it on every renderer, native included. `Select` and `Combobox` move `id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` to their focusable control (the trigger button or the text input), so a `<label for>` and focus-on-error reach it.

## Source

Original to this repo. The idea (a form-state hook plus bound fields) follows the pattern in Rust/UI's `use_form`, but nothing is copied; it is not Leptos- or serde-based.

## Stability

Experimental, `#[derive(Form)]` included. The form API was reshaped twice in October 2026 (`mounted`, then `field_with`, `load` and the select and combobox fields), and binding a raw `Select` is still open. It may change in any release; see `docs/STABILITY.md` in the kit repository.

## API

```rust
/// Checks one value and returns the message to show when it is not acceptable.
pub type Validator;

/// The value must not be empty (whitespace only counts as empty).
pub fn required() -> Validator

/// A deliberately loose `x@y.z` check.
pub fn email() -> Validator

pub fn min_len(min: usize) -> Validator

pub fn max_len(max: usize) -> Validator

/// A time (`"14:05"`) from `min` to `max`, both inclusive; a `max` earlier than `min` wraps
/// past midnight (22:00 to 02:00). Empty and unreadable values pass, so pair it with
/// `required()` when the time must be given. [`TimeField`] adds this rule itself when given
/// `min` or `max`.
pub fn time_between(
    min: Option<Time>,
    max: Option<Time>,
    message: impl Into<String>,
) -> Validator

/// A date range (`"2026-10-15/2026-10-20"`) that spans at least `min` and at most `max`
/// days (nights, for a stay). Empty and unreadable values pass, like [`time_between`].
pub fn days_between(min: Option<u32>, max: Option<u32>, message: impl Into<String>) -> Validator

/// Your own rule: return `Err(message)` to reject.
pub fn custom(rule: impl Fn(&str) -> Result<(), String> + 'static) -> Validator

/// The first failing message, checking rules in order. Rules other than `required()` do not
/// special-case empty input, so list `required()` first (or leave it out for an optional field
/// and make your own rules accept empty).
pub fn first_error(validators: &[Validator], value: &str) -> Option<String>

/// One field's state: value, error and touched flag, plus the ids that tie its label,
/// description and error message together. Create with [`FormState::field`].
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub struct FormField {
    value: Signal<String>,
    initial: Signal<String>,
    error: Signal<Option<String>>,
    touched: Signal<bool>,
    ids: Signal<FieldIds>,
    validators: Signal<Vec<ValidatorBox>>,
    /// The control, once mounted (see [`FormField::mounted`]).
    element: Signal<Option<Rc<MountedData>>>,
}

/// All the fields of one form. Create with [`use_form`].
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub struct FormState {
    fields: Signal<Vec<FormField>>,
}

/// Create the state for one form.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub fn use_form() -> FormState

/// A `<form>` wired to a [`FormState`]: native validation is off (we show our own messages),
/// and submit validates, focuses the first error, or calls `on_valid`.
#[component]
pub fn Form(
    /// The form's state: a [`FormState`], or a `#[derive(Form)]` form (it converts).
    #[props(into)]
    state: FormState,
    #[props(default)] on_valid: Callback<()>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// Label, input, optional description and error, all wired to a [`FormField`] with the right
/// `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`.
#[component]
pub fn TextField(
    field: FormField,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(into, default)] description: Option<String>,
    #[props(into, default = "text".to_string())] r#type: String,
    #[props(into, default)] placeholder: Option<String>,
    #[props(into, default)] autocomplete: Option<String>,
    /// Anything else for the `<input>`: `inputmode`, `maxlength`, `pattern`, `class`, ...
    /// The field's own wiring (`id`, `value`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`) wins.
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=input)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element

/// One choice of a [`SelectField`] or [`ComboboxField`]: the value stored in the field and
/// the text shown. `"UTC".into()` uses the same text for both.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub struct FieldOption {
    pub value: String,
    pub label: String,
}

/// A [`Select`] bound to a [`FormField`], with the same wiring as [`TextField`]: a label, the
/// error and description in `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, and focus on a failed submit.
/// The field holds the chosen option's `value` (empty while nothing is chosen, so
/// `required()` works). It validates when the list closes, as a text field does on blur.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn SelectField(
    field: FormField,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    options: Vec<FieldOption>,
    #[props(into, default)] description: Option<String>,
    #[props(into, default)] placeholder: Option<String>,
    /// Mark the control `aria-required` (pair it with a `required()` rule).
    #[props(default)]
    required: bool,
) -> Element

/// A searchable [`Combobox`] bound to a [`FormField`], wired like [`SelectField`]. `empty` is
/// shown when the search matches nothing.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn ComboboxField(
    field: FormField,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    options: Vec<FieldOption>,
    #[props(into, default)] description: Option<String>,
    #[props(into, default)] placeholder: String,
    #[props(into, default = "No results.".to_string())] empty: String,
    /// Mark the control `aria-required` (pair it with a `required()` rule).
    #[props(default)]
    required: bool,
) -> Element

/// A multi-line [`Textarea`] bound to a [`FormField`], wired like [`TextField`]. Extra
/// attributes (`rows`, `maxlength`, ...) go to the `<textarea>`.
#[component]
pub fn TextareaField(
    field: FormField,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(into, default)] description: Option<String>,
    #[props(into, default)] placeholder: Option<String>,
    /// Grow with the text (see [`Textarea`]).
    #[props(default)]
    autosize: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=textarea)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element

/// A [`Checkbox`] with its label beside it, bound to a [`FormField`] ("I accept the terms").
/// The field holds `"true"` while checked and `""` while not, so `required()` (or `custom` with
/// your own message) makes it mandatory. It validates on every change, and a failed submit
/// focuses it like any other field.
#[component]
pub fn CheckboxField(
    field: FormField,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(into, default)] description: Option<String>,
    /// Mark the control `aria-required` (pair it with a `required()` rule).
    #[props(default)]
    required: bool,
) -> Element

/// A [`TimePicker`](crate::components::time_picker::TimePicker) bound to a [`FormField`], wired
/// like [`TextField`]. The field holds `"14:05"` (`"14:05:09"` with `seconds`), the format of
/// `<input type="time">`, and stays empty until every segment is filled, so `required()`
/// works. It validates when focus leaves the picker.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn TimeField(
    field: FormField,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(into, default)] description: Option<String>,
    #[props(default)] hour_cycle: HourCycle,
    #[props(default)] seconds: bool,
    #[props(default = 1)] minute_step: u8,
    /// Earliest allowed time. With `min` or `max` the field also gets a range rule
    /// ([`time_between`]), with the message from `UiStrings::time_out_of_range`.
    #[props(default)]
    min: Option<Time>,
    /// Latest allowed time (inclusive); earlier than `min` wraps past midnight.
    #[props(default)]
    max: Option<Time>,
) -> Element

/// A [`DateTimePicker`] bound to a [`FormField`], wired like [`TextField`]. The field holds
/// `"2026-10-15T14:05"`, the format of `<input type="datetime-local">`, and stays empty until
/// both the date and the time are entered. It validates when focus leaves the picker; a
/// failed submit focuses the time's first segment.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn DateTimeField(
    field: FormField,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(into, default)] description: Option<String>,
    #[props(default)] hour_cycle: HourCycle,
    #[props(default)] seconds: bool,
    #[props(default = 1)] minute_step: u8,
    /// Filled in when a date is picked while the time is still empty.
    #[props(default)]
    default_time: Option<Time>,
) -> Element

/// A [`DateRangePicker`] bound to a [`FormField`]. The field holds `"2026-10-15/2026-10-20"`
/// (an ISO 8601 interval; [`parse_iso_date_range`] reads it back) and stays empty until both
/// dates are entered, so `required()` works; [`days_between`] limits the length. The picker
/// group is named by the label and described by the description and error. It validates when
/// focus leaves the picker, its calendar included; a failed submit focuses the group.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn DateRangeField(
    field: FormField,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(into, default)] description: Option<String>,
    #[props(default = Date::from_calendar_date(1925, Month::January, 1).expect("valid date"))]
    min_date: Date,
    #[props(default = Date::from_calendar_date(2050, Month::December, 31).expect("valid date"))]
    max_date: Date,
    /// Dates that can't be picked (already booked, closed).
    #[props(default)]
    disabled_ranges: ReadSignal<Vec<DateRange>>,
    /// How many months the calendar shows at once.
    #[props(default = 1)]
    month_count: u8,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::Button;
use crate::components::callout::{Callout, CalloutVariant};
use crate::components::form::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let form = use_form();
    let email = form.field(vec![required(), email()]);
    let password = form.field(vec![required(), min_len(8)]);
    let role = form.field(vec![custom(|v| {
        if v.is_empty() {
            Err("Pick a role.".to_string())
        } else {
            Ok(())
        }
    })]);
    let zone = form.field_with("UTC", vec![required()]);
    let mut done = use_signal(|| false);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 1rem; max-width: 22rem;",
            Form {
                state: form,
                on_valid: move |_| {
                    done.set(true);
                    form.reset();
                },
                TextField {
                    field: email,
                    label: "Email",
                    r#type: "email",
                    placeholder: "you@example.com",
                    autocomplete: "email",
                    description: "We never share it.",
                }
                TextField {
                    field: password,
                    label: "Password",
                    r#type: "password",
                    autocomplete: "new-password",
                }
                SelectField {
                    field: role,
                    label: "Role",
                    placeholder: "Choose a role",
                    options: vec![
                        FieldOption::new("dev", "Developer"),
                        FieldOption::new("design", "Designer"),
                        FieldOption::new("pm", "Product manager"),
                    ],
                }
                ComboboxField {
                    field: zone,
                    label: "Time zone",
                    description: "Resets to UTC.",
                    placeholder: "Search time zones",
                    options: vec!["UTC".into(), "Europe/London".into(), "Asia/Tokyo".into()],
                }
                Button { r#type: "submit", "Create account" }
            }
            if done() {
                Callout { variant: CalloutVariant::Success, "Account created." }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

---

# Hooks

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add hooks` or `dx components add hooks --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::hooks::*;` after copying, or `use ui::hooks::{...};` (by path, no glob) with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

Hooks shared by the components and by apps.

The sidebar keeps its own `use_is_mobile` (from upstream, through `document::eval`, so it also works in the desktop webview); `use_media_query(MOBILE_QUERY)` is the web-sys equivalent. `rust-ui add hooks` copies them; a component that uses one (the command palette uses `use_hotkey`) brings this item along when you add it.

| Hook | What it does |
|---|---|
| `use_hotkey("k", f)` | Runs `f` on Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on macOS) anywhere on the page |
| `use_selection()` / `use_selected(sel, key)` | Row selection that re-renders only the rows that change |
| `use_media_query("(min-width: 1024px)")` | Follows a CSS media query |
| `MOBILE_QUERY` | `"(max-width: 767px)"`, the kit's phone breakpoint, for `use_media_query` |
| `use_copy_clipboard()` | Copies text; a flag stays true for two seconds after the copy succeeds |

The ones that listen to the browser (`use_hotkey`, `use_media_query`, `use_copy_clipboard`) are web only: they use Rust `web-sys` listeners, never JavaScript of ours, and remove them when the component unmounts. They are compiled in for `wasm32` builds with a `web` feature in your crate (the `dx new` template has one). On desktop and native they do nothing, so keep a visible way to do the same thing (a button for the shortcut, selectable text next to the copy button, a layout that works when the query is false).

## Accessibility

- Role and name: hooks render nothing. Announce what they change: give a copy button a visible "Copied" state, and show the shortcut next to the button it mirrors (`Kbd`).
- Keyboard: `use_hotkey` only fires on Ctrl or Cmd with no Alt or Shift, so it does not take keys that screen readers and text inputs use.
- Reduced motion: none.

## Source

`use_hotkey` and `Selection` are original to this repo. `use_media_query` and `use_copy_clipboard` follow Rust/UI's hooks (rust-ui/ui@43ddc65, MIT), rewritten to remove their listeners on unmount and to report a copy only after the browser confirms it.

## API

```rust
/// How long `copied` stays true after a successful copy.
pub const COPIED_FOR_MS: i32;

/// Copies text to the clipboard. Returns the copy callback and a flag that is true for
/// [`COPIED_FOR_MS`] after the browser confirms the copy, for a "Copied" label:
///
/// ```rust,ignore
/// let (copy, copied) = use_copy_clipboard();
/// rsx! { Button { onclick: move |_| copy.call("cargo add rust-ui".into()),
///     if copied() { "Copied" } else { "Copy" } } }
/// ```
///
/// Announce the result for screen readers too (a toast, or the button's own text as above).
///
/// Web only: the async Clipboard API through web-sys, which needs a secure context (https or
/// localhost). On desktop and native it does nothing and `copied` stays false, so keep the
/// text itself selectable.
pub fn use_copy_clipboard() -> (Callback<String>, ReadSignal<bool>)

/// Is this key event Ctrl+`key` (or Cmd+`key` on macOS), with no Alt or Shift?
pub fn is_hotkey(key: &str, pressed: &str, ctrl: bool, meta: bool, alt: bool, shift: bool) -> bool

/// Runs `on_press` when Ctrl+`key` (Cmd+`key` on macOS) is pressed anywhere on the page,
/// for example `use_hotkey("k", move || open.set(true))` to open a command palette.
///
/// Web only: a Rust (web-sys) listener on `window`, no JavaScript (docs/GUARDRAILS.md).
/// On desktop and native it does nothing, so always keep a visible button that does the
/// same thing.
pub fn use_hotkey(key: &'static str, mut on_press: impl FnMut() + 'static)

/// Phone-sized viewports, matching the kit's CSS breakpoint: `use_media_query(MOBILE_QUERY)`.
pub const MOBILE_QUERY: &str;

/// Whether the CSS media `query` matches, updated when it changes (window resized, OS theme
/// switched, and so on): `let wide = use_media_query("(min-width: 1024px)");`.
///
/// Prefer a CSS `@media` rule when only styling changes; use this when the *markup* has to
/// differ, such as a sheet on phones and a popover on desktop.
///
/// Web only: a Rust (web-sys) listener on the `MediaQueryList`, removed when the component
/// unmounts. On desktop and native, and during server rendering, it is always `false`, so
/// make `false` the layout that works everywhere.
pub fn use_media_query(query: &'static str) -> ReadSignal<bool>

/// The `href` to render for `href`: inside a router with a base path (for example a site
/// served from `/my-app/`), an in-app path gets that prefix, so opening it in a new tab or
/// copying it works. Anything else is returned unchanged.
pub fn in_app_href(href: &str) -> String

/// Sends a plain left click on a link to `href` through the router, when there is one and
/// it knows the path. Returns `true` when it did (the browser's own navigation is then
/// cancelled). Clicks with a modifier key (new tab, new window), other buttons, links with
/// a `target`, and clicks whose default was already prevented are left alone.
pub fn follow_in_app(href: &str, event: &MouseEvent) -> bool

/// Whether `href` is the path the router is showing now, for `aria-current="page"`.
pub fn is_current_route(href: &str) -> bool

/// Which rows of a list are selected, with updates that touch only the rows that change.
///
/// A plain `Signal<HashSet<K>>` re-renders every row that reads it whenever the selection
/// changes, so selecting one row of 1,000 diffs all 1,000. Here each row owns a `bool`
/// signal (from [`use_selected`]) and `Selection` flips only the rows that actually
/// change: selecting one row costs two row renders, whatever the list size. This is
/// SolidJS's `createSelector` idea on Dioxus signals.
///
/// ```rust,ignore
/// let sel = use_selection::<usize>();
/// // in each row component:
/// let selected = use_selected(sel, id);
/// rsx! { tr { class: if selected() { "selected" }, onclick: move |_| sel.select_only(id) } }
/// ```
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub struct Selection<K: 'static> {
    keys: CopyValue<HashSet<K>>,
    rows: CopyValue<HashMap<K, Signal<bool>>>,
    count: Signal<usize>,
}

/// Creates an empty [`Selection`] owned by the calling component.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub fn use_selection<K: Hash + Eq + Clone + 'static>() -> Selection<K>

/// Whether the row `key` is selected. Re-renders the calling row only when its own state
/// changes. The key must not change for the life of the row (key the row by it).
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub fn use_selected<K: Hash + Eq + Clone + 'static>(
    selection: Selection<K>,
    key: K,
) -> ReadSignal<bool>
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::hooks::{use_copy_clipboard, use_media_query, MOBILE_QUERY};
use crate::components::kbd::{Kbd, KbdGroup};
use dioxus::prelude::*;

const INSTALL: &str = "rust-ui add hooks";

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mobile = use_media_query(MOBILE_QUERY);
    let dark = use_media_query("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)");
    let (copy, copied) = use_copy_clipboard();
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.75rem;",
            p { style: "margin: 0;",
                "use_media_query(MOBILE_QUERY): "
                strong { if mobile() { "phone-sized" } else { "wider than a phone" } }
                ". use_media_query(prefers-color-scheme: dark): "
                strong { if dark() { "dark" } else { "light (or not on the web)" } }
                "."
            }
            div { style: "display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap;",
                code { "{INSTALL}" }
                Button {
                    variant: ButtonVariant::Outline,
                    onclick: move |_| copy.call(INSTALL.to_string()),
                    if copied() { "Copied" } else { "Copy" }
                }
            }
            p { style: "margin: 0;",
                "use_hotkey: "
                KbdGroup {
                    Kbd { "Ctrl" }
                    Kbd { "K" }
                }
                " opens the command palette above."
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Hover card

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add hover_card` or `dx components add hover_card --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::hover_card::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The HoverCard component can be used to display additional information when a user hovers over an element. It is useful for showing tooltips, additional details, or any other content that should be revealed on hover.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The HoverCard component wraps the trigger element and the content that will be displayed on hover.
HoverCard {
    HoverCardTrigger {
        // Anything inside the trigger (icon, text, rich markup) acts as the hover target.
        {children}
    }
    HoverCardContent {
        side: ContentSide::Bottom,
        align: ContentAlign::Start,
        {children}
    }
}
```

## Don't put controls in the trigger

`HoverCardTrigger` is itself focusable (`role="button"`, `tabindex="0"`), so keyboard users can open the card. A button or link inside it is a control inside a control (axe `nested-interactive`), and screen readers announce it badly. Put text, an avatar or an icon directly inside the trigger, and put links and buttons inside `HoverCardContent` (or next to the trigger).

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn HoverCard(props: HoverCardProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn HoverCardTrigger(props: HoverCardTriggerProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn HoverCardContent(props: HoverCardContentProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::hover_card::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;
use dioxus_primitives::ContentSide;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "padding: 50px; display: flex; flex-direction: row; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 40px; justify-content: center; align-items: center;",
            HoverCard {
                HoverCardTrigger {
                    i { "Dioxus" }
                }
                HoverCardContent { side: ContentSide::Bottom,
                    div { padding: "1rem",
                        "Dioxus is"
                        i { " the " }
                        "Rust framework for building fullstack web, desktop, and mobile apps. Iterate with live hotreloading, add server functions, and deploy in record time."
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```
