# Icons

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add icons` or `dx components add icons --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::icons::*;` after copying, or `use ui::icons::{...};` (by path, no glob) with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The kit's one icon set: every Lucide icon, generated into Rust as shape data plus one component per icon, so apps and components import icons from one place.

```rust
use ui::icons::{lucide, Icon, IconSize, Search, Trash};

rsx! {
    // Decorative (the default): the button text names the action.
    button { Trash { size: IconSize::Sm } "Delete" }
    // Icon-only control: name the control, not the SVG.
    button { "aria-label": "Search", Search { size: IconSize::Sm } }
    // An icon that carries meaning on its own gets a label (role="img").
    Icon { icon: lucide::BADGE_CHECK, label: "Verified" }
}
```

There are two ways to draw an icon. Each Lucide icon is a component (`Check`, `ChevronRight`), and also a constant with its shapes (`lucide::CHECK`) that `Icon` draws; use the constant when the icon is a value, such as a field in a nav item list. Old Lucide names (`AlertCircle` for `CircleAlert`) keep working.

Only the icons you name end up in your app's binary. `lucide::ALL` lists every icon; naming it pulls them all in, so keep it to tests and tools.

Import icons by path (`ui::icons::Check`), not with a glob: Lucide has icons named `Link`, `Badge`, `Calendar` and so on that would clash with the components.

## Size and stroke

- `size: IconSize::Sm` (and `Xs`, `Md`, `Lg`, `Xl`) read `--icon-size-sm` and friends from the theme. The default is `Lg`, 24px like Lucide's own.
- `size: 16` is pixels and `size: "1em"` any CSS length, when an icon must follow the text or a fixed box.
- The stroke is `--icon-stroke-width` (2) unless you pass `stroke_width`.
- Icons draw with `currentColor`, so they follow the text colour in both themes. Any other SVG attribute passes through (`class`, `style`, `"data-*"`).

## Right-to-left

Icons that point along the reading direction (arrows and chevrons that point left or right, undo and redo, reply, panel toggles, log in and out) are mirrored when they sit inside `dir="rtl"`. Pass `mirror_rtl: false` to keep one as drawn, or `mirror_rtl: true` to mirror another.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: icons are `aria-hidden="true"` unless you give them a `label`, which makes them `role="img"` with that name. Put the name of an icon-only button on the button (`aria-label` or `sr-only` text), not on the icon.
- Keyboard: not focusable.
- Reduced motion: icons do not animate.

## Stability

`Icon`, `IconData`, `IconNode`, the `lucide` constants and the `label`, `mirror_rtl` and named `size` props are experimental. The icon component names (`ui::icons::Check`) are stable.

## Source

Generated by `scripts/gen-lucide-icons.mjs` from the `lucide-static` npm package (Lucide 1.57.0, ISC; the Feather-derived icons MIT). The licence is in the header of `lucide.rs` and in `crates/ui/LICENSE-lucide`. The choice is in `docs/ICONS.md`.

## API

```rust
/// One shape of an icon, in Lucide's 24×24 coordinate space. Values are kept as Lucide's text.
pub enum IconNode {
    /// `<path d>`.
    Path { d: &'static str },
    /// `<circle cx cy r>`; `filled` draws it with `fill="currentColor"` (a dot).
    Circle {
        cx: &'static str,
        cy: &'static str,
        r: &'static str,
        filled: bool,
    },
    /// `<ellipse cx cy rx ry>`.
    Ellipse {
        cx: &'static str,
        cy: &'static str,
        rx: &'static str,
        ry: &'static str,
    },
    /// `<rect x y width height rx ry>`.
    Rect {
        x: &'static str,
        y: &'static str,
        width: &'static str,
        height: &'static str,
        rx: Option<&'static str>,
        ry: Option<&'static str>,
    },
    /// `<line x1 y1 x2 y2>`.
    Line {
        x1: &'static str,
        y1: &'static str,
        x2: &'static str,
        y2: &'static str,
    },
    /// `<polyline points>`.
    Polyline { points: &'static str },
    /// `<polygon points>`.
    Polygon { points: &'static str },
}

/// One icon's shape data, as generated from Lucide: `ui::icons::lucide::CHECK`.
pub struct IconData {
    /// Lucide's name (`"chevron-right"`), also rendered as `data-icon`.
    pub name: &'static str,
    /// Whether the icon points along the reading direction and is mirrored in RTL text.
    pub mirror_rtl: bool,
    /// The shapes, drawn in order.
    pub nodes: &'static [IconNode],
}

/// Width and height of an icon. The named steps read `--icon-size-xs` … `--icon-size-xl`
/// from the theme; a number is pixels, and a string is any CSS length (`"1rem"`, `"1em"`).
///
/// The default, [`IconSize::Lg`], is 24px like Lucide's own.
pub enum IconSize {
    /// `--icon-size-xs` (0.75rem).
    Xs,
    /// `--icon-size-sm` (1rem): inside buttons, inputs and menus.
    Sm,
    /// `--icon-size-md` (1.25rem).
    Md,
    /// `--icon-size-lg` (1.5rem, 24px). The default.
    #[default]
    Lg,
    /// `--icon-size-xl` (2rem).
    Xl,
    /// A fixed width and height (`16`, `"1rem"`).
    Custom(AttributeValue),
}

/// Props of every per-icon component (`Check`, `ChevronRight`, ...).
pub struct IconProps {
    /// Width and height; a theme step ([`IconSize::Sm`]), pixels (`16`) or a CSS length (`"1rem"`).
    #[props(into, default)]
    pub size: IconSize,
    /// Accessible name. With one the icon is `role="img"`; without one it is `aria-hidden`.
    /// Leave it out when text next to the icon (or the control holding it) already says the same.
    #[props(into, default)]
    pub label: Option<String>,
    /// Override whether the icon mirrors in right-to-left text (default: the icon's own setting).
    #[props(default)]
    pub mirror_rtl: Option<bool>,
    /// Any SVG attribute (`stroke_width`, `class`, `style`, `"data-*"`), applied to the `<svg>`.
    #[props(extends = SvgAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
}

/// Props of [`Icon`]: the icon's shape data plus everything in [`IconProps`].
pub struct IconDataProps {
    /// The icon's shape data, from [`lucide`](super::lucide).
    pub icon: IconData,
    /// Width and height; a theme step ([`IconSize::Sm`]), pixels (`16`) or a CSS length.
    #[props(into, default)]
    pub size: IconSize,
    /// Accessible name. With one the icon is `role="img"`; without one it is `aria-hidden`.
    #[props(into, default)]
    pub label: Option<String>,
    /// Override whether the icon mirrors in right-to-left text.
    #[props(default)]
    pub mirror_rtl: Option<bool>,
    /// Any SVG attribute, applied to the `<svg>`.
    #[props(extends = SvgAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
}

/// Draws an icon from its shape data: `Icon { icon: lucide::CHECK, label: "Saved" }`.
///
/// Same props as the per-icon components; use this when the icon is a value (stored in a
/// list or chosen at runtime).
pub fn Icon(props: IconDataProps) -> Element

pub use lucide::components::*;
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant, IconButton};
use crate::components::icons::{
    lucide, Bell, ChevronRight, Copy, Download, Heart, Icon, IconSize, Search, Settings, Star,
    Trash,
};
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem;",
            // Decorative icons in a row: the label below each one is the text.
            ul {
                "aria-label": "Sample icons",
                style: "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1rem; list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0;",
                IconCell { label: "Bell", Bell { size: "1.25rem", "aria-hidden": "true" } }
                IconCell { label: "Heart", Heart { size: "1.25rem", "aria-hidden": "true" } }
                IconCell { label: "Settings", Settings { size: "1.25rem", "aria-hidden": "true" } }
                IconCell { label: "Star", Star { size: "1.25rem", "aria-hidden": "true" } }
                IconCell { label: "Download", Download { size: "1.25rem", "aria-hidden": "true" } }
            }
            // Theme sizes (`--icon-size-*`), and an icon chosen at runtime from its data.
            div { style: "display: flex; gap: 0.75rem; align-items: end;",
                for size in [IconSize::Xs, IconSize::Sm, IconSize::Md, IconSize::Lg, IconSize::Xl] {
                    Icon { icon: lucide::SPARKLES, size }
                }
            }
            // A labelled icon is an image with a name; nothing else says "Verified" here.
            p { style: "display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; align-items: center; margin: 0;",
                "Ada Lovelace"
                Icon { icon: lucide::BADGE_CHECK, size: IconSize::Sm, label: "Verified" }
            }
            // Directional icons mirror in right-to-left text.
            div { style: "display: flex; gap: 1.5rem;",
                span { dir: "ltr", style: "display: inline-flex; gap: 0.25rem; align-items: center;",
                    "Next"
                    ChevronRight { size: IconSize::Sm }
                }
                span {
                    dir: "rtl",
                    lang: "ar",
                    style: "display: inline-flex; gap: 0.25rem; align-items: center;",
                    "التالي"
                    ChevronRight { size: IconSize::Sm }
                }
            }
            div { style: "display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; align-items: center;",
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline,
                    Copy { size: "1rem", "aria-hidden": "true" }
                    "Copy"
                }
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Destructive,
                    Trash { size: "1rem", "aria-hidden": "true" }
                    "Delete"
                }
                // Icon-only: `IconButton`'s required `label` carries the name.
                IconButton { label: "Search", variant: ButtonVariant::Ghost,
                    Search { size: "1rem", "aria-hidden": "true" }
                }
                // Or with hidden text (the theme's `sr-only` class), which translators and
                // find-in-page also see.
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Ghost,
                    Settings { size: "1rem", "aria-hidden": "true" }
                    span { class: "sr-only", "Settings" }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

#[component]
fn IconCell(label: &'static str, children: Element) -> Element {
    rsx! {
        li { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 0.25rem; font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--secondary-color-5);",
            {children}
            span { "{label}" }
        }
    }
}
```

# Input

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add input` or `dx components add input --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::input::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The input element is used to accept a text input from the user. It can be styled and configured to fit various use cases, such as forms or search bars.

## Component Structure

```rust
input {
    // Global html attributes
    class: "dx-input",
    // Children
    {children}
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Input(
    oninput: Option<EventHandler<FormEvent>>,
    onchange: Option<EventHandler<FormEvent>>,
    oninvalid: Option<EventHandler<FormEvent>>,
    onselect: Option<EventHandler<SelectionEvent>>,
    onselectionchange: Option<EventHandler<SelectionEvent>>,
    onfocus: Option<EventHandler<FocusEvent>>,
    onblur: Option<EventHandler<FocusEvent>>,
    onfocusin: Option<EventHandler<FocusEvent>>,
    onfocusout: Option<EventHandler<FocusEvent>>,
    onkeydown: Option<EventHandler<KeyboardEvent>>,
    onkeypress: Option<EventHandler<KeyboardEvent>>,
    onkeyup: Option<EventHandler<KeyboardEvent>>,
    onwheel: Option<EventHandler<WheelEvent>>,
    oncompositionstart: Option<EventHandler<CompositionEvent>>,
    oncompositionupdate: Option<EventHandler<CompositionEvent>>,
    oncompositionend: Option<EventHandler<CompositionEvent>>,
    oncopy: Option<EventHandler<ClipboardEvent>>,
    oncut: Option<EventHandler<ClipboardEvent>>,
    onpaste: Option<EventHandler<ClipboardEvent>>,
    onmounted: Option<EventHandler<MountedEvent>>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=input)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::input::*;
use crate::components::label::Label;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut name = use_signal(String::new);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 0.5rem; max-width: 20rem;",
            Label { html_for: "gallery-name", "Name" }
            Input {
                id: "gallery-name",
                placeholder: "Enter your name",
                value: name,
                oninput: move |e: FormEvent| name.set(e.value()),
            }
            if !name.read().is_empty() {
                p { style: "margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem;", "Hello, {name}!" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# InputGroup

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add input_group` or `dx components add input_group --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::input_group::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

An input with text, icons or buttons attached inside one bordered box.

```rust
InputGroup {
    InputGroupAddon { "https://" }
    InputGroupInput { "aria-label": "Website" }
    InputGroupAddon { end: true, Button { "Go" } }
}
```

The group draws the border and the focus ring (`:focus-within`), so the control inside has none. `invalid` turns the border to the error colour.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: `role="group"`; the control needs its own label (`<label for>` or `aria-label`), because addon text is not a label. Add `aria-invalid` on the control when invalid and show an error message linked with `aria-describedby`.
- Keyboard: Tab moves between the control and any buttons in addons.
- Reduced motion: no animation.

## Source

Structure adapted from Rust/UI's `input_group.rs` (MIT, rust-ui/ui commit 43ddc65); styling and API rewritten.

## API

```rust
/// An input with text, icons or buttons attached inside one bordered box ("https://", "USD",
/// a search button). Use `InputGroupInput` for the control and `InputGroupAddon` for the rest.
/// Give the control a visible `<label>` or `aria-label`.
#[component]
pub fn InputGroup(
    #[props(default)] invalid: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// Static content or a button before (default) or after (`end`) the control.
#[component]
pub fn InputGroupAddon(
    #[props(default)] end: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// The text control. It has no border of its own; the group draws it.
#[component]
pub fn InputGroupInput(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=input)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    oninput: Option<EventHandler<FormEvent>>,
    onblur: Option<EventHandler<FocusEvent>>,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::input_group::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 1rem; max-width: 24rem;",
            InputGroup {
                InputGroupAddon { "https://" }
                InputGroupInput { "aria-label": "Website", placeholder: "example.com" }
            }
            InputGroup {
                InputGroupInput { "aria-label": "Amount", r#type: "number", placeholder: "0.00" }
                InputGroupAddon { end: true, "USD" }
            }
            InputGroup { invalid: true,
                InputGroupInput { "aria-label": "Username", value: "taken_name", "aria-invalid": "true" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# InputOtp

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add input_otp` or `dx components add input_otp --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::input_otp::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A one-time-code input: one box per character.

```rust
InputOtp { label: "Verification code", length: 6, group: 3, on_complete: move |code| verify(code) }
```

Typing advances to the next box; Backspace on an empty box clears and goes back; Left/Right/Home/End move; pasting (or an SMS autofill into the first box, which carries `autocomplete="one-time-code"`) spreads across the boxes. `numeric: false` accepts letters too. Set `invalid` to show an error state (pair it with a visible error message).

## Accessibility

- Role and name: a `role="group"` named by `label`; every box is a real `<input>` named "label, character n of N".
- Keyboard: as above; Tab leaves the group normally.
- Reduced motion: no animation.

## Source

Original to this repo. Rust/UI has an `input_otp` driven by a wasm-bindgen DOM controller; this one is plain Dioxus state and native inputs.

## API

```rust
/// Something the user did to one box of an [`InputOtp`].
pub enum OtpEvent {
    /// The box at `slot` received `text`: one character when typing, several for a paste
    /// or SMS autofill, empty when its character was deleted.
    Input {
        slot: usize,
        text: String,
    },
    /// Backspace in the box at `slot`.
    Backspace(usize),
    Left(usize),
    Right(usize),
    Home,
    End,
}

/// What [`OtpState::apply`] did.
pub enum OtpOutcome {
    /// Not ours; let the browser handle the key.
    Ignored,
    /// Only focus moved.
    Moved,
    /// The code changed (and focus may have moved).
    Changed,
}

/// The code inside an [`InputOtp`] and which box has focus. Pure, so the keyboard
/// behaviour is tested without a browser (`crates/ui/tests/keyboard_state.rs`).
pub struct OtpState {
    pub chars: Vec<Option<char>>,
    pub focus: usize,
    /// Accept only digits (otherwise letters and digits).
    pub numeric: bool,
}

/// One-time-code input: one box per character with auto-advance, Backspace to go back, arrow
/// keys, and paste or SMS autofill spread across the boxes. Each box is a real input, so it
/// works with screen readers and password managers.
#[component]
pub fn InputOtp(
    /// Number of characters.
    #[props(default = 6)]
    length: usize,
    /// Accessible name of the whole code, for example "Verification code".
    #[props(into)]
    label: Option<String>,
    /// Only accept digits (the default). Off accepts letters and digits.
    #[props(default = true)]
    numeric: bool,
    /// Draw a dash after every `group` boxes (0 for none), for example 3 for `123-456`.
    #[props(default = 0)]
    group: usize,
    #[props(default)] invalid: bool,
    #[props(default)] disabled: bool,
    /// Called on every change with the code so far.
    #[props(default)]
    on_change: Callback<String>,
    /// Called once all boxes are filled.
    #[props(default)]
    on_complete: Callback<String>,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::input_otp::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut code = use_signal(String::new);
    let mut done = use_signal(|| false);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 0.75rem;",
            InputOtp {
                label: "Verification code",
                length: 6,
                group: 3,
                on_change: move |c: String| {
                    code.set(c);
                    done.set(false);
                },
                on_complete: move |_| done.set(true),
            }
            p { style: "margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem;", role: "status",
                if done() { "Code {code()} entered." } else { "Enter the 6-digit code." }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

---

# Item

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add item` or `dx components add item --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `separator`).
- Import: `use crate::components::item::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A versatile component for displaying content with media, title, description, and actions.

`ItemGroup` is a list (`role="list"`), and every `Item` inside it is a list item (`role="listitem"`); an `Item` on its own has no role.

## Component Structure

```rust
ItemGroup {
    Item {
        // Available variants: Default, Outline, Muted
        variant: ItemVariant::Outline,

        // Available sizes: Default, Sm
        size: ItemSize::Default,

        ItemHeader {
            "Optional header"
        }

        ItemMedia {
            // Media variants: Default, Icon, Image
            variant: ItemMediaVariant::Image,
            img { src: "/path/to/image.png", alt: "Description" }
        }

        ItemContent {
            ItemTitle { "Item title" }
            ItemDescription { "Detailed description that can span multiple lines." }
        }

        ItemActions {
            button { "Primary action" }
        }

        ItemFooter {
            "Optional footer"
        }
    }

    ItemSeparator {}

    Item {
        // ... next item in the group
    }
}
```

## API

```rust
pub enum ItemVariant {
    #[default]
    Default,
    Outline,
    Muted,
}

pub enum ItemSize {
    #[default]
    Default,
    Sm,
}

pub enum ItemMediaVariant {
    #[default]
    Default,
    Icon,
    Image,
}

#[component]
pub fn ItemGroup(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=div)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ItemSeparator(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=div)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn Item(
    #[props(default)] variant: ItemVariant,
    #[props(default)] size: ItemSize,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=div)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    onclick: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    onkeydown: Option<EventHandler<KeyboardEvent>>,
    r#as: Option<Callback<Vec<Attribute>, Element>>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ItemMedia(
    #[props(default)] variant: ItemMediaVariant,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=div)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ItemContent(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=div)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ItemTitle(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=div)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ItemDescription(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=p)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ItemActions(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=div)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ItemHeader(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=div)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ItemFooter(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=div)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::icons::{BadgeCheck, ChevronRight};
use crate::components::item::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div {
            display: "flex",
            flex_direction: "column",
            gap: "1.5rem",
            width: "100%",
            max_width: "28rem",

            Item { variant: ItemVariant::Outline,
                ItemContent {
                    ItemTitle { "Basic Item" }
                    ItemDescription { "A simple item with title and description." }
                }
                ItemActions {
                    Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, "Action" }
                }
            }

            Item {
                variant: ItemVariant::Outline,
                size: ItemSize::Sm,
                as: move |attrs: Vec<Attribute>| rsx! {
                    a { href: "#", ..attrs,
                        ItemMedia { variant: ItemMediaVariant::Icon,
                            BadgeCheckIcon {}
                        }
                        ItemContent {
                            ItemTitle { "Your profile has been verified." }
                        }
                        ItemActions {
                            ChevronRightIcon {}
                        }
                    }
                },
            }
        }
    }
}

#[component]
fn BadgeCheckIcon() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        BadgeCheck { size: "20" }
    }
}

#[component]
fn ChevronRightIcon() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        ChevronRight { size: "16" }
    }
}
```

# Kbd

A keyboard key cap, for showing shortcuts.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: plain text in a `kbd` element
- Keyboard: none (not interactive)
- Reduced motion: none

## API

```rust
/// A keyboard key, e.g. `Kbd { "Ctrl" }`.

pub fn Kbd(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// A row of keys that make up one shortcut.

    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

# Label

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add label` or `dx components add label --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::label::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Label component is used to provide a label for form elements, enhancing accessibility and usability. It is typically used in conjunction with form controls like inputs, selects, and textareas.

## Component Structure

```rust
Label {
    html_for: "id", // The ID of the form control this label is associated with
}
button {
    id: "id", // The ID of the labeled element
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Label(props: LabelProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::input::Input;

    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 0.5rem; max-width: 20rem;",
            Label { html_for: "label-demo-name", "Your name" }
            Input { id: "label-demo-name", placeholder: "Ada Lovelace" }
        }
    }
}
```

# Link

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add link` or `dx components add link --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `hooks`, `icons`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::link::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

`TextLink`: an inline text link, a plain `<a href>` with an underline, the kit's text colour and a visible focus ring. `external: true` opens it in a new tab safely and says so; `current: true` marks the page you are on.

```rust
p { "Read the " TextLink { href: "/docs/theming", "theming guide" } "." }
TextLink { href: "https://lucide.dev", external: true, "Lucide" }
```

It is named `TextLink` so it never clashes with the router's `Link`.

## With the Dioxus router

Turn on the kit's `router` feature (`ui = { ..., features = ["router"] }`). Inside a `Router`, `TextLink`, `BreadcrumbLink` and `PaginationLink` then send a plain left click on a path `href` (`"/stays/3"`) through the router instead of loading the page again, add the router's base path to the rendered `href`, and `TextLink` marks itself `aria-current="page"` while its path is the current route. Ctrl/Cmd-click, middle-click, external links and `href`s the route enum doesn't parse stay ordinary links. `SidebarMenuButton` renders a button; for a route, pass the router's `Link` through its `as` prop. The helpers (`follow_in_app`, `in_app_href`, `is_current_route`) are in `ui::hooks` for your own links. For buttons that look like links, use `Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Link }`; for actions that do not navigate, use a button.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: a native link named by its text; external links add "(opens in a new tab)" (from `UiStrings`) and a hidden icon
- Keyboard: Tab reaches it, Enter follows it
- State: `aria-current="page"` when `current` (or, with the `router` feature, when its path is the current route), shown with a thicker underline, not colour alone
- Reduced motion: the hover underline changes without transition

## Source

Idea from Rust/UI `link.rs` (rust-ui/ui@43ddc65, MIT). Not copied: its `force_reload` mode renders a `<button>` that sets `window.location` through web-sys, which breaks middle-click, "open in new tab" and the link role, so it is left out; active-route matching (`PathMatchType`) is replaced by the explicit `current` prop.

## API

```rust
/// An inline text link: a plain `<a href>` with the kit's colours and focus ring.
///
/// Named `TextLink` so it does not clash with the router's `Link` when both preludes are
/// imported. With the kit's `router` feature, a path `href` inside a `Router` navigates in
/// the app and is marked `aria-current="page"` while it is the current route.
#[component]
pub fn TextLink(
    #[props(into)] href: String,
    /// Opens in a new tab, with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, an icon, and
    /// "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers.
    #[props(default)]
    external: bool,
    /// Marks the link for the page you are on (`aria-current="page"`), e.g. in a nav list.
    #[props(default)]
    current: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::link::TextLink;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.75rem;",
            p { style: "margin: 0;",
                "Read the "
                TextLink { href: "#theming", "theming guide" }
                " or browse the "
                TextLink { href: "https://lucide.dev/icons", external: true, "Lucide icons" }
                "."
            }
            nav { "aria-label": "Link demo",
                ul { style: "display: flex; gap: 1rem; list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0;",
                    li { TextLink { href: "#link", current: true, "Overview" } }
                    li { TextLink { href: "#chips", "Chips" } }
                    li { TextLink { href: "#icons", "Icons" } }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

---

# Marquee

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add marquee` or `dx components add marquee --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::marquee::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A looping auto-scrolling strip (logos, quotes).

## Accessibility

- Role and name: `role="group"` with `label`; the repeated copy is `aria-hidden` and `inert`.
- Keyboard: a Pause/Play button (`aria-pressed`) and focus-within pauses; WCAG 2.2.2 needs a pause control for motion over 5 s
- Reduced motion: scrolling stops and the row becomes horizontally scrollable

## Source

Structure and API adapted from Rust/UI (`marquee.rs`, rust-ui/ui commit 43ddc65, MIT); styling rewritten in plain CSS with this kit's tokens. Behaviour and accessibility were reworked here.

## API

```rust
/// A looping, auto-scrolling strip (logos, quotes). It has a pause button, pauses while
/// hovered or focused, and under reduced motion stops and becomes a scrollable row. The
/// repeated copy is hidden from assistive tech.
#[component]
pub fn Marquee(
    /// Seconds for one full loop.
    #[props(default = 20)]
    duration: u32,
    /// Accessible name for the strip. Defaults to "Scrolling content" ([`UiStrings`](crate::components::ui_strings::UiStrings)).
    #[props(into)]
    label: Option<String>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::marquee::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "max-width: 32rem;",
            Marquee { label: "Customer logos", duration: 15,
                for name in ["Acme", "Globex", "Initech", "Umbrella", "Hooli", "Stark"] {
                    span { style: "font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap;", "{name}" }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Menubar

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add menubar` or `dx components add menubar --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::menubar::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Menubar component can be used to display a menu bar with collapsible menus.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The Menubar component wraps the entire menu bar and contains the individual menus in the order of their index.
Menubar {
    // The MenubarMenu contains the individual menus that can be opened.
    MenubarMenu {
        // The index of the menu, used to determine the order in which menus are displayed.
        index: 0,
        // The menubar trigger is the element that will display the menu when activated.
        MenubarTrigger {
            // The content of the trigger button
            {children}
        }
        // The menubar content contains all the items that will be displayed in the menu when it is opened.
        MenubarContent {
            // Each menubar item represents an individual items in the menu.
            MenubarItem {
                // The value of the item which will be passed to the on_select callback when the item is selected.
                value: "",
                on_select: |value: String| {
                    // This callback is triggered when the item is selected.
                    // The value parameter contains the value of the selected item.
                },
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Menu Bar](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/) pattern. Roles: `menubar`, `menu`, `menuitem`. Works on native (Blitz): partly.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| ArrowRight | On a menu bar item | Moves focus to the next menu bar item. | yes |
| ArrowLeft | On a menu bar item | Moves focus to the previous menu bar item. | yes |
| ArrowDown | On a menu bar item | Opens its menu and moves focus to the first item. | yes |
| Enter | On a menu bar item | Opens or closes its menu. | yes |
| Escape | In an open menu | Closes the menu. | yes |
| Escape | After the menu closes | Focus goes back to the menubar item that opened it. | not yet |

States:

- `file-open`: The first menu is open.
- `file-closed`: The first menu is closed.

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Menubar(props: MenubarProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn MenubarMenu(props: MenubarMenuProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn MenubarTrigger(props: MenubarTriggerProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn MenubarContent(props: MenubarContentProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn MenubarItem(props: MenubarItemProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::menubar::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div {
            Menubar {
                MenubarMenu { index: 0usize,
                    MenubarTrigger { "File" }
                    MenubarContent {
                        MenubarItem {
                            index: 0usize,
                            value: "new".to_string(),
                            on_select: move |value| {
                                tracing::info!("Selected value: {}", value);
                            },
                            "New"
                        }
                        MenubarItem {
                            index: 1usize,
                            value: "open".to_string(),
                            disabled: true,
                            on_select: move |value| {
                                tracing::info!("Selected value: {}", value);
                            },
                            "Open"
                        }
                        MenubarItem {
                            index: 2usize,
                            value: "save".to_string(),
                            on_select: move |value| {
                                tracing::info!("Selected value: {}", value);
                            },
                            "Save"
                        }
                    }
                }
                MenubarMenu { index: 1usize,
                    MenubarTrigger { "Edit" }
                    MenubarContent {
                        MenubarItem {
                            index: 0usize,
                            value: "cut".to_string(),
                            on_select: move |value| {
                                tracing::info!("Selected value: {}", value);
                            },
                            "Cut"
                        }
                        MenubarItem {
                            index: 1usize,
                            value: "copy".to_string(),
                            on_select: move |value| {
                                tracing::info!("Selected value: {}", value);
                            },
                            "Copy"
                        }
                        MenubarItem {
                            index: 2usize,
                            value: "paste".to_string(),
                            on_select: move |value| {
                                tracing::info!("Selected value: {}", value);
                            },
                            "Paste"
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# MultiSelect

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add multi_select` or `dx components add multi_select --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::multi_select::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

Pick several options from a list.

```rust
MultiSelect { label: "Teams", options: vec![MultiOption::new("design", "Design"), MultiOption::new("eng", "Engineering")],
              on_change: move |values| save(values) }
```

A button shows the selection ("Design, Engineering +2"). It opens a panel with a filter box and a list of native checkboxes. `summary()` and `filter_options()` are public, pure helpers.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: the button has `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` and is named "label: current selection"; the panel is a `role="group"` of real checkboxes, so no custom listbox keyboard model is needed; the count or "No options match." is in a `role="status"` region.
- Focus: inside the open list, Tab moves through the filter, the checkboxes and the Clear/Done buttons. The keys are in the table below.
- Pointer: a click outside the panel closes it.
- Reduced motion: no animation.

## Source

Original to this repo (a checkbox-group disclosure, not an ARIA listbox). Rust/UI's `multi_select.rs` was only used to see the feature set.

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Disclosure with a checkbox list](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/) pattern. Works on native (Blitz): yes.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | On the button | Opens the list of choices. | yes |
| Space | On the button | Opens the list of choices. | yes |
| Escape | In the open list | Closes it and returns focus to the button. | yes |

States:

- `open`: The list of choices is shown.
- `closed`: Only the button, showing the current choice, is shown.

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
pub struct MultiOption {
    pub value: String,
    pub label: String,
}

/// Button text for the current selection: the placeholder, the labels (up to two), or
/// "A, B +3".
pub fn summary(labels: &[&str], placeholder: &str) -> String

/// Options whose label contains every word of the query, ignoring case.
pub fn filter_options<'a>(options: &'a [MultiOption], query: &str) -> Vec<&'a MultiOption>

/// Pick several options from a list. A button shows the selection and opens a panel of native
/// checkboxes with a filter box. Escape or "Done" closes it and returns focus to the button.
#[component]
pub fn MultiSelect(
    options: Vec<MultiOption>,
    /// Accessible name, for example "Teams".
    #[props(into)]
    label: String,
    /// Shown when nothing is selected. Defaults to "Select…" ([`UiStrings`](crate::components::ui_strings::UiStrings)).
    #[props(into)]
    placeholder: Option<String>,
    /// Values selected at first.
    #[props(default)]
    default_selected: Vec<String>,
    #[props(default)] disabled: bool,
    /// Called with the selected values (in option order) after every change.
    #[props(default)]
    on_change: Callback<Vec<String>>,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::multi_select::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut picked = use_signal(|| vec!["design".to_string()]);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 0.75rem;",
            MultiSelect {
                label: "Teams",
                placeholder: "Choose teams",
                default_selected: vec!["design".to_string()],
                options: vec![
                    MultiOption::new("design", "Design"),
                    MultiOption::new("eng", "Engineering"),
                    MultiOption::new("ops", "Operations"),
                    MultiOption::new("sales", "Sales"),
                    MultiOption::new("support", "Support"),
                ],
                on_change: move |v| picked.set(v),
            }
            p { style: "margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem;", "Selected: {picked().join(\", \")}" }
        }
    }
}
```

# NumberField

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add number_field` or `dx components add number_field --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `button`, `field`, `form`, `icons`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::number_field::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

`NumberInput` is a number with - and + buttons, for counts and amounts (guests, quantity, nights). `NumberField` is the same control bound to a `use_form` field, with a label, a description and the field's error.

```rust
let mut guests = use_signal(|| 2.0);
rsx! {
    NumberInput { label: "Guests", value: guests(), min: 1.0, max: 8.0, on_value_change: move |v| guests.set(v) }
}

let form = use_form();
let nights = form.field_with("2", vec![required()]);
rsx! { NumberField { field: nights, label: "Nights", min: 1.0, max: 30.0 } }
```

`value` is a plain number (no signal needed); leave it out and use `default_value` for an uncontrolled one. `step` defaults to 1. Typed numbers outside `min`/`max` are pulled back into range when the box loses focus. `NumberField` keeps the number as text in the form field (`"2"`, `"2.5"`), so `field.value().parse()` reads it back.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: the box is `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`; it is named by `label` (or by the visible label in `NumberField`). The buttons are named "Decrease {label}" and "Increase {label}" (`UiStrings::decrease` / `increase`)
- Buttons: left out of the Tab order, as in the WAI-ARIA spin button pattern, and disabled at the ends. Typed text is applied on Enter or when the field loses focus. The keys are in the table below
- Forms: `NumberField` wires `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`, and a failed submit focuses the box
- Reduced motion: nothing animates

## Source

Original to this repo (booking app gap 12). Keyboard behaviour follows the WAI-ARIA APG spin button pattern.

## Stability

Experimental (docs/STABILITY.md): new on 2026-10-15; the `f64` value and the `empty` prop may change once forms need decimals or units.

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Spinbutton](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/spinbutton/) pattern. Roles: `spinbutton`. Works on native (Blitz): partly.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| ArrowUp | In the field | Increases the value by one step. | yes |
| ArrowDown | In the field | Decreases the value by one step. | yes |
| Home | In the field | Sets the minimum. | yes |
| End | In the field | Sets the maximum. | yes |
| PageUp | In the field | Increases the value by ten steps, up to the maximum. | yes |
| PageDown | In the field | Decreases the value by ten steps, down to the minimum. | yes |
| Enter | After typing a number | Applies the typed value. | not yet |

Native: Typing a new value into the field does not apply on Enter yet.

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
/// A number with - and + buttons: a `role="spinbutton"` text box that Up/Down change by
/// `step`, Page Up/Down by ten steps, and Home/End set to `min`/`max`. Typing works too;
/// the value is kept between `min` and `max` when the box loses focus.
///
/// Controlled with `value` + `on_value_change` (a plain number, no signal needed), or
/// uncontrolled with `default_value`. `label` names the buttons ("Increase Guests") and,
/// unless `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or an `id` for a `<label for>` is passed, the box
/// itself. For `use_form`, use [`NumberField`].
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn NumberInput(
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(default)] value: Option<f64>,
    #[props(default)] default_value: f64,
    #[props(default)] min: Option<f64>,
    #[props(default)] max: Option<f64>,
    #[props(default = 1.0)] step: f64,
    #[props(default)] disabled: bool,
    /// Shows an empty box: no number has been entered yet. Typing, a key or a button sets one
    /// (starting from `value`).
    #[props(default)]
    empty: bool,
    #[props(default)] on_value_change: Callback<f64>,
    #[props(default)] onblur: Option<EventHandler<FocusEvent>>,
    #[props(default)] onmounted: Option<EventHandler<MountedEvent>>,
    /// Goes on the text box: `id`, `name`, `aria-*`, `class`, ...
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=input)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element

/// A [`NumberInput`] bound to a `use_form` field, with a visible label, an optional
/// description and the field's error. The field holds the number as text: start it with
/// `form.field_with("2", ..)`, or leave it empty (the box is empty and `required()` applies).
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn NumberField(
    field: FormField,
    #[props(into)] label: String,
    #[props(into, default)] description: Option<String>,
    #[props(default)] min: Option<f64>,
    #[props(default)] max: Option<f64>,
    #[props(default = 1.0)] step: f64,
    #[props(default)] disabled: bool,
    /// Anything else for the text box (`name`, `class`, ...). The field's wiring wins.
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=input)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::form::{required, use_form};
use crate::components::number_field::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut guests = use_signal(|| 2.0);
    let form = use_form();
    let nights = form.field_with("3", vec![required()]);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 2rem; align-items: flex-start;",
            div { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem;",
                span { id: "number-demo-guests", style: "font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500;", "Guests" }
                NumberInput {
                    label: "Guests",
                    "aria-labelledby": "number-demo-guests",
                    value: guests(),
                    min: 1.0,
                    max: 8.0,
                    on_value_change: move |v| guests.set(v),
                }
            }
            NumberField { field: nights, label: "Nights", description: "Between 1 and 30.", min: 1.0, max: 30.0 }
        }
    }
}
```

# Pagination

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add pagination` or `dx components add pagination --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `hooks`, `icons`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::pagination::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The pagination component provides navigational controls for paged content. It exposes a consistent structure for previous/next actions, individual page links, and an optional ellipsis for truncated ranges.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The Pagination component wraps the entire control.
Pagination {
    // PaginationContent groups all items in a horizontal list.
    PaginationContent {
        // PaginationItem is the container for a single pagination element.
        // Use one item at a time and swap the inner component as needed.
        PaginationItem {
            // PaginationPrevious renders a previous-page link.
            // - Set href to your previous page url.
            PaginationPrevious { href: "#" }

            // PaginationLink renders a numbered page link.
            // - is_active marks the current page.
            // - href sets the target page.
            PaginationLink { href: "#", is_active: true, "2" }

            // PaginationEllipsis indicates truncated pages.
            PaginationEllipsis {}

            // PaginationNext renders a next-page link.
            // - Set href to your next page url.
            PaginationNext { href: "#" }
        }
    }
}
```

## Notes

- `PaginationLink` uses `is_active` to indicate the current page.
- `PaginationPrevious` and `PaginationNext` show labels on larger (non-mobile) screens; labels are hidden on smaller screens to keep the control compact.

## API

```rust
pub enum PaginationLinkSize {
    #[default]
    Icon,
    Default,
}

pub enum PaginationLinkKind {
    Previous,
    Next,
}

#[component]
pub fn Pagination(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn PaginationContent(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn PaginationItem(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

pub struct PaginationLinkProps {
    #[props(default)]
    pub is_active: bool,
    #[props(default)]
    pub size: PaginationLinkSize,
    #[props(default)]
    pub data_kind: Option<PaginationLinkKind>,
    onclick: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    onmousedown: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    onmouseup: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends = a)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn PaginationLink(mut props: PaginationLinkProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn PaginationPrevious(
    onclick: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    onmousedown: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    onmouseup: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends = a)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn PaginationNext(
    onclick: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    onmousedown: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    onmouseup: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends = a)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn PaginationEllipsis(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element

/// Client-side paging: Previous, numbered pages and Next as buttons, for a list that pages
/// in place (no URL per page). `page` is 1-based. Previous and Next are `aria-disabled` on
/// the first and last page, so they keep focus but do nothing; long ranges collapse to
/// "1 … 4 5 6 … 20" (`siblings` pages each side of the current one).
///
/// For pages that are URLs, compose [`Pagination`] with [`PaginationLink`] instead.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn Pager(
    page: usize,
    pages: usize,
    on_page_change: EventHandler<usize>,
    #[props(default = 1)] siblings: usize,
    /// Goes on the `<nav>`: give it an `aria-label` ("Pages of results").
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element

/// The page numbers [`Pager`] shows, `None` for a gap: the first and last page, and
/// `siblings` pages each side of `page`. A gap of one page shows that page instead.
pub fn page_items(page: usize, pages: usize, siblings: usize) -> Vec<Option<usize>>
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::pagination::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut page = use_signal(|| 6usize);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1.5rem;",
        Pagination {
            PaginationContent {
                PaginationItem {
                    PaginationPrevious { href: "#" }
                }
                PaginationItem {
                    PaginationLink { href: "#", "1" }
                }
                PaginationItem {
                    PaginationLink { href: "#", is_active: true, "2" }
                }
                PaginationItem {
                    PaginationLink { href: "#", "3" }
                }
                PaginationItem {
                    PaginationEllipsis {}
                }
                PaginationItem {
                    PaginationNext { href: "#" }
                }
            }
        }
        // Client-side paging: buttons, and the ends do nothing on the first and last page.
        Pager {
            aria_label: "Pages of results",
            page: page(),
            pages: 20,
            on_page_change: move |p| page.set(p),
        }
        }
    }
}
```

# Popover

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add popover` or `dx components add popover --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::popover::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Popover primitive provides an interactive modal that is positioned relative to the target element. It can be used to display additional options, or actions related to the trigger.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The PopoverRoot is the root component that contains the trigger and content.
PopoverRoot {
    // The PopoverTrigger contains the elements that will trigger the popover to display when clicked.
    PopoverTrigger {
        "Show Popover"
    }
    // The PopoverContent contains the content that will be displayed when the user clicks on the trigger.
    PopoverContent {
        side: ContentSide::Top,
        align: ContentAlign::Center,
        {children}
    }
}
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

Pattern: Disclosure (non-modal dialog). Roles: `dialog`. Works on native (Blitz): partly.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | On the trigger | Opens the popover. | yes |
| Escape | In the open popover | Closes it and returns focus to the trigger. | not yet |

Native: Closing works, but focus is left on the removed content instead of going back to the trigger.

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn PopoverRoot(props: PopoverRootProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn PopoverTrigger(props: PopoverTriggerProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn PopoverContent(props: PopoverContentProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::popover::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut open = use_signal(|| false);
    rsx! {
        PopoverRoot { open: open(), on_open_change: move |v| open.set(v),
            PopoverTrigger { "Open popover" }
            PopoverContent { gap: "0.5rem",
                strong { "Dimensions" }
                span { style: "font-size: 0.875rem;", "Set the dimensions for the layer." }
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, onclick: move |_| open.set(false), "Done" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Progress

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add progress` or `dx components add progress --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::progress::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Progress component is used to display the progress of a task or operation. It can be used to indicate loading states, file uploads, or any other process that takes time to complete.

## Component Structure

```rust
Progress {
    // The current progress value (0 to max
    value: 0.5,
    // The maximum value of the progress (default is 100.0)
    max: 1.0,
    // Elements that will be displayed inside the progress bar
    {children}
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Progress(props: ProgressProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::*;
use crate::components::progress::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

/// Driven by buttons rather than a JavaScript timer, so it also works on the native renderer.
#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut progress = use_signal(|| 30_u32);

    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 0.75rem; max-width: 20rem;",
            Progress { aria_label: "Upload progress", value: progress() as f64 }
            div { style: "display: flex; gap: 0.5rem;",
                Button {
                    variant: ButtonVariant::Outline,
                    onclick: move |_| progress.set((progress() + 10).min(100)),
                    "Add 10%"
                }
                Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Ghost, onclick: move |_| progress.set(0), "Reset" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Radio group

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add radio_group` or `dx components add radio_group --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::radio_group::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The RadioGroup component is used to create a group of radio buttons that allows the user to select one option from a set.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The RadioGroup component wraps all radio items in the group.
RadioGroup {
    // The value property represents the currently selected radio button in the group.
    value: "option1",
    on_value_change: |value: String| {
        // This callback is triggered when the selected radio button changes.
        // The value parameter contains the value of the newly selected radio button.
    },
    // The RadioItem component represents each individual radio button in the group.
    RadioItem {
        // The index of the radio item, used to determine the order in which items are displayed.
        index: 0,
        // The value of the radio button, which is used to identify the selected option and will be passed to the on_value_change callback when selected.
        value: "option1",
        // The contents of the radio item button
        {children}
    }
}
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Radio Group](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/) pattern. Roles: `radiogroup`, `radio`. Works on native (Blitz): yes.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Space | On a radio | Checks the focused radio. | yes |
| ArrowDown | On a radio | Moves focus to the next radio, skipping disabled ones. | yes |
| ArrowUp | On a radio | Moves focus to the previous radio. | yes |

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn RadioGroup(props: RadioGroupProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn RadioItem(props: RadioItemProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::radio_group::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        RadioGroup { aria_label: "Favourite colour",
            RadioItem { value: "option1".to_string(), index: 0usize, "Blue" }
            RadioItem { value: "option2".to_string(), index: 1usize, "Red" }
            RadioItem { value: "option3".to_string(), index: 2usize, disabled: true, "Green" }
        }
    }
}
```

# Select

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add select` or `dx components add select --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`).
- Import: `use crate::components::select::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Select component is used to create a dropdown menu that allows users to select one or more options from the select groups.

## Component Structure

```rust
Select::<String> {
    selected: "option1".to_string(),
    on_value_change: |value: Option<String>| {
        // Handle the change in selected value.
    },
    SelectGroup {
        SelectGroupLabel { "Group A" }
        SelectOption::<String> {
            index: 0,
            value: "option1",
            "Option 1"
        }
    }
}
```

## Controlled values

`selected` takes a plain value (`selected: filters.read().sort`): the select shows whatever the parent passes on each render, with no signal or `use_memo` adapter. `value` takes a `ReadSignal<Option<T>>` when the state already lives in one (`value: Some(choice.into())`), and `default_value` leaves the select uncontrolled. In forms, `SelectField` binds a `use_form` field instead.

## Labelling

Give every Select a name. `aria_label` or `aria_labelledby` on `Select` (or `SelectMulti`) is moved to the trigger button, and the trigger adds itself to `aria-labelledby`, so screen readers announce the label and the current value ("Fruit, Apple").

```rust
// A visible label.
Label { id: "fruit-label", "Fruit" }
Select::<String> { aria_labelledby: "fruit-label", /* options */ }

// No visible label.
Select::<String> { aria_label: "Fruit", /* options */ }
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Select-Only Combobox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/) pattern. Roles: `listbox`, `option`. Works on native (Blitz): partly.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | On the trigger | Opens the list. | yes |
| Space | On the trigger | Opens the list. | yes |
| ArrowDown | In the open list | Moves focus to the first option, then to the next one, skipping disabled ones. | yes |
| Enter | On an option | Picks the option, closes the list and shows the value on the trigger. | yes |
| Enter | After picking an option | Focus goes back to the trigger. | not yet |
| Escape | In the open list | Closes the list without changing the value. | yes |
| Escape | After the list closes | Focus goes back to the trigger. | not yet |

States:

- `open`: The list of options is shown.
- `closed`: Only the trigger, showing the current value, is shown.

Known gaps:

- The trigger is a button with `aria-haspopup=listbox`, not `role=combobox` as in the APG example.

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
pub use dioxus_primitives::select::SelectGroup;

/// Props for [`Select`]: dioxus-primitives' `SelectProps` plus `selected`, a plain value.
pub struct SelectProps<T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static = String> {
    /// The selected option as a plain value: the select is controlled and shows whatever the
    /// parent passes on each render (`selected: filters.read().sort`), with no signal or memo
    /// needed. Wins over `value`.
    #[props(default, into)]
    pub selected: Option<T>,

    /// The controlled value as a signal; its `None` means no option is selected.
    #[props(default)]
    pub value: Option<ReadSignal<Option<T>>>,

    /// The initial value when uncontrolled. `None` shows the placeholder.
    #[props(default)]
    pub default_value: Option<T>,

    /// Called when the selected value changes.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_value_change: Callback<Option<T>>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// The controlled open state of the list.
    #[props(default)]
    pub open: ReadSignal<Option<bool>>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub default_open: ReadSignal<bool>,

    #[props(default)]
    pub on_open_change: Callback<bool>,

    /// Name for form submission.
    #[props(default)]
    pub name: ReadSignal<String>,

    /// Whether arrow keys wrap around at the ends of the list.
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(true)))]
    pub roving_loop: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// How long typed letters are remembered for typeahead.
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(Duration::from_millis(1000))))]
    pub typeahead_timeout: ReadSignal<Duration>,

    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn Select<T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static>(props: SelectProps<T>) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SelectMulti<T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static>(props: SelectMultiProps<T>) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SelectGroupLabel(props: SelectGroupLabelProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SelectOption<T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static>(props: SelectOptionProps<T>) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::select::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;
use strum::{EnumCount, IntoEnumIterator};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, strum::EnumCount, strum::EnumIter, strum::Display)]
enum Fruit {
    Apple,
    Banana,
    Orange,
    Orangeade,
    Strawberry,
    Watermelon,
}

impl Fruit {
    const fn emoji(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Fruit::Apple => "🍎",
            Fruit::Banana => "🍌",
            Fruit::Orange => "🍊",
            Fruit::Orangeade => "🧃",
            Fruit::Strawberry => "🍓",
            Fruit::Watermelon => "🍉",
        }
    }
}

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let fruits = Fruit::iter().enumerate().map(|(i, f)| {
        rsx! {
            SelectOption::<Option<Fruit>> { index: i, value: f, text_value: "{f}",
                disabled: matches!(f, Fruit::Orange),
                // The emoji is decoration: read "Apple", not "red apple Apple".
                span { "aria-hidden": "true", "{f.emoji()} " }
                "{f}"
            }
        }
    });

    rsx! {
        Select::<Option<Fruit>> {
            width: "12rem",
            aria_label: "Fruit",
            SelectGroup {
                SelectGroupLabel { "Fruits" }
                {fruits}
            }
            SelectGroup {
                SelectGroupLabel { "Other" }
                SelectOption::<Option<Fruit>> {
                    index: Fruit::COUNT,
                    value: None,
                    text_value: "Other",
                    "Other"
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Separator

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add separator` or `dx components add separator --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::separator::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Separator component is a simple horizontal or vertical line that can be used to visually separate content in your application.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The Separator component can be oriented horizontally or vertically.
Separator {
    // The orientation of the separator line. true for horizontal, false for vertical.
    horizontal: true,
    // The decorative property controls if the separator is decorative and should not be visible to screen readers.
    decorative: false,
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Separator(props: SeparatorProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::separator::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "max-width: 20rem;",
            strong { "Rust UI kit" }
            p { style: "margin: 0.25rem 0; font-size: 0.875rem;", "A personal component library." }
            Separator { horizontal: true, decorative: true, style: "margin: 1rem 0;" }
            div { style: "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem; font-size: 0.875rem;", "Docs" Separator { horizontal: false, decorative: true, style: "height: 1rem;" } "Source" }
        }
    }
}
```

# Sheet

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add sheet` or `dx components add sheet --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::sheet::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The sheet component is a panel that slides in from the edge of the screen. It can be used to display additional content, forms, or navigation menus without leaving the current page.

## Component Structure

```rust
Sheet {
    open: open(),
    // Which edge to slide in from. Available sides: Top, Right (default), Bottom, Left.
    "data-side": SheetSide::Right.as_str(),
    // Required: shown in the sheet's header and used as its accessible name.
    // Leaving it out is a compile error.
    title: "Edit Profile",
    description: "Make changes to your profile here.",
    SheetContentClose {}
    SheetFooter {
        SheetClose { "Close" }
    }
}
```

The sheet renders its own header (`title`, then `description`) above the children. `hide_title: true` hides that header visually but keeps it for screen readers, as the mobile sidebar does. For a description with links or formatting, put a `SheetDescription` in the children instead of `description`.

## SheetClose with `as` prop

The `as` prop allows you to render a custom element while preserving the close behavior, similar to shadcn/ui's `asChild` pattern.

```rust
// Default: renders as <button>
SheetClose { "Close" }

// Custom element: attributes include the preset onclick handler
SheetClose {
    as: |attributes| rsx! {
        a { href: "#", ..attributes, "Go back" }
    }
}
```

## API

```rust
pub enum SheetSide {
    Top,
    #[default]
    Right,
    Bottom,
    Left,
}

/// The props for [`Sheet`].
///
/// `title` is required: a sheet is a dialog, and one without a name is announced as just
/// "dialog". Hide it with `hide_title` when the content makes the purpose clear to sighted users.
///
/// ```
/// # use dioxus::prelude::*;
/// # use ui::prelude::*;
/// # fn app() -> Element {
/// rsx! { Sheet { open: true, title: "Rename file", p { "…" } } }
/// # }
/// ```
///
/// Leaving `title` out is a compile error ("Missing required field title"):
///
/// ```compile_fail,E0061
/// # use dioxus::prelude::*;
/// # use ui::prelude::*;
/// # fn app() -> Element {
/// rsx! { Sheet { open: true, p { "…" } } }
/// # }
/// ```
pub struct SheetProps {
    /// The sheet's heading, and its accessible name (`aria-labelledby`). Shown in the header.
    #[props(into)]
    pub title: String,

    /// One line read after the title (`aria-describedby`), shown under it. For richer text, put
    /// a [`SheetDescription`] in the children instead (not both).
    #[props(default, into)]
    pub description: Option<String>,

    /// Hide the header (title and `description`) visually; screen readers still read it.
    #[props(default)]
    pub hide_title: bool,

    /// The ID of the dialog root element.
    pub id: ReadSignal<Option<String>>,

    /// Whether the sheet is modal. If true, it will trap focus within the sheet when open.
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(true)))]
    pub is_modal: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// The controlled `open` state of the sheet.
    pub open: ReadSignal<Option<bool>>,

    /// The default `open` state of the sheet if it is not controlled.
    #[props(default)]
    pub default_open: bool,

    /// Called when the open state changes.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_open_change: Callback<bool>,

    /// Attributes for the sheet panel (`"data-side"` picks the edge).
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The sheet's content, shown below the header.
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn Sheet(props: SheetProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SheetContentClose(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SheetHeader(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SheetFooter(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// A longer description for a [`Sheet`] (links, formatting). For one line of text, use the
/// sheet's `description` prop instead.
#[component]
pub fn SheetDescription(props: DialogDescriptionProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SheetClose(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    r#as: Option<Callback<Vec<Attribute>, Element>>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::input::Input;
use crate::components::label::Label;
use crate::components::sheet::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut open = use_signal(|| false);
    let mut side = use_signal(|| SheetSide::Right);
    let mut show = move |s: SheetSide| {
        side.set(s);
        open.set(true);
    };
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem;",
            Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, onclick: move |_| show(SheetSide::Left), "Left" }
            Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, onclick: move |_| show(SheetSide::Right), "Right" }
            Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, onclick: move |_| show(SheetSide::Top), "Top" }
            Button { variant: ButtonVariant::Outline, onclick: move |_| show(SheetSide::Bottom), "Bottom" }
        }
        Sheet {
            open: open(),
            on_open_change: move |v| open.set(v),
            "data-side": side().as_str(),
            title: "Edit profile",
            description: "Make changes to your profile here.",
            div { style: "display: grid; gap: 0.5rem; max-width: 20rem; padding: 0 1rem;",
                Label { html_for: "sheet-name", "Name" }
                Input { id: "sheet-name", initial_value: "Ferris" }
            }
            SheetFooter {
                Button { onclick: move |_| open.set(false), "Save changes" }
            }
            SheetContentClose {}
        }
    }
}
```

# Shimmer

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add shimmer` or `dx components add shimmer --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::shimmer::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

Wraps loading content and sweeps a highlight across it.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: `aria-busy="true"` while loading.
- Keyboard: none
- Reduced motion: the sweep becomes a static tint

## Source

Structure and API adapted from Rust/UI (`shimmer.rs`, rust-ui/ui commit 43ddc65, MIT); styling rewritten in plain CSS with this kit's tokens. Behaviour and accessibility were reworked here.

## API

```rust
/// Wraps content that is still loading and sweeps a highlight across it. While `loading` is
/// true the wrapper is marked `aria-busy`. Under reduced motion the sweep becomes a static tint.
#[component]
pub fn Shimmer(
    #[props(default = true)] loading: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::shimmer::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut loading = use_signal(|| true);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 0.75rem; max-width: 24rem;",
            Shimmer { loading: loading(),
                div { style: "padding: 1rem;",
                    strong { "Quarterly report" }
                    p { style: "margin: 0.25rem 0 0;", "Revenue is up 12% on the previous quarter." }
                }
            }
            label {
                input {
                    r#type: "checkbox",
                    checked: loading(),
                    onchange: move |e| loading.set(e.checked()),
                }
                " Loading"
            }
        }
    }
}
```
