# Sidebar

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add sidebar` or `dx components add sidebar --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `button`, `icons`, `separator`, `sheet`, `skeleton`, `tooltip`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::sidebar::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Sidebar component is a vertical interface panel fixed to the screen edge, displaying navigation menus or filters that enable quick access to different sections of an application.

## Component Structure

```rust
// Provider: supplies open/side/collapsible signals and ⌘/Ctrl+B toggle
SidebarProvider {
    Sidebar {
        side: SidebarSide::Left,                     // left/right placement
        variant: SidebarVariant::Sidebar,            // chrome: Sidebar | Floating | Inset
        collapsible: SidebarCollapsible::Offcanvas,  // behavior: Offcanvas | Icon | None

        // Layout - Header
        SidebarHeader {
            SidebarTrigger {}                        // toggle button (as)
        }

        // Layout - Scrollable content area
        SidebarContent {
            SidebarGroup {
                SidebarGroupLabel { "..." }          // optional label (as)
                SidebarGroupAction { "..." }         // optional action (as)
                SidebarGroupContent {                // wraps menus
                    SidebarMenu {
                        SidebarMenuItem {
                            SidebarMenuButton {      // primary item (as)
                                is_active: true,     // highlight state
                                tooltip: rsx!("..."),// Option<Element>; wraps tooltip only when Some
                                Icon {}              // icon node
                                span { "..." }       // text node
                            }
                            SidebarMenuAction { show_on_hover: true, Icon {} } // trailing action (as)
                            SidebarMenuBadge { "+..." }                        // optional badge
                        }
                        SidebarMenuItem {            // nested submenu
                            SidebarMenuSub {
                                SidebarMenuSubItem {
                                    SidebarMenuSubButton { "..." } // submenu button/link (as)
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        // Layout -  Footer
        SidebarFooter {
            SidebarMenu { /* ... */ }
        }
    }

    // Optional desktop rail controller placed between rail and content
    SidebarRail {}                               // draggable resize handle

    // Layout - Main content area beside the rail
    SidebarInset { /* ... */ }
}
```

## Behaviors
- Layout: `variant` adjusts chrome (`Floating/Inset` adds padding/radius); `side` selects left/right.
- Collapse: `Offcanvas` hides the rail; `Icon` keeps a thin icon strip and hides labels/actions/badges; `None` is static.
- Keyboard: ⌘/Ctrl+B toggles via provider. Focus rings are defined in `sidebar/style.css`; keep or replace with `:focus-visible` styles.
- Tooltips: `tooltip: Option<Element>` on `SidebarMenuButton`; `None` skips wrapping in Tooltip.
- Landmarks: `Sidebar` is a navigation landmark named "Sidebar" (`UiStrings::sidebar`; pass `aria_label` to rename it, or `role` to change it). `SidebarInset` renders `<main>`, so it is the page's `main` landmark: don't add another `main` inside it.

## Custom Rendering with `as`
Supported components: `SidebarTrigger`, `SidebarGroupLabel`, `SidebarGroupAction`, `SidebarMenuButton`, `SidebarMenuAction`, `SidebarMenuSubButton`. Use `as: |attrs| rsx! { ... }` and spread `..attrs` to retain merged attributes, state data, and handlers.

## API

```rust
pub enum SidebarState {
    #[default]
    Expanded,
    Collapsed,
}

pub enum SidebarSide {
    #[default]
    Left,
    Right,
}

pub enum SidebarVariant {
    #[default]
    Sidebar,
    Floating,
    Inset,
}

pub enum SidebarCollapsible {
    #[default]
    Offcanvas,
    Icon,
    None,
}

pub struct SidebarCtx {
    pub state: Memo<SidebarState>,
    pub side: Signal<SidebarSide>,
    pub is_mobile: Signal<bool>,
    // From use_controlled:
    open: Memo<bool>,
    set_open: Callback<bool>,
    // Mobile state:
    open_mobile: Signal<bool>,
}

pub fn use_sidebar() -> SidebarCtx

pub fn use_is_mobile() -> Signal<bool>

#[component]
pub fn SidebarProvider(
    #[props(default = true)] default_open: bool,
    #[props(default)] open: ReadSignal<Option<bool>>,
    #[props(default)] on_open_change: Callback<bool>,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// The sidebar panel. It is a navigation landmark named [`UiStrings::sidebar`]
/// (`role` and `aria_label` override it); on small screens it becomes a sheet.
///
/// [`UiStrings::sidebar`]: crate::components::ui_strings::UiStrings
#[component]
pub fn Sidebar(
    #[props(default)] side: SidebarSide,
    #[props(default)] variant: SidebarVariant,
    #[props(default)] collapsible: SidebarCollapsible,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarTrigger(
    #[props(default)] onclick: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends = button)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarRail(#[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>) -> Element {
    let ctx = use_sidebar();

/// The page's main content beside the sidebar. It renders `<main>`, so it is the page's
/// `main` landmark: don't put another `main` inside it.
#[component]
pub fn SidebarInset(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarHeader(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarContent(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarFooter(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarSeparator(
    #[props(default = true)] horizontal: bool,
    #[props(default = true)] decorative: bool,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarGroup(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarGroupLabel(
    r#as: Option<Callback<Vec<Attribute>, Element>>,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarGroupAction(
    r#as: Option<Callback<Vec<Attribute>, Element>>,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarGroupContent(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarMenu(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarMenuItem(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

pub enum SidebarMenuButtonVariant {
    #[default]
    Default,
    Outline,
}

pub enum SidebarMenuButtonSize {
    #[default]
    Default,
    Sm,
    Lg,
}

#[component]
pub fn SidebarMenuButton(
    #[props(default = false)] is_active: bool,
    #[props(default)] variant: SidebarMenuButtonVariant,
    #[props(default)] size: SidebarMenuButtonSize,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    #[props(default)] tooltip: Option<Element>,
    /// Click handler for the default `<button>` (ignored when `as` renders something else).
    #[props(default)]
    onclick: Option<EventHandler<MouseEvent>>,
    r#as: Option<Callback<Vec<Attribute>, Element>>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarMenuAction(
    #[props(default = false)] show_on_hover: bool,
    r#as: Option<Callback<Vec<Attribute>, Element>>,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarMenuBadge(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarMenuSkeleton(
    #[props(default = false)] show_icon: bool,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarMenuSub(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn SidebarMenuSubItem(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

pub enum SidebarMenuSubButtonSize {
    Sm,
    #[default]
    Md,
}

#[component]
pub fn SidebarMenuSubButton(
    #[props(default = false)] is_active: bool,
    #[props(default)] size: SidebarMenuSubButtonSize,
    r#as: Option<Callback<Vec<Attribute>, Element>>,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::avatar::{AvatarImageSize, ImageAvatar};
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::collapsible::{Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger};
use crate::components::dropdown_menu::{
    DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuTrigger,
};
use crate::components::icons::{ChevronRight, Circle};
use crate::components::separator::Separator;
use crate::components::sidebar::{
    Sidebar, SidebarCollapsible, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupLabel,
    SidebarHeader, SidebarInset, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuAction, SidebarMenuBadge,
    SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuButtonSize, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuSub,
    SidebarMenuSubButton, SidebarMenuSubItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarRail, SidebarSide,
    SidebarTrigger, SidebarVariant,
};
use crate::components::skeleton::Skeleton;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[css_module("/src/components/sidebar/demo.css")]
struct DemoStyles;

#[css_module("/src/components/sidebar/style.css")]
struct Styles;

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
struct Team {
    name: &'static str,
    plan: &'static str,
}

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
struct NavMainItem {
    title: &'static str,
    url: &'static str,
    is_active: bool,
    items: &'static [SubItem],
}

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
struct SubItem {
    title: &'static str,
    url: &'static str,
}

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
struct Project {
    name: &'static str,
    url: &'static str,
}

const TEAMS: &[Team] = &[
    Team {
        name: "Acme Inc",
        plan: "Enterprise",
    },
    Team {
        name: "Acme Corp.",
        plan: "Startup",
    },
    Team {
        name: "Evil Corp.",
        plan: "Free",
    },
];

const NAV_MAIN: &[NavMainItem] = &[
    NavMainItem {
        title: "Playground",
        url: "#",
        is_active: true,
        items: &[
            SubItem {
                title: "History",
                url: "#",
            },
            SubItem {
                title: "Starred",
                url: "#",
            },
            SubItem {
                title: "Settings",
                url: "#",
            },
        ],
    },
    NavMainItem {
        title: "Models",
        url: "#",
        is_active: false,
        items: &[
            SubItem {
                title: "Genesis",
                url: "#",
            },
            SubItem {
                title: "Explorer",
                url: "#",
            },
            SubItem {
                title: "Quantum",
                url: "#",
            },
        ],
    },
    NavMainItem {
        title: "Documentation",
        url: "#",
        is_active: false,
        items: &[
            SubItem {
                title: "Introduction",
                url: "#",
            },
            SubItem {
                title: "Get Started",
                url: "#",
            },
            SubItem {
                title: "Tutorials",
                url: "#",
            },
            SubItem {
                title: "Changelog",
                url: "#",
            },
        ],
    },
    NavMainItem {
        title: "Settings",
        url: "#",
        is_active: false,
        items: &[
            SubItem {
                title: "General",
                url: "#",
            },
            SubItem {
                title: "Team",
                url: "#",
            },
            SubItem {
                title: "Billing",
                url: "#",
            },
            SubItem {
                title: "Limits",
                url: "#",
            },
        ],
    },
];

const PROJECTS: &[Project] = &[
    Project {
        name: "Design Engineering",
        url: "#",
    },
    Project {
        name: "Sales & Marketing",
        url: "#",
    },
    Project {
        name: "Travel",
        url: "#",
    },
];

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let side = use_signal(|| SidebarSide::Left);
    let collapsible = use_signal(|| SidebarCollapsible::Offcanvas);

    rsx! {
        SidebarProvider {
            Sidebar {
                variant: SidebarVariant::Sidebar,
                collapsible: collapsible(),
                side: side(),
                SidebarHeader {
                    TeamSwitcher { teams: TEAMS }
                }
                SidebarContent {
                    NavMain { items: NAV_MAIN }
                    NavProjects { projects: PROJECTS }
                }
                SidebarFooter { NavUser {} }
                SidebarRail {}
            }
            SidebarInset {
                header { style: "display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; height:3.5rem; flex-shrink:0; padding:0 1rem; border-bottom:1px solid var(--dx-sidebar-border); background:var(--primary-color-1);",
                    div { style: "display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem;",
                        SidebarTrigger {}
                        Separator { height: "1rem", horizontal: false }
                        span { "Sidebar Setting" }
                    }
                }
                div { style: "display:flex; flex:1; flex-direction:column; gap:1.5rem; padding:1.5rem; min-height:0; overflow-y:auto; overflow-x:hidden;",
                    DemoSettingControls { side, collapsible }
                    Skeleton { style: "height: 10rem; width: 100%; flex-shrink:0;" }
                    Skeleton { style: "height: 20rem; width: 100%; flex-shrink:0;" }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

#[component]
fn TeamSwitcher(teams: &'static [Team]) -> Element {
    let mut active_team = use_signal(|| 0usize);

    rsx! {
        SidebarMenu {
            SidebarMenuItem {
                DropdownMenu { class: Styles::dx_sidebar_dropdown_menu,
                    DropdownMenuTrigger { class: Styles::dx_sidebar_dropdown_menu_trigger,
                        as: move |attributes: Vec<Attribute>| rsx! {
                            SidebarMenuButton { class: DemoStyles::dx_sidebar_menu_disclosure_button, size: SidebarMenuButtonSize::Lg, attributes,
                                div { style: "display:flex; flex-shrink:0; align-items:center; justify-content:center; width:2rem; height:2rem; aspect-ratio:1; border-radius:0.5rem; background:var(--dx-sidebar-accent); color:var(--dx-sidebar-accent-foreground);",
                                    DemoIcon {}
                                }
                                div { class: DemoStyles::dx_sidebar_info_block,
                                    span { class: DemoStyles::dx_sidebar_info_title, {teams[active_team()].name} }
                                    span { class: DemoStyles::dx_sidebar_info_subtitle, {teams[active_team()].plan} }
                                }
                                ChevronIcon {}
                            }
                        },
                    }
                    DropdownMenuContent { class: Styles::dx_sidebar_dropdown_menu_content,
                        div { style: "padding:0.5rem; font-size:0.75rem; opacity:0.7;",
                            "Teams"
                        }
                        for (idx , team) in teams.iter().enumerate() {
                            DropdownMenuItem {
                                index: idx,
                                value: idx,
                                on_select: move |v: usize| active_team.set(v),
                                DemoIcon {}
                                {team.name}
                                span { style: "margin-left:auto; font-size:0.75rem; opacity:0.7;",
                                    "⌘{idx + 1}"
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        Separator { class: Styles::dx_sidebar_dropdown_separator, decorative: true }
                        DropdownMenuItem {
                            index: teams.len(),
                            value: 999usize,
                            on_select: move |_: usize| {},
                            DemoIcon {}
                            div { style: "opacity:0.7; font-weight:500;", "Add team" }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

#[component]
fn NavMain(items: &'static [NavMainItem]) -> Element {
    rsx! {
        SidebarGroup {
            SidebarGroupLabel { "Platform" }
            SidebarMenu {
                for item in items.iter() {
                    Collapsible {
                        default_open: item.is_active,
                        as: move |attributes: Vec<Attribute>| rsx! {
                            SidebarMenuItem { key: "{item.title}", attributes,
                                CollapsibleTrigger { class: Styles::dx_sidebar_collapsible_trigger,
                                    as: move |attributes: Vec<Attribute>| rsx! {
                                        SidebarMenuButton {
                                            class: DemoStyles::dx_sidebar_menu_disclosure_button,
                                            tooltip: rsx! {
                                                {item.title}
                                            },
                                            attributes,
                                            DemoIcon {}
                                            span { {item.title} }
                                            ChevronIcon {}
                                        }
                                    },
                                }
                                CollapsibleContent {
                                    SidebarMenuSub {
                                        for sub_item in item.items {
                                            SidebarMenuSubItem { key: "{sub_item.title}",
                                                SidebarMenuSubButton {
                                                    as: move |attributes: Vec<Attribute>| rsx! {
                                                        a { href: sub_item.url, ..attributes,
                                                            span { {sub_item.title} }
                                                        }
                                                    },
                                                }
                                            }
                                        }
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                        },
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

#[component]
fn DemoSettingControls(
    side: Signal<SidebarSide>,
    collapsible: Signal<SidebarCollapsible>,
) -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.75rem; padding: 0.75rem; border: 1px solid var(--dx-sidebar-border); border-radius: 0.75rem; background: var(--primary-color-2);",
            div { style: "display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 0.75rem; flex-wrap: wrap;",
                span { style: "font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--secondary-color-4);",
                    "Side"
                }
                div { style: "display: inline-flex; gap: 0.5rem;",
                    Button {
                        variant: if side() == SidebarSide::Left { ButtonVariant::Primary } else { ButtonVariant::Outline },
                        onclick: move |_| side.set(SidebarSide::Left),
                        style: "padding: 0.4rem 0.6rem; font-size: 0.75rem;",
                        "Left"
                    }
                    Button {
                        variant: if side() == SidebarSide::Right { ButtonVariant::Primary } else { ButtonVariant::Outline },
                        onclick: move |_| side.set(SidebarSide::Right),
                        style: "padding: 0.4rem 0.6rem; font-size: 0.75rem;",
                        "Right"
                    }
                }
            }
            div { style: "display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 0.75rem; flex-wrap: wrap;",
                span { style: "font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--secondary-color-4);",
                    "Collapse"
                }
                div { style: "display: inline-flex; gap: 0.5rem; flex-wrap: wrap;",
                    Button {
                        variant: if collapsible() == SidebarCollapsible::Offcanvas { ButtonVariant::Primary } else { ButtonVariant::Outline },
                        onclick: move |_| collapsible.set(SidebarCollapsible::Offcanvas),
                        style: "padding: 0.4rem 0.6rem; font-size: 0.75rem;",
                        "Offcanvas"
                    }
                    Button {
                        variant: if collapsible() == SidebarCollapsible::Icon { ButtonVariant::Primary } else { ButtonVariant::Outline },
                        onclick: move |_| collapsible.set(SidebarCollapsible::Icon),
                        style: "padding: 0.4rem 0.6rem; font-size: 0.75rem;",
                        "Icon"
                    }
                    Button {
                        variant: if collapsible() == SidebarCollapsible::None { ButtonVariant::Primary } else { ButtonVariant::Outline },
                        onclick: move |_| collapsible.set(SidebarCollapsible::None),
                        style: "padding: 0.4rem 0.6rem; font-size: 0.75rem;",
                        "None"
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

        }
    }
}

# Skeleton

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add skeleton` or `dx components add skeleton --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::skeleton::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Skeleton component is used to display a placeholder preview of content before the data gets loaded. This helps improve perceived performance and provides users with a visual indication that content is being loaded.

## Component Structure

```rust
Skeleton {
    // Accepts all GlobalAttributes, commonly used with style for sizing
    style: "width: 15rem; height: 1rem;",
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Skeleton(#[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>) -> Element {
    let base = attributes!(div
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::skeleton::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 2rem;",
            SkeletonInfoDemo {}
            SkeletonCardDemo {}
        }
    }
}

#[component]
fn SkeletonInfoDemo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1rem;",
            Skeleton { style: "width: 3rem; height: 3rem; border-radius: 50%;" }
            div { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem;",
                Skeleton { style: "width: 11.625rem; height: 1rem;" }
                Skeleton { style: "width: 8.5rem; height: 1rem;" }
            }
        }
    }
}

#[component]
fn SkeletonCardDemo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.75rem;",
            Skeleton { style: "width: 15rem; height: 8rem; border-radius: 0.75rem;" }
            div { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem;",
                Skeleton { style: "width: 15.625rem; height: 1rem;" }
                Skeleton { style: "width: 12.5rem; height: 1rem;" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# SkipLink

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add skip_link` or `dx components add skip_link --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::skip_link::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

`SkipLink` is a "Skip to content" link that stays hidden until it has keyboard focus, then appears in the corner, so keyboard users can jump past the header and navigation. `MainContent` is the page's `<main>` landmark it points at.

```rust
rsx! {
    SkipLink {}
    header { /* logo, nav */ }
    MainContent { Outlet::<Route> {} }
}
```

`SkipLink` points at `#main-content` by default (`target` changes it) and reads `UiStrings::skip_to_content` unless it has children. It is positioned against the nearest positioned ancestor, usually the page. `MainContent` renders `main id="main-content" tabindex="-1"`, so following the skip link moves focus into it.

With the kit's `router` feature, `MainContent` inside a `Router` also takes focus after every in-app navigation (not on the first load). Keyboard and screen reader users then start at the new page, and a screen reader reads the main landmark, instead of staying on the link they used. Set the page's title (`document::Title`) and give each page a heading.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: `SkipLink` is a native link named by its text; `MainContent` is the `main` landmark
- Keyboard: the skip link is the first Tab stop; Enter moves focus to the main content
- Focus: shown with the kit's focus ring when focused; `MainContent` shows no ring, since it is not a control
- Reduced motion: nothing animates

## Source

Original to this repo (booking app gaps 11 and 21).

## Stability

`SkipLink` and `MainContent` are stable; the focus move after a route change (the `router` feature) is experimental (docs/STABILITY.md).

## API

```rust
/// The id [`SkipLink`] points at and [`MainContent`] carries unless told otherwise.
pub const MAIN_CONTENT_ID: &str;

/// A "Skip to content" link for keyboard users: hidden until it has focus, then shown at
/// the top corner of the nearest positioned ancestor. Put it first in the page, before the
/// header and navigation, and point it at the page's [`MainContent`].
#[component]
pub fn SkipLink(
    /// The id of the element to skip to, without `#`.
    #[props(into, default = MAIN_CONTENT_ID.to_string())]
    target: String,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    /// The link text. Defaults to `UiStrings::skip_to_content`.
    children: Option<Element>,
) -> Element

/// The page's `<main>` landmark: the target of [`SkipLink`] (`id="main-content"`,
/// focusable from script with `tabindex="-1"`).
///
/// With the kit's `router` feature, inside a `Router`, it also takes focus after an in-app
/// navigation (not on the first load), so keyboard and screen reader users start at the new
/// page instead of on the link they used. Give the page a heading inside it.
#[component]
pub fn MainContent(
    #[props(into, default = MAIN_CONTENT_ID.to_string())] id: String,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::skip_link::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; padding-top: 2.75rem;",
            SkipLink { target: "skip-link-demo-main" }
            p { style: "margin: 0;", "Tab into this demo: the skip link appears above, and Enter jumps past the links below." }
            nav { "aria-label": "Skip link demo",
                a { href: "#skip-link", "One" }
                " · "
                a { href: "#skip-link", "Two" }
            }
            // A page has one `MainContent` (`<main>`); the gallery already has its own, so the
            // demo skips to a plain focusable block.
            div { id: "skip-link-demo-main", tabindex: "-1", style: "outline: none;",
                p { style: "margin: 0;", "The main content." }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

---

# Slider

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add slider` or `dx components add slider --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::slider::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The slider component allows users to select a value from a range by sliding a handle along a track.

## Component Structure

```rust
Slider {
    value: 0.0,
    horizontal: true,
    on_value_change: |value: f64| {
        // Handle the change in slider value.
    },
}
```

For a two-thumb range selector, use `RangeSlider`:

```rust
RangeSlider {
    default_value: 20.0..80.0,
    on_value_change: |value: std::ops::Range<f64>| {
        // value.start and value.end give the two endpoints
    },
}
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Slider](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/slider/) pattern. Roles: `slider`. Works on native (Blitz): yes.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| ArrowRight | On the thumb | Increases the value by one step. | yes |
| ArrowLeft | On the thumb | Decreases the value by one step. | yes |
| Home | On the thumb | Sets the minimum. | yes |
| End | On the thumb | Sets the maximum. | yes |

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Slider(props: SliderProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn RangeSlider(props: RangeSliderProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::slider::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut current_value = use_signal(|| 50.0);

    rsx! {
        div {
            display: "flex",
            flex_direction: "column",
            align_items: "center",

            // Display the current value
            div { style: "margin-bottom: 15px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: bold;", "{current_value:.0}%" }

            Slider {
                label: "Volume",
                horizontal: true,
                min: 0.0,
                max: 100.0,
                step: 1.0,
                default_value: 50.0,
                on_value_change: move |value: f64| {
                    current_value.set(value);
                },
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Spinner

A loading indicator.

## Accessibility

- Reduced motion: the spin slows to 3s instead of stopping, so it still shows that work is happening

# Status

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add status` or `dx components add status --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::status::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A coloured dot plus required text label (idle, online, degraded, down). Optional `pulse`.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: The dot is `aria-hidden`; the label carries the meaning, never colour alone.
- Keyboard: none
- Reduced motion: the pulse ring is removed

## Source

Structure and API adapted from Rust/UI (`status.rs`, rust-ui/ui commit 43ddc65, MIT); styling rewritten in plain CSS with this kit's tokens. Behaviour and accessibility were reworked here.

## API

```rust
pub enum StatusKind {
    #[default]
    Neutral,
    Active,
    Warning,
    Error,
    Info,
}

/// A coloured dot with a text label. The label is required: colour alone never carries the
/// meaning. `pulse` adds a soft ring animation (off under reduced motion).
#[component]
pub fn Status(
    #[props(default)] kind: StatusKind,
    #[props(default)] pulse: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::status::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1.25rem;",
            Status { "Idle" }
            Status { kind: StatusKind::Active, pulse: true, "Online" }
            Status { kind: StatusKind::Warning, "Degraded" }
            Status { kind: StatusKind::Error, "Down" }
            Status { kind: StatusKind::Info, "Deploying" }
        }
    }
}
```

# Stepper

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add stepper` or `dx components add stepper --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::stepper::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A multi-step progress indicator with Back/Next control via `use_stepper()`.

To move on only when something allows it (a step's form validates), own the step: pass `current: step` (a `Signal<usize>`) and set it yourself; the step panels can then live outside the stepper. Disable the items the user hasn't reached so they can't skip ahead:

```rust
let step = use_signal(|| 0usize);
rsx! {
    Stepper { total: 3, current: step,
        StepperItem { step: 0usize, title: "Trip" }
        StepperItem { step: 1usize, title: "Details", disabled: reached() < 1 }
        StepperItem { step: 2usize, title: "Payment", disabled: reached() < 2 }
    }
    match step() { /* the current step's form */ }
}
```

## Accessibility

- Role and name: An ordered list; the current step has `aria-current="step"`; completed steps add hidden "(completed)" text.
- Keyboard: each step is a button (Tab/Enter/Space); `disabled` steps are skipped
- Reduced motion: none

## Source

Structure and API adapted from Rust/UI (`stepper.rs`, rust-ui/ui commit 43ddc65, MIT); styling rewritten in plain CSS with this kit's tokens. Behaviour and accessibility were reworked here.

## API

```rust
/// Shared state of a [`Stepper`]. Get it with [`use_stepper`] inside the stepper to build
/// Back/Next buttons.
pub struct StepperContext {
    pub current: Signal<usize>,
    pub total: usize,
}

/// The stepper context. Call inside a [`Stepper`].
pub fn use_stepper() -> StepperContext

/// A multi-step progress indicator. Steps are an ordered list; the current one carries
/// `aria-current="step"`. Put [`StepperItem`]s inside, one per step.
#[component]
pub fn Stepper(
    /// Number of steps.
    total: usize,
    #[props(default = 0)] default_step: usize,
    /// Drive the step from outside (for example, move on only after a form validates). When
    /// given, `default_step` is ignored and the stepper reads and writes this signal.
    #[props(default)]
    current: Option<Signal<usize>>,
    #[props(default)] vertical: bool,
    /// Called with the new index whenever the step changes.
    #[props(default)]
    on_change: Callback<usize>,
    /// Rendered after the list, inside the stepper, so it can call [`use_stepper`]
    /// (for example Back/Next buttons).
    #[props(default)]
    footer: Option<Element>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// One step. Clicking its button jumps there unless `disabled`.
#[component]
pub fn StepperItem(
    /// Zero-based index of this step.
    step: usize,
    #[props(into)] title: String,
    #[props(into, default)] description: Option<String>,
    #[props(default)] disabled: bool,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::stepper::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 1.25rem; max-width: 36rem;",
            Stepper { total: 3, default_step: 1, "aria-label": "Checkout progress", footer: rsx! { StepperControls {} },
                StepperItem { step: 0, title: "Account", description: "Your details" }
                StepperItem { step: 1, title: "Shipping", description: "Where to send it" }
                StepperItem { step: 2, title: "Payment" }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Back/Next buttons driven by the stepper context.
#[component]
fn StepperControls() -> Element {
    let ctx = use_stepper();
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; gap: 0.5rem;",
            Button {
                variant: ButtonVariant::Outline,
                disabled: !ctx.can_prev(),
                onclick: move |_| ctx.prev(),
                "Back"
            }
            Button { disabled: !ctx.can_next(), onclick: move |_| ctx.next(), "Next" }
        }
    }
}
```

# Switch

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add switch` or `dx components add switch --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::switch::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Switch component allows users to toggle between two states, such as on and off.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The Switch component includes the switch thumb.
Switch {
    // The current state of the switch, true for on and false for off.
    checked: true,
    // Callback function triggered when the switch state changes.
    on_checked_change: |checked: bool| {
        // Handle the change in switch state.
    }
}
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Switch](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/switch/) pattern. Roles: `switch`. Works on native (Blitz): yes.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Space | On the switch | Turns it on or off. | yes |

Known gaps:

- Enter does not toggle it (optional in the APG); Space does.

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Switch(props: SwitchProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::switch::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut on = use_signal(|| false);
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem;",
            Switch {
                checked: on(),
                aria_label: "Airplane mode",
                on_checked_change: move |v| on.set(v),
            }
            span { style: "font-size: 0.875rem;", if on() { "On" } else { "Off" } }
        }
    }
}
```

# Table

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add table` or `dx components add table --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::table::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A styled table. Give a `TableHead` an `on_sort` to make it a sort button; see `DataTable` for filtering, paging and selection.

Mark number columns `numeric: true` on both the `TableHead` and its `TableCell`s: they align to the end with tabular figures, and a sortable numeric header puts its arrow before the text so the text lines up with the figures below.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: native table semantics; sortable headers are buttons with `aria-sort`
- Keyboard: sort buttons are tabbable and activate with Enter or Space
- Reduced motion: none

## API

```rust
/// A scrollable wrapper around a native `<table>`, so wide tables don't break the page.
#[component]
pub fn Table(
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// A body cell. `numeric` aligns it to the end with tabular figures, to match a
/// `numeric` [`TableHead`].
#[component]
pub fn TableCell(
    #[props(default)] numeric: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes, extends=td)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// The direction a column is sorted in.
pub enum SortDirection {
    #[default]
    None,
    Ascending,
    Descending,
}

/// A column header. Pass `on_sort` to make it a sort button (with `aria-sort`). `numeric`
/// aligns it to the end, with the sort arrow before the text so the text lines up with
/// the `numeric` cells below.
#[component]
pub fn TableHead(
    #[props(default)] sort: SortDirection,
    #[props(default)] on_sort: Option<EventHandler<()>>,
    #[props(default)] numeric: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::badge::{Badge, BadgeVariant};
use crate::components::table::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
struct Invoice {
    id: &'static str,
    status: &'static str,
    method: &'static str,
    cents: u32,
}

const INVOICES: &[Invoice] = &[
    Invoice {
        id: "INV-001",
        status: "Paid",
        method: "Card",
        cents: 25_000,
    },
    Invoice {
        id: "INV-002",
        status: "Pending",
        method: "Bank",
        cents: 15_050,
    },
    Invoice {
        id: "INV-003",
        status: "Unpaid",
        method: "Card",
        cents: 35_000,
    },
    Invoice {
        id: "INV-004",
        status: "Paid",
        method: "Bank",
        cents: 45_075,
    },
];

#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq)]
enum Column {
    Id,
    Status,
    Amount,
}

/// Sort `rows` by `column`. Stable, so equal rows keep their original order.
fn sorted(column: Column, direction: SortDirection) -> Vec<Invoice> {
    let mut rows = INVOICES.to_vec();
    match (column, direction) {
        (_, SortDirection::None) => {}
        (Column::Id, d) => rows.sort_by(|a, b| apply(d, a.id.cmp(b.id))),
        (Column::Status, d) => rows.sort_by(|a, b| apply(d, a.status.cmp(b.status))),
        (Column::Amount, d) => rows.sort_by(|a, b| apply(d, a.cents.cmp(&b.cents))),
    }
    rows
}

fn apply(direction: SortDirection, ordering: std::cmp::Ordering) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
    match direction {
        SortDirection::Descending => ordering.reverse(),
        _ => ordering,
    }
}

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let sort = use_signal(|| (Column::Id, SortDirection::None));
    let (column, direction) = sort();
    let rows = sorted(column, direction);
    let total: u32 = rows.iter().map(|r| r.cents).sum();

    rsx! {
        Table {
            TableCaption { "A list of recent invoices." }
            TableHeader {
                TableRow {
                    SortableHead { label: "Invoice", column: Column::Id, sort }
                    SortableHead { label: "Status", column: Column::Status, sort }
                    TableHead { "Method" }
                    SortableHead {
                        label: "Amount",
                        column: Column::Amount,
                        sort,
                        numeric: true,
                    }
                }
            }
            TableBody {
                for row in rows {
                    TableRow { key: "{row.id}",
                        TableCell { style: "font-weight: 500;", "{row.id}" }
                        TableCell {
                            Badge {
                                variant: if row.status == "Paid" { BadgeVariant::Primary } else { BadgeVariant::Outline },
                                "{row.status}"
                            }
                        }
                        TableCell { "{row.method}" }
                        TableCell { numeric: true, "{money(row.cents)}" }
                    }
                }
            }
            TableFooter {
                TableRow {
                    TableCell { colspan: "3", "Total" }
                    TableCell { numeric: true, "{money(total)}" }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

#[component]
fn SortableHead(
    label: &'static str,
    column: Column,
    sort: Signal<(Column, SortDirection)>,
    #[props(default)] numeric: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element {
    let (current, direction) = sort();
    let shown = if current == column {
        direction
    } else {
        SortDirection::None
    };
    let mut sort = sort;
    rsx! {
        TableHead {
            sort: shown,
            numeric,
            on_sort: move |_| {
                let next = if current == column { direction.cycle() } else { SortDirection::Ascending };
                sort.set((column, next));
            },
            attributes,
            "{label}"
        }
    }
}

fn money(cents: u32) -> String {
    format!("${}.{:02}", cents / 100, cents % 100)
}
```

---

# Tabs

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add tabs` or `dx components add tabs --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::tabs::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Tabs component is used to create a tabbed interface, allowing users to switch between different views or sections of content.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The Tabs component wraps all tab triggers and contents and orders them based on their index.
Tabs {
    // The TabList component contains all the tab triggers
    TabList {
        // The TabTrigger component is used to create a clickable tab button that switches the active tab.
        TabTrigger {
            // The index of the tab trigger, used to determine the focus order of the tabs.
            index: 0,
            // The value of the tab trigger, which must be unique and is used to identify the active tab.
            value: "tab1",
            // The contents of the tab trigger button
            {children}
        }
    }
    // The TabContent component contains the content that is displayed when the corresponding tab is active.
    TabContent {
        // The index of the tab content, used to determine the focus order of the tabs.
        index: 0,
        // The value of the tab content, which must match the value of the corresponding TabTrigger to be displayed.
        value: "tab1",
        // The content of the tab, which is displayed when the tab is active.
        {children}
    }
}
```

## Accessibility

Each `TabContent` is labelled by the `TabTrigger` with the same `index` (`aria-labelledby`). If you give a `TabTrigger` your own `id`, set `aria_labelledby` to that id on its `TabContent`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Tabs](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/) pattern. Roles: `tablist`, `tab`, `tabpanel`. Works on native (Blitz): partly.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tab | On a tab | Leaves the tab list and moves focus to the shown panel. | not yet |
| ArrowRight | On a tab | Moves focus to the next tab without selecting it (manual activation). | yes |
| ArrowLeft | On a tab | Moves focus to the previous tab. | yes |
| Enter | On a tab | Selects the focused tab and shows its panel. | yes |
| Space | On a tab | Selects the focused tab and shows its panel. | yes |
| Home | On a tab | Moves focus to the first tab. | yes |
| End | On a tab | Moves focus to the last tab. | yes |

States:

- `first-selected`: The first tab is selected and its panel is shown.
- `second-selected`: The second tab is selected and its panel is shown.

Native: Tab moves to the next tab instead of leaving the tab list for the panel.

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
/// The props for the [`Tabs`] component.
pub struct TabsProps {
    /// The class of the tabs component.
    #[props(default)]
    pub class: String,

    /// The controlled value of the active tab.
    pub value: ReadSignal<Option<String>>,

    /// The default active tab value when uncontrolled.
    #[props(default)]
    pub default_value: String,

    /// Callback fired when the active tab changes.
    #[props(default)]
    pub on_value_change: Callback<String>,

    /// Whether the tabs are disabled.
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// Whether the tabs are horizontal.
    #[props(default)]
    pub horizontal: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// Whether focus should loop around when reaching the end.
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(true)))]
    pub roving_loop: ReadSignal<bool>,

    /// The variant of the tabs component.
    #[props(default)]
    pub variant: TabsVariant,

    /// Additional attributes to apply to the tabs element.
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,

    /// The children of the tabs component.
    pub children: Element,
}

/// The variant of the tabs component.
pub enum TabsVariant {
    /// The default variant.
    #[default]
    Default,
    /// The ghost variant.
    Ghost,
}

#[component]
pub fn Tabs(props: TabsProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn TabList(props: TabListProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn TabTrigger(props: TabTriggerProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn TabContent(props: TabContentProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::tabs::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        Tabs { default_value: "account".to_string(), horizontal: true, max_width: "24rem",
            TabList {
                TabTrigger { value: "account".to_string(), index: 0usize, "Account" }
                TabTrigger { value: "password".to_string(), index: 1usize, "Password" }
            }
            TabContent { index: 0usize, value: "account".to_string(),
                p { "Make changes to your account here." }
            }
            TabContent { index: 1usize, value: "password".to_string(),
                p { "Change your password here." }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Tag group

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add tag_group` or `dx components add tag_group --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `icons`).
- Import: `use crate::components::tag_group::*;` after copying, or `use ui::components::tag_group::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A Tag Group is a focusable group of tags (labels, categories, filters and similar items) with keyboard navigation, optional selection and removal.

## Structure

Single selection with [`TagGroup`](component.rs):

```rust
TagGroup {
    value: Some(value.into()),
    on_value_change: move |value| { /* ... */ },
    TagGroupLabel { "Labels" }
    TagList {
        TagGroupEmpty { "No tags" }
        Tag { index: 0usize, value: "bug", "bug" RemoveButton {} }
        Tag { index: 1usize, value: "feature", disabled: true, "feature" }
    }
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn TagGroup(props: TagGroupProps<String>) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn TagGroupMulti(props: TagGroupMultiProps<String>) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn TagGroupLabel(props: TagGroupLabelProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn TagGroupEmpty(props: TagGroupEmptyProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn TagList(props: TagListProps) -> Element

pub struct TagProps {
    pub value: ReadSignal<String>,
    #[props(default)]
    pub text_value: ReadSignal<Option<String>>,
    pub index: ReadSignal<usize>,
    #[props(default)]
    pub id: ReadSignal<Option<String>>,
    #[props(default)]
    pub disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    pub attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn Tag(props: TagProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn RemoveButton(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use dioxus::prelude::*;

use crate::components::tag_group::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let labels = ["bug", "feature", "core", "desktop", "example", "duplicate"];
    let tags = labels.iter().enumerate().map(|(index, &t)| {
        rsx! {
            Tag {
                index,
                value: t,
                "{t}"
                RemoveButton {}
            }
        }
    });

    let mut value = use_signal(|| Some("core".to_string()));

    rsx! {
        TagGroup {
            value: Some(value.into()),
            on_value_change: move |v| value.set(v),
            allow_empty_selection: false,
            TagGroupLabel { "Labels" }
            TagList {
                TagGroupEmpty { "No tags" }
                {tags}
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Textarea

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add textarea` or `dx components add textarea --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::textarea::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The textarea element is used to allow users to enter multi-line text input in a user interface.

## Component Structure

```rust
textarea {
    // Global html attributes
    class: "dx-textarea",
    "data-style": "default",
    // Children
    {children}
}
```

## API

```rust
pub enum TextareaVariant {
    #[default]
    Default,
    Fade,
    Outline,
    Ghost,
}

#[component]
pub fn Textarea(
    oninput: Option<EventHandler<FormEvent>>,
    onchange: Option<EventHandler<FormEvent>>,
    oninvalid: Option<EventHandler<FormEvent>>,
    onselect: Option<EventHandler<SelectionEvent>>,
    onselectionchange: Option<EventHandler<SelectionEvent>>,
    onfocus: Option<EventHandler<FocusEvent>>,
    onblur: Option<EventHandler<FocusEvent>>,
    onfocusin: Option<EventHandler<FocusEvent>>,
    onfocusout: Option<EventHandler<FocusEvent>>,
    onkeydown: Option<EventHandler<KeyboardEvent>>,
    onkeypress: Option<EventHandler<KeyboardEvent>>,
    onkeyup: Option<EventHandler<KeyboardEvent>>,
    oncompositionstart: Option<EventHandler<CompositionEvent>>,
    oncompositionupdate: Option<EventHandler<CompositionEvent>>,
    oncompositionend: Option<EventHandler<CompositionEvent>>,
    oncopy: Option<EventHandler<ClipboardEvent>>,
    oncut: Option<EventHandler<ClipboardEvent>>,
    onpaste: Option<EventHandler<ClipboardEvent>>,
    onmounted: Option<EventHandler<MountedEvent>>,
    #[props(default)] variant: TextareaVariant,
    /// Grow with the text instead of scrolling, up to `--textarea-max-height` (CSS
    /// `field-sizing: content`, no JavaScript). Browsers without it keep a fixed height.
    #[props(default)]
    autosize: bool,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends=textarea)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::label::Label;
use crate::components::textarea::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut description = use_signal(|| "sample text".to_string());
    rsx! {
        div {
            display: "flex",
            flex_direction: "column",
            gap: "1.5rem",

            p { id: "textarea-message", "Description here: {description}" }

            div {
                display: "flex",
                flex_direction: "column",
                gap: ".5rem",
                justify_content: "center",

                Label { html_for: "default", "Default" }
                Textarea {
                    id: "default",
                    variant: TextareaVariant::Default,
                    placeholder: "Enter your description",
                    value: description,
                    oninput: move |e: FormEvent| description.set(e.value()),
                }
            }

            div {
                display: "flex",
                flex_direction: "column",
                gap: ".5rem",

                Label { html_for: "autosize", "Grows as you type" }
                Textarea {
                    id: "autosize",
                    autosize: true,
                    placeholder: "Write a few lines",
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# ThemeCustomizer

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add theme_customizer` or `dx components add theme_customizer --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `hooks`).
- Import: `use crate::components::theme_customizer::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

Pick an accent colour, corner radius and light/dark mode for the whole page. It only writes `data-accent`, `data-theme` and `--radius` on `<html>`, so you can drive the same attributes from your own settings.

## One theme state: `use_theme()`

The customizer's choices live in one shared state. Read and change it from app code with `use_theme()`, so a header switch and the customizer never disagree:

```rust
let theme = use_theme();
rsx! {
    Switch {
        checked: theme.is_dark(),
        aria_label: "Dark mode",
        on_checked_change: move |dark| theme.set_mode(if dark { ThemeMode::Dark } else { ThemeMode::Light }),
    }
}
```

`mode()` / `set_mode(ThemeMode::System | Light | Dark)`, `is_dark()` (follows the OS in `System` mode, on the web), `accent()` / `set_accent(name)` (one of `ACCENTS`), `density()` / `set_density(name)` (one of `DENSITIES`) and `radius()` / `set_radius(px)`. Don't write `data-theme` yourself as well; that is the second source of truth this replaces.

## Native (no JavaScript)

dioxus-native can't run the script that writes to `<html>`. Wrap the app in `ThemeScope { ... }` there: it applies the same choices to everything inside it, and doesn't change layout (`display: contents`). On the web and desktop it is harmless.

## Theming without the component

- `data-accent="blue|green|violet|rose|orange"` on `<html>` recolors primary buttons, checked checkboxes/switches/radios, slider and progress fills and the focus ring. Remove it for the neutral default.
- For a brand colour set `--accent-color` and `--accent-contrast` yourself (keep text on the fill at 4.5:1 or better).
- `--radius` (default `0.5rem`) scales the corners of controls.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: native radio inputs grouped in `fieldset`/`legend`; the radius slider is a native range input with a label.
- Keyboard: arrow keys move within a group, Tab between groups (native behaviour).
- Reduced motion: no animation.

## Source

Original to this repo.

## Stability

`ACCENTS`, `DENSITIES` and the attributes and tokens the customizer writes are stable. `use_theme`, `Theme`, `ThemeMode`, `ThemeScope` and the customizer's own markup are experimental and may change in any release; see `docs/STABILITY.md` in the kit repository.

## API

```rust
/// Accent presets defined in `theme.css` (`[data-accent=...]`). `neutral` is the default.
pub const ACCENTS: [&str; 6];

/// Light or dark, or whatever the operating system prefers.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub enum ThemeMode {
    #[default]
    System,
    Light,
    Dark,
}

/// The page's theme: mode, accent, density and corner radius. One shared state, so a
/// header switch, a settings screen and [`ThemeCustomizer`] always agree. Get it with
/// [`use_theme`]; the setters write `<html>` and every [`ThemeScope`], like the customizer.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub struct Theme {
    choices: Choices,
    prefers_dark: ReadSignal<bool>,
}

/// The shared [`Theme`]. Reading it subscribes the component, so it re-renders on changes
/// made anywhere else.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub fn use_theme() -> Theme

/// Applies [`ThemeCustomizer`]'s choices to its children.
///
/// On the web and in desktop webviews the customizer sets them on `<html>` and this wrapper
/// is not needed. Renderers without JavaScript (dioxus-native) can't reach `<html>`, so wrap
/// the app in `ThemeScope` there. It is a `display: contents` box: it doesn't change layout.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn ThemeScope(children: Element) -> Element

/// Density presets defined in `theme.css` (`[data-density=...]`). `default` sets nothing.
pub const DENSITIES: [&str; 3];

/// Controls for the accent colour, corner radius, density and light/dark mode of the whole page.
///
/// It only sets `data-accent` / `data-density` / `data-theme` and `--radius` on `<html>`. Its
/// state is the shared [`use_theme`], so app controls (a header dark-mode switch) stay in step.
#[component]
pub fn ThemeCustomizer() -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::theme_customizer::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        // ThemeScope carries the choices where `<html>` can't be reached (native).
        ThemeScope { ThemeCustomizer {} }
    }
}
```

# TimePicker

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add time_picker` or `dx components add time_picker --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `form`, `icons`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::time_picker::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

A time input: one field per part (hours, minutes, optional seconds and AM/PM), each a spin button. Type digits and focus moves on by itself, or use the arrow keys. Written in Rust on plain inputs, with no JavaScript, so it also runs on the desktop webview and native.

```rust
let mut time = use_signal(|| Time::from_hms(9, 30, 0).ok());
rsx! {
    TimePicker {
        label: "Meeting",
        value: time(),
        on_value_change: move |t| time.set(t),
        minute_step: 15,                 // Up/Down move minutes by 15
        hour_cycle: HourCycle::H12,      // adds an AM/PM segment
        seconds: false,
    }
}
```

`value` is `Option<Time>` (`time::Time`, re-exported). It is `Some` once every segment is filled and `None` while any is empty; a half-typed entry stays on screen. `name` submits the time with a native `<form>` as `HH:MM`. `format_time` writes a time the way the picker shows it ("2:05 PM"); `format_iso_time` / `parse_iso_time` read and write `14:05`, the `<input type="time">` format.

## Earliest and latest time

`min` and `max` limit the picker to a range, inclusive: `min: Time::from_hms(9, 0, 0).ok(), max: Time::from_hms(17, 0, 0).ok()`. Up, Down, Home and End only stop on hours and minutes that can still make an allowed time (17 is the last hour, and at 17 the only minute is :00). Typing is not blocked: a typed 18:30 stays on screen, is reported in `on_value_change` and is marked invalid, the way React Aria's TimeField handles it. A `max` earlier than `min` means the range runs past midnight (22:00 to 02:00, a night shift). `TimeField` takes the same props and adds a range rule itself, with the message from `UiStrings::time_out_of_range` ("Choose a time from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM."); `time_between(min, max, message)` is that rule for your own fields.

In a `use_form` form, use `TimeField { field, label: "Start" }`: the field holds `14:05` (empty until complete, so `required()` works), is labelled, marked invalid with its error linked, and gets focus on a failed submit. For a time with a date, see `DateTimePicker`. When a plain native control is enough (mobile-first forms), `TextField { r#type: "time" }` gives the browser's own time input.

## Accessibility

- Role and name: a `role="group"` named by `label` (default "Time") or by a visible label through `labelled_by`. Each segment is an `<input role="spinbutton">` named "Hours", "Minutes", "Seconds" or "AM/PM" (from `UiStrings`), plus the visible label when `labelled_by` is set, with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext` ("Empty" while empty). `first_segment_id` lets a `<label for>` reach the hours.
- Typing: digits fill the focused segment and move on after two digits, or at once when no second digit could follow ("3" in hours). A or P (the first letters of `UiStrings::am`/`pm`) set AM/PM. Tab moves through the segments and out. The other keys are in the table below.
- Out of range: a time outside `min`/`max` sets `aria-invalid` on every segment; `TimeField` also shows the range message.
- Touch: segments are real inputs with `inputmode="numeric"`, so phones show a number pad.
- Reduced motion: no animation.

## Source

Original to this repo. The segment behaviour follows the WAI-ARIA spin button pattern and React Aria's TimeField (behaviour only, nothing copied). dioxus-primitives' date segments are private and `contenteditable`, so they could not be reused.

## Stability

Experimental. New on 2026-10-15, `min`/`max` on 2026-10-30; the props may change once a real app uses it. See `docs/STABILITY.md` in the kit repository.

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Spinbutton (one per segment)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/spinbutton/) pattern. Roles: `group`, `spinbutton`. Works on native (Blitz): yes.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| ArrowUp | On a segment | Increases the segment (minutes by `minute_step`), wrapping at the top. With `min`/`max`, skips values outside the range. | yes |
| ArrowDown | On a segment | Decreases the segment, wrapping at the bottom. With `min`/`max`, skips values outside the range. | yes |
| PageUp | On minutes or seconds | Increases by 10 (or the minute step, when larger). | yes |
| PageDown | On minutes or seconds | Decreases by 10 (or the minute step, when larger). | yes |
| Home | On a segment | Sets the lowest allowed value. | yes |
| End | On a segment | Sets the highest allowed value on the step grid. | yes |
| Backspace | On a segment | Undoes the digit just typed, then clears the segment, then moves to the segment before. | yes |
| Delete | On a segment | Clears the segment. | yes |
| ArrowRight | On a segment | Moves to the next segment. | yes |
| ArrowLeft | On a segment | Moves to the previous segment. | yes |

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
pub use time::Time;

/// 24-hour ("14:05") or 12-hour ("2:05 PM") entry.
pub enum HourCycle {
    #[default]
    H24,
    H12,
}

pub enum Period {
    Am,
    Pm,
}

/// One editable part of a [`TimePicker`].
pub enum TimeSegment {
    Hour,
    Minute,
    Second,
    Period,
}

/// A key (or a focus change) sent to one segment of a [`TimePicker`].
pub enum TimeKey {
    /// The segment at this index received focus: typing starts afresh there.
    Focus(usize),
    Digit(char),
    /// A letter that picks AM or PM (the component maps the localised first letters).
    SetPeriod(Period),
    Up,
    Down,
    PageUp,
    PageDown,
    Home,
    End,
    Backspace,
    Delete,
    Left,
    Right,
}

/// What [`TimeState::apply`] did.
pub enum TimeOutcome {
    /// Not ours; let the browser handle the key.
    Ignored,
    /// Only focus moved.
    Moved,
    /// A segment's value changed (and focus may have moved).
    Changed,
}

/// The segments of a [`TimePicker`] and which one has focus. Each part may be empty while
/// the user types. Pure, so the keyboard behaviour is tested without a browser
/// (`crates/ui/tests/time_picker.rs`).
pub struct TimeState {
    pub hour: Option<u8>,
    pub minute: Option<u8>,
    pub second: Option<u8>,
    pub period: Option<Period>,
    pub cycle: HourCycle,
    pub seconds: bool,
    /// Arrow keys move minutes by this much (1 to 30).
    pub minute_step: u8,
    /// Earliest allowed time. With [`max`](Self::max) earlier than this, the range runs past
    /// midnight (22:00 to 02:00).
    pub min: Option<Time>,
    /// Latest allowed time.
    pub max: Option<Time>,
    /// Index into [`segments`](Self::segments).
    pub focus: usize,
    /// Digits typed into the focused segment since it got focus.
    typed: String,
}

/// `"14:05"`, or `"14:05:09"` with seconds: the format of `<input type="time">`, used by
/// [`TimeField`](crate::components::form::TimeField) to keep a time in a form field.
pub fn format_iso_time(time: Time, seconds: bool) -> String

/// Reads `"14:05"` or `"14:05:09"`; anything else is `None`.
pub fn parse_iso_time(text: &str) -> Option<Time>

/// How a time reads in the picker's own format: `"14:05"` or `"2:05 PM"`.
pub fn format_time(time: Time, cycle: HourCycle, seconds: bool, strings: &UiStrings) -> String

/// A time input: one field per part (hours, minutes, optional seconds and AM/PM), each a
/// spin button. Type digits (focus moves on by itself), or use the arrow keys.
///
/// ```rust,ignore
/// let mut time = use_signal(|| None::<Time>);
/// TimePicker { value: time(), on_value_change: move |t| time.set(t), minute_step: 5 }
/// ```
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn TimePicker(
    /// The time; `None` while empty or only partly entered.
    #[props(default)]
    value: ReadSignal<Option<Time>>,
    /// Called with the new time once every segment is filled, and with `None` when one is
    /// cleared.
    #[props(default)]
    on_value_change: Callback<Option<Time>>,
    #[props(default)] hour_cycle: HourCycle,
    /// Add a seconds segment.
    #[props(default)]
    seconds: bool,
    /// Up and Down move minutes by this much; typing still takes any minute.
    #[props(default = 1)]
    minute_step: u8,
    /// Earliest allowed time. The arrow keys skip what is outside `min`..`max`; a typed time
    /// outside it is kept but marked invalid. A `max` earlier than `min` wraps past midnight.
    #[props(default)]
    min: Option<Time>,
    /// Latest allowed time (inclusive).
    #[props(default)]
    max: Option<Time>,
    #[props(default)] disabled: ReadSignal<bool>,
    #[props(default)] read_only: ReadSignal<bool>,
    /// Accessible name of the group when no visible label is linked with `labelled_by`.
    /// Defaults to "Time" from `UiStrings`.
    #[props(into, default)]
    label: Option<String>,
    /// Id of a visible label. The group and every segment are named by it ("Hours Start time").
    #[props(into, default)]
    labelled_by: Option<String>,
    /// Id for the first segment, so a `<label for>` can point at it.
    #[props(into, default)]
    first_segment_id: Option<String>,
    /// Marks every segment `aria-invalid`.
    #[props(default)]
    invalid: bool,
    /// Ids of a description and error message, read with every segment.
    #[props(into, default)]
    described_by: Option<String>,
    /// Submit the time with a native `<form>` under this name, as `HH:MM` or `HH:MM:SS`.
    #[props(into, default)]
    name: Option<String>,
    /// Called when focus leaves the picker.
    #[props(default)]
    on_blur: Callback<()>,
    /// The first segment's element, once mounted (for focus on a failed submit).
    #[props(default)]
    on_mounted: Callback<MountedEvent>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::Button;
use crate::components::form::*;
use crate::components::time_picker::*;
use crate::components::ui_strings::use_ui_strings;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let strings = use_ui_strings();
    let mut meeting = use_signal(|| Time::from_hms(9, 30, 0).ok());
    let form = use_form();
    let reminder = form.field(vec![custom(|v| {
        if v.is_empty() {
            Err("Enter a time.".to_string())
        } else {
            Ok(())
        }
    })]);
    // Its own form, so the reminder form above keeps one time field.
    let shift_form = use_form();
    let night_shift = shift_form.field(vec![]);
    let mut saved = use_signal(|| None::<String>);
    let meeting_text = meeting()
        .map(|t| format_time(t, HourCycle::H24, false, &strings))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "not set".to_string());
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: grid; gap: 1rem; justify-items: start;",
            TimePicker {
                label: "Meeting",
                value: meeting(),
                on_value_change: move |t| meeting.set(t),
                minute_step: 15,
            }
            p { style: "margin: 0;", "Meeting: {meeting_text}" }
            TimePicker { label: "Alarm", hour_cycle: HourCycle::H12, seconds: true }
            // Up and Down skip hours outside 9:00 to 17:00; a typed 18:00 is marked invalid.
            TimePicker {
                label: "Office hours",
                min: Time::from_hms(9, 0, 0).ok(),
                max: Time::from_hms(17, 0, 0).ok(),
                minute_step: 30,
            }
            Form {
                state: form,
                on_valid: move |_| {
                    let text = parse_iso_time(&reminder.value())
                        .map(|t| format_time(t, HourCycle::H12, false, &strings));
                    saved.set(text);
                },
                TimeField {
                    field: reminder,
                    label: "Reminder",
                    hour_cycle: HourCycle::H12,
                    description: "Type the hour, minutes, then A or P.",
                }
                Button { r#type: "submit", "Set reminder" }
            }
            Form { state: shift_form,
                TimeField {
                    field: night_shift,
                    label: "Night shift start",
                    min: Time::from_hms(22, 0, 0).ok(),
                    max: Time::from_hms(2, 0, 0).ok(),
                    description: "Between 22:00 and 02:00.",
                }
            }
            if let Some(text) = saved() {
                p { role: "status", style: "margin: 0;", "Reminder set for {text}" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Toast

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add toast` or `dx components add toast --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::toast::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Toast component is used to display brief messages to the user, typically for notifications or alerts. The toast messages can be focused with the keyboard with the `f6` key.

## Short form

For the common case use `ToastsExt` (in the prelude): it takes `&str`, `String` or a `(title, description)` pair, so no `.to_string()` or `ToastOptions::new()`:

```rust
let toasts = use_toast();
toasts.notify_success("Saved");
toasts.notify_error(("Failed", "Try again."));
```

`notify_warning` and `notify_info` work the same. Use the long form below for a duration or a permanent toast.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The Toast provider provides the toast context to its children and handler rendering any toasts that are sent.
ToastProvider {
    // Any child component can consume the toast context and send a toast to be rendered.
    button {
        onclick: |event: MouseEvent| {
            // Consume the toast context to send a toast.
            let toast_api = consume_toast();
            toast_api
                .error(
                    "Critical Error".to_string(),
                    ToastOptions::new()
                        .description("Some info you need")
                        .duration(Duration::from_secs(60))
                        .permanent(false),
                );
        },
        "Show Toast"
    }
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn ToastProvider(
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(Some(Duration::from_secs(5)))))]
    default_duration: ReadSignal<Option<Duration>>,
    #[props(default = ReadSignal::new(Signal::new(10)))] max_toasts: ReadSignal<usize>,
    #[props(default)] render_toast: Option<Callback<toast::ToastPropsWithOwner, Element>>,
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// A toast's title and optional description. Built from `"title"`, a `String`, or a
/// `(title, description)` pair.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub struct ToastMessage {
    pub title: String,
    pub description: Option<String>,
}
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::toast::{ToastProvider, ToastsExt};
use dioxus::prelude::*;
use dioxus_primitives::toast::use_toast;

/// Self-contained: the demo brings its own provider, so it also works on a docs page.
#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        ToastProvider { Buttons {} }
    }
}

#[component]
fn Buttons() -> Element {
    let toasts = use_toast();
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem;",
            Button {
                variant: ButtonVariant::Outline,
                onclick: move |_| toasts.notify_success(("Saved", "Your changes are stored.")),
                "Success toast"
            }
            Button {
                variant: ButtonVariant::Outline,
                onclick: move |_| toasts.notify_error(("Failed", "Something went wrong.")),
                "Error toast"
            }
            Button {
                variant: ButtonVariant::Outline,
                onclick: move |_| toasts.notify_info("Copied"),
                "Info toast"
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Toggle

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add toggle` or `dx components add toggle --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::toggle::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Toggle component is used to create a toggle button that can be pressed or unpressed. It is useful for creating a binary option, such as enabling or disabling a feature.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The Toggle component is used to create a toggle button that can be pressed or unpressed.
Toggle {
    // The contents of the toggle button.
    "Bold",
}
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Button (toggle)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/) pattern. Works on native (Blitz): yes.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Space | On the toggle | Presses or releases it. | yes |
| Enter | On the toggle | Presses or releases it. | yes |

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Toggle(props: ToggleProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::toggle::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        Toggle { width: "2rem", height: "2rem",
            em { "B" }
        }
    }
}
```
