# Toggle group

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add toggle_group` or `dx components add toggle_group --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::toggle_group::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Toggle Group component is used to create a group of toggle buttons that allows the user to select one or more options from a set. It is useful for creating a set of options.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The ToggleGroup component wraps all toggle items in the group.
ToggleGroup {
    // The orientation of the toggle group, true for horizontal and false for vertical.
    horizontal: true,
    // The toggle item represents each individual toggle button in the group.
    ToggleItem {
        // The index of the toggle item, used to determine the order in which items are focused.
        index: 0,
        // The contents of the toggle item button
        {children}
    }
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn ToggleGroup(props: ToggleGroupProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ToggleItem(props: ToggleItemProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::toggle_group::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {

        ToggleGroup { horizontal: true, allow_multiple_pressed: true, role: "group", aria_label: "Text style",
            ToggleItem { index: 0usize, aria_label: "Bold",
                b { "B" }
            }
            ToggleItem { index: 1usize, aria_label: "Italic",
                i { "I" }
            }
            ToggleItem { index: 2usize, aria_label: "Underline",
                u { "U" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Tool call

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add tool_call` or `dx components add tool_call --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-` (also copies `chat`, `collapsible`, `icons`, `ui_strings`).
- Import: `use crate::components::tool_call::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

What an agent did and is doing. `ToolCall` is one tool call: its name, a one-line summary and
its status in words, with arguments and output folded away until opened (it is a
[`Collapsible`](collapsible)). `actions` stay visible when closed: put Allow and Deny there
for `ToolStatus::NeedsApproval`. `AgentSteps` and `AgentStep` show a plan as an ordered list.

```rust
ToolCall { name: "read_file", summary: "src/date.rs", status: ToolStatus::Succeeded,
    pre { "{output}" }
}
AgentSteps { label: "Plan",
    AgentStep { status: ToolStatus::Succeeded, "Read the failing test" }
    AgentStep { status: ToolStatus::Running, "Patch the parser" }
}
```

## Accessibility

- Role and name: the header is a disclosure button (`aria-expanded`) whose name includes the
  tool, the summary and the status, so the status is never colour or icon alone. Glyphs are
  decorative.
- Inside a [`ChatLog`](chat), a call that turns `Failed` or `NeedsApproval` is announced
  ("deploy_preview: Needs approval") through the log's announcer; quieter changes are not.
- `AgentSteps` is an `ol` with a required `label`; the running step has
  `aria-current="step"`, and each step's status is read after its text.
- Reduced motion: the running glyph turns slowly instead of spinning (like `Spinner`).

## Source

Original to this repo. The idea of a status glyph, tool steps and an approval card comes from
the agent components in deeplethe/solid-glass (MIT); no code was copied.

## Stability

Experimental: new on 2026-10-30, and the props may change once a real agent app uses them (docs/STABILITY.md).

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Disclosure (Show/Hide)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/) pattern. Works on native (Blitz): yes.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | On a tool call's header | Shows or hides its details. | yes |
| Space | On a tool call's header | Shows or hides its details. | yes |

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
/// Where a tool call or agent step is.
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
pub enum ToolStatus {
    #[default]
    Queued,
    Running,
    Succeeded,
    Failed,
    /// Waits for the reader to allow it (put the Allow and Deny buttons in `actions`).
    NeedsApproval,
}

/// One tool call an agent made: its name, a one-line summary and its status in words, with
/// the input and output folded away until opened. The status is never colour alone, and a call
/// that fails or needs approval is announced through the [`ChatLog`](crate::components::chat::ChatLog)
/// it sits in.
///
/// Opens and closes like [`Collapsible`] (Enter or Space on the header). `actions` stay visible
/// when it is closed: put Allow and Deny there for [`ToolStatus::NeedsApproval`].
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn ToolCall(
    /// The tool's name, shown in code type ("search_docs").
    #[props(into)]
    name: String,
    #[props(default)] status: ToolStatus,
    /// One line about this call ("3 results", "src/main.rs").
    #[props(into)]
    summary: Option<String>,
    /// Start open.
    #[props(default)]
    open: bool,
    /// Buttons under the header, shown even when closed.
    actions: Option<Element>,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    /// Details: arguments, output, logs.
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// An agent's plan or progress as an ordered list. The running step is marked
/// `aria-current="step"`, and each step's status is read after its text.
///
/// ```
/// # use dioxus::prelude::*;
/// # use ui::prelude::*;
/// # fn app() -> Element {
/// rsx! {
///     AgentSteps { label: "Plan",
///         AgentStep { status: ToolStatus::Succeeded, "Read the issue" }
///         AgentStep { status: ToolStatus::Running, "Write the fix" }
///         AgentStep { "Run the tests" }
///     }
/// }
/// # }
/// ```
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn AgentSteps(
    /// The list's accessible name ("Plan", "Progress").
    #[props(into)]
    label: String,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// One step of [`AgentSteps`].
///
/// # Stability
///
/// Experimental: may change in any release (docs/STABILITY.md).
#[component]
pub fn AgentStep(
    #[props(default)] status: ToolStatus,
    #[props(extends=GlobalAttributes)] attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonSize, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::tool_call::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut approval = use_signal(|| ToolStatus::NeedsApproval);
    let deploy_step = match approval() {
        ToolStatus::NeedsApproval => ToolStatus::Queued,
        other => other,
    };
    rsx! {
        div { display: "flex", flex_direction: "column", gap: "1rem", max_width: "36rem",
            AgentSteps { label: "Plan",
                AgentStep { status: ToolStatus::Succeeded, "Read the failing test" }
                AgentStep { status: ToolStatus::Running, "Patch the date parser" }
                AgentStep { status: deploy_step, "Deploy the preview" }
            }
            ToolCall {
                name: "read_file",
                summary: "src/date.rs",
                status: ToolStatus::Succeeded,
                pre { "fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Date> {{ … }}" }
            }
            ToolCall {
                name: "run_tests",
                summary: "cargo test date",
                status: ToolStatus::Running,
                pre { "running 12 tests…" }
            }
            ToolCall {
                name: "deploy_preview",
                summary: "preview-142",
                status: approval(),
                actions: (approval() == ToolStatus::NeedsApproval).then(|| {
                    rsx! {
                        Button {
                            size: ButtonSize::Sm,
                            onclick: move |_| approval.set(ToolStatus::Running),
                            "Allow"
                        }
                        Button {
                            size: ButtonSize::Sm,
                            variant: ButtonVariant::Outline,
                            onclick: move |_| approval.set(ToolStatus::Failed),
                            "Deny"
                        }
                    }
                }),
                pre { "{{ \"branch\": \"fix/date-parser\" }}" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Toolbar

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add toolbar` or `dx components add toolbar --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::toolbar::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The toolbar component is a flexible and customizable component that can be used to create a variety of toolbars. It can be used to create a simple toolbar with a title, or a more complex toolbar with multiple buttons and actions.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The Toolbar component wraps all toolbar items.
Toolbar {
    // The aria_label of the toolbar, used for accessibility purposes.
    aria_label: "Toolbar Title",
    // The ToolbarButton component represents each individual button in the toolbar.
    ToolbarButton {
        // The index of the toolbar button, used to determine the order in which buttons are focused.
        index: 0,
        on_click: |_: ()| {
            // This callback is triggered when the button is clicked.
        },
        // The contents of the toolbar button
        {children}
    }
    // The ToolbarSeparator component represents a separator line in the toolbar.
    ToolbarSeparator {
        // The orientation of the separator, true for horizontal and false for vertical.
        horizontal: true,
        // The decorative property controls if the separator is decorative and should not be visible to screen readers.
        decorative: false,
    }
}
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

Follows the WAI-ARIA [Toolbar](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/) pattern. Roles: `toolbar`. Works on native (Blitz): yes.

| Key | When | What it does | Native |
|---|---|---|---|
| ArrowRight | On a toolbar button | Moves focus to the next button. | yes |
| ArrowLeft | On a toolbar button | Moves focus to the previous button. | yes |
| Home | On a toolbar button | Moves focus to the first button. | yes |

Known gaps:

- Home works, End does not: the primitive moves focus to an item index that does not exist.

Every row is run as a keyboard test on the web, and on native where it says yes. Generated from the component's `contract.toml`.

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Toolbar(props: ToolbarProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ToolbarButton(props: ToolbarButtonProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ToolbarSeparator(props: ToolbarSeparatorProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn ToolbarGroup(
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    #[props(extends = div)]
    attributes: Vec<Attribute>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::toolbar::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
fn ToggleToolbarButton(
    index: usize,
    is_on: bool,
    on_click: Callback<()>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element {
    rsx! {
        ToolbarButton {
            index,
            on_click,
            "data-state": if is_on { "on" } else { "off" },
            background: if is_on { "var(--light, var(--primary-color-5)) var(--dark, var(--primary-color-6))" } else { "" },
            color: if is_on { "var(--secondary-color-1)" } else { "" },
            {children}
        }
    }
}

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut is_bold = use_signal(|| false);
    let mut is_italic = use_signal(|| false);
    let mut is_underline = use_signal(|| false);
    let mut text_align = use_signal(|| "left".to_string());

    rsx! {
        div { class: "dx-toolbar-demo",
            Toolbar { aria_label: "Text formatting",
                ToolbarGroup {
                    ToggleToolbarButton {
                        index: 0usize,
                        is_on: is_bold(),
                        on_click: move |_| is_bold.toggle(),
                        "Bold"
                    }
                    ToggleToolbarButton {
                        index: 1usize,
                        is_on: is_italic(),
                        on_click: move |_| is_italic.toggle(),
                        "Italic"
                    }
                    ToggleToolbarButton {
                        index: 2usize,
                        is_on: is_underline(),
                        on_click: move |_| is_underline.toggle(),
                        "Underline"
                    }
                }
                ToolbarSeparator {}
                ToolbarGroup {
                    ToggleToolbarButton {
                        index: 3usize,
                        is_on: text_align() == "left",
                        on_click: move |_| text_align.set("left".to_string()),
                        "Align Left"
                    }
                    ToggleToolbarButton {
                        index: 4usize,
                        is_on: text_align() == "center",
                        on_click: move |_| text_align.set("center".to_string()),
                        "Align Center"
                    }
                    ToggleToolbarButton {
                        index: 5usize,
                        is_on: text_align() == "right",
                        on_click: move |_| text_align.set("right".to_string()),
                        "Align Right"
                    }
                }
            }
            p {
                max_width: "30rem",
                text_align: "{text_align}",
                font_weight: if is_bold() { "bold" } else { "normal" },
                font_style: if is_italic() { "italic" } else { "normal" },
                text_decoration: if is_underline() { "underline" } else { "none" },
                "This is a sample text that will be formatted according to the toolbar buttons you click. Try clicking the buttons above to see how the text formatting changes."
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Tooltip

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add tooltip` or `dx components add tooltip --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::tooltip::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The Tooltip component is used to display additional information when a user hovers over an element.

## Component Structure

```rust
// The Tooltip component wraps the trigger element and the content that will be displayed on hover.
Tooltip {
    // The TooltipTrigger contains the elements that will trigger the tooltip to display when hovered over.
    TooltipTrigger {
        // The elements that will trigger the tooltip when hovered over.
        {children}
    }
    // The TooltipContent contains the content that will be displayed when the user hovers over the trigger.
    TooltipContent {
        // The side of the TooltipTrigger where the content will be displayed. Can be one of Top, Right, Bottom, or Left.
        side: ContentSide::Top,
        // The alignment of the TooltipContent relative to the TooltipTrigger. Can be one of Start, Center, or End.
        align: ContentAlign::Center,
        // The content of the tooltip, which can include text, images, or any other elements.
        {children}
    }
}
```

## API

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Tooltip(props: TooltipProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn TooltipTrigger(props: TooltipTriggerProps) -> Element

#[component]
pub fn TooltipContent(props: TooltipContentProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::tooltip::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;
use dioxus_primitives::ContentSide;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        Tooltip {
            TooltipTrigger { "Hover or focus me" }
            TooltipContent { side: ContentSide::Top, "Add to library" }
        }
    }
}
```

# UiStrings

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add ui_strings` or `dx components add ui_strings --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::ui_strings::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

Every word the kit shows or announces on its own ("Next", "Clear", "No results found.", "Go to next page", screen-reader names) lives in one `UiStrings` struct with English defaults. Wrap the app in `UiStringsProvider` to translate them, and pass a signal to switch language at runtime. Text you pass as props (labels, placeholders) always wins.

```rust
let strings = use_signal(|| UiStrings { next: "Suivant".into(), ..UiStrings::default() });
rsx! { UiStringsProvider { strings, App {} } }
```

Templates use `{name}` placeholders (`"Select {row}"`, `"Showing {first}–{last} of {total} rows"`), filled with `fill`.

Not covered: calendar weekday names (use the calendar's `day_name` prop), month names (dioxus-primitives), and the field validators' messages (pass your own validator).

## Accessibility

- Role and name: renders no element of its own; it changes the accessible names inside it.
- Keyboard: none.
- Reduced motion: no motion.

## Source

Original to this repo. The idea follows thaw's `ConfigProvider` (MIT).

## API

```rust
/// Every string the kit renders on its own. Fields are grouped by component.
pub struct UiStrings {
    // Shared
    pub previous: String,
    pub next: String,
    pub loading: String,
    pub filter: String,
    /// Name of icon-only close buttons (sheet).
    pub close: String,
    // Pagination
    pub go_to_previous_page: String,
    pub go_to_next_page: String,
    // Data table
    pub filter_rows: String,
    pub select_all_rows: String,
    /// `{row}` is the row's first cell.
    pub select_row: String,
    pub no_rows: String,
    pub table_pages: String,
    /// `{count}` is the number of rows.
    pub row_count: String,
    /// `{first}`, `{last}` and `{total}` are row numbers.
    pub showing_rows: String,
    /// `{page}` and `{pages}` are page numbers.
    pub page_of: String,
    // Multi-select
    pub select_placeholder: String,
    /// `{label}` is the multi-select's name.
    pub filter_named: String,
    /// `{label}` is the multi-select's name.
    pub options_named: String,
    pub no_options: String,
    /// `{count}` is the number of selected options.
    pub selected_count: String,
    pub clear: String,
    pub done: String,
    // Command palette
    pub command_palette: String,
    pub command_help: String,
    pub search_commands: String,
    pub search_commands_placeholder: String,
    pub commands: String,
    pub no_results: String,
    // One-time code
    pub otp_label: String,
    /// `{label}` is the code's name, `{n}` the box number and `{total}` the box count.
    pub otp_character: String,
    // Marquee
    pub play: String,
    pub pause: String,
    pub scrolling_content: String,
    /// Read after Play or Pause by screen readers.
    pub scrolling: String,
    // Dropzone
    pub drop_files: String,
    pub selected_files: String,
    pub only_one_file: String,
    /// `{types}` is the accepted file types.
    pub accepts: String,
    /// `{name}` is the file name.
    pub not_accepted: String,
    /// `{name}` is the file name, `{size}` the limit.
    pub too_large: String,
    // Navigation
    pub breadcrumb: String,
    pub main_navigation: String,
    pub toggle_sidebar: String,
    pub sidebar: String,
    pub sidebar_description: String,
    pub sortable_list: String,
    /// `{label}` is the carousel's name.
    pub slides: String,
    // Date picker
    pub show_calendar: String,
    // Time picker
    pub time: String,
    pub date_and_time: String,
    pub hours: String,
    pub minutes: String,
    pub seconds: String,
    /// Name of the AM/PM segment.
    pub day_period: String,
    pub am: String,
    pub pm: String,
    /// Read for a time segment that has no value yet.
    pub empty_value: String,
    // Chart
    pub no_data: String,
    /// Opens a chart's data table.
    pub show_data: String,
    /// Header of a chart table's first column.
    pub chart_category: String,
    /// Header of a single-series chart's value column.
    pub chart_value: String,
    /// Header of a pie chart's percentage column.
    pub chart_share: String,
    /// Radial chart summary. `{value}`, `{max}` and `{percent}` are filled in.
    pub value_of_max: String,
    /// Read when a keyboard-explorable chart gets focus.
    pub chart_keys_hint: String,
    /// The focused point of a chart. `{point}`, `{index}` and `{count}` are filled in.
    pub chart_point: String,
    /// Read for a time picker whose time is outside `min`/`max`. `{min}` and `{max}` are
    /// filled in.
    pub time_out_of_range: String,
    // Link
    /// Read after a link that opens in a new tab.
    pub opens_in_new_tab: String,
    // Skip link
    pub skip_to_content: String,
    // Chat
    /// The chat log's button when the reader has scrolled up.
    pub jump_to_latest: String,
    /// The same button once a message arrived below.
    pub new_messages: String,
    /// Typing indicator. `{author}` is who is typing.
    pub typing: String,
    /// Announced when a streamed reply ends. `{author}` and `{text}` are filled in.
    pub message_from: String,
    /// Read after the composer's name: how to send.
    pub composer_hint: String,
    pub send: String,
    pub stop: String,
    // Tool calls
    pub tool_queued: String,
    pub tool_running: String,
    pub tool_succeeded: String,
    pub tool_failed: String,
    pub tool_needs_approval: String,
    /// Announced when a tool call fails or needs approval. `{name}` and `{status}`.
    pub tool_status: String,
    // Number field
    /// The - button's name. `{label}` is the field's name.
    pub decrease: String,
    /// The + button's name. `{label}` is the field's name.
    pub increase: String,
}

/// Provides `strings` to every kit component below it. Pass a signal to switch language
/// at runtime.
#[component]
pub fn UiStringsProvider(strings: ReadSignal<UiStrings>, children: Element) -> Element

/// The strings from the nearest [`UiStringsProvider`], or English.
pub fn use_ui_strings() -> UiStrings

/// Replaces each `{name}` in `template` with its value.
///
/// ```
/// assert_eq!(ui::components::ui_strings::fill("Select {row}", &[("row", "Ada")]), "Select Ada");
/// ```
pub fn fill(template: &str, values: &[(&str, &str)]) -> String
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::button::{Button, ButtonVariant};
use crate::components::carousel::{Carousel, CarouselItem};
use crate::components::spinner::Spinner;
use crate::components::ui_strings::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

fn french() -> UiStrings {
    UiStrings {
        previous: "Précédent".into(),
        next: "Suivant".into(),
        loading: "Chargement".into(),
        ..UiStrings::default()
    }
}

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    let mut french_on = use_signal(|| false);
    let strings = use_memo(move || {
        if french_on() {
            french()
        } else {
            UiStrings::default()
        }
    });
    rsx! {
        div { style: "display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; max-width: 32rem;",
            div { role: "group", "aria-label": "Language", style: "display: flex; gap: 0.5rem;",
                Button {
                    variant: if french_on() { ButtonVariant::Outline } else { ButtonVariant::Primary },
                    "aria-pressed": "{!french_on()}",
                    onclick: move |_| french_on.set(false),
                    "English"
                }
                Button {
                    variant: if french_on() { ButtonVariant::Primary } else { ButtonVariant::Outline },
                    "aria-pressed": "{french_on()}",
                    onclick: move |_| french_on.set(true),
                    "Français"
                }
            }
            UiStringsProvider { strings,
                div { style: "display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem;",
                    Spinner {}
                    span { "The spinner's name and the carousel buttons follow the language." }
                }
                Carousel { label: "Plans",
                    for (i , name) in ["Starter", "Team", "Business"].into_iter().enumerate() {
                        CarouselItem { label: "{i + 1} of 3", strong { "{name}" } }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Virtual list

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add virtual_list` or `dx components add virtual_list --git https://github.com/Amit-1of1/Rust-UI-`.
- Import: `use crate::components::virtual_list::*;` after copying, or `use ui::prelude::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate.

The VirtualList component virtualizes large lists by rendering only visible rows plus a buffer. It is useful for long, dynamic-height datasets where rendering every row at once would be expensive.

## Component Structure

```rust
VirtualList {
    // Total number of items.
    count: 2000usize,
    // Render buffer (approximate row count) above and below viewport.
    buffer: 8usize,
    // Row renderer callback receives the absolute index.
    render_item: move |idx: usize| rsx! {
        article { key: "{idx}", "{rows[idx].title}" }
    },
}
```

## API

```rust
pub use dioxus_primitives::virtual_list::VirtualListProps;

/// Styled wrapper around the primitive `VirtualList`.
#[component]
pub fn VirtualList(props: VirtualListProps) -> Element
```

## Example

```rust
use crate::components::virtual_list::*;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn Demo() -> Element {
    rsx! {
        div { class: "dx-virtual-list-demo",
            p { class: "dx-virtual-list-subtitle", "Scroll this page to verify virtualized rendering with dynamic row heights." }
            style { r#".dx-virtual-list-container {{
  position: relative;
  max-height: 36rem;
  contain: layout paint;
  overflow-y: auto;
}}

.dx-virtual-list-demo {{
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  margin: 0 auto;
  gap: 0.75rem;
}}

.dx-virtual-list-demo .dx-virtual-list-subtitle {{
  margin: 0;
  margin-bottom: 0.75rem;
  color: var(--secondary-color-5);
  font-size: 0.9rem;
}}

.dx-virtual-list-card {{
  padding: 0.75rem 0.9rem;
  border: 1px solid var(--primary-color-6);
  border-radius: 0.625rem;
  background: var(--primary-color-2);
}}

.dx-virtual-list-card h3 {{
  margin: 0 0 0.3rem;
  color: var(--secondary-color-1);
  font-size: 0.95rem;
}}

.dx-virtual-list-card p {{
  margin: 0;
  color: var(--secondary-color-4);
  font-size: 0.875rem;
  line-height: 1.4;
}}"# }
            VirtualList {
                count: 2000usize,
                buffer: 12usize,
                // Estimate height based on content pattern (idx % 6 repeats)
                // Measured: min=68.4px (0 repeats), max=127.2px (5 repeats)
                estimate_size: |idx| {
                    let base_height = 68;
                    let repeats: usize = idx % 6;
                    let lines = repeats.div_ceil(2); // 2 repeats per line
                    let per_line = 20;
                    base_height + lines as u32 * per_line
                },
                render_item: move |idx: usize| {
                    let extra_text = "Extra content to vary row height. ".repeat(idx % 6);
                    rsx! {
                        article { class: "dx-virtual-list-card",
                            h3 { "#{idx + 1} - Item {idx + 1}" }
                            p { "Virtualized row preview. Index = {idx}" }
                            p { "{extra_text}" }
                        }
                    }
                },
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# Dashboard 01

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add dashboard_01` (also copies `badge`, `button`, `card`, `chart`, `dropdown_menu`, `empty`, `icons`, `separator`, `sidebar`, `switch`, `table`, `theme_customizer`).
- Import: `use crate::blocks::dashboard_01::*;` after copying, or `use ui::blocks::dashboard_01::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate's `blocks` feature (internal).

An app shell plus an overview page: a sidebar that collapses to icons, a header with a dark-mode switch and an account menu, key figures, a line and a bar chart, and a recent-orders table. Built from `sidebar`, `card`, `chart`, `table`, `badge`, `dropdown_menu`, `switch`, `empty` and `theme_customizer` (for `use_theme`).

```sh
rust-ui add dashboard_01
```

Use the whole screen, or only the shell around your own pages:

```rust
let mut page = use_signal(|| "home".to_string());
rsx! {
    DashboardShell {
        brand: "Acme",
        nav: vec![
            NavItem::new("home", "Home", rsx! { House {} }),
            NavItem::new("reports", "Reports", rsx! { ChartBar {} }),
        ],
        active: page(),
        on_navigate: move |id| page.set(id),
        on_sign_out: move |_| sign_out(),
        match page().as_str() {
            "home" => rsx! { Home {} },
            _ => rsx! { Reports {} },
        }
    }
}
```

## Props (`DashboardShell`)

- `brand: String`: the name in the sidebar and header; its first letter is the logo.
- `nav: Vec<NavItem>`: `NavItem::new(id, label, icon)`.
- `active: String`: the current page's `id`. Its label becomes the page `h1`.
- `on_navigate: Callback<String>`: called with the clicked item's `id`.
- `initials`, `on_sign_out`: the account menu.

## Accessibility

- The sidebar is a `nav` landmark named "Main"; the current page's link has `aria-current="page"`.
- `SidebarInset` is the page's `main`; it starts with the page title as an `h1`, and each card title is an `h2`.
- Collapsed to icons, every link keeps its name (and a tooltip); icons are hidden from screen readers.
- Charts are `role="img"` with a text summary; the table has a caption and right-aligned numbers.

## API

```rust
/// One link in the [`DashboardShell`] sidebar.
pub struct NavItem {
    pub id: String,
    pub label: String,
    /// Shown before the label and alone when the sidebar is collapsed. Hidden from screen readers.
    pub icon: Element,
}

/// The frame of an app screen: a collapsible sidebar (to icons), a header with the sidebar
/// toggle, a dark-mode switch and an account menu, and a `<main>` with the page title as its
/// `h1`. Put the page in `children`.
#[component]
pub fn DashboardShell(
    #[props(into)] brand: String,
    nav: Vec<NavItem>,
    /// The `id` of the current page; its link gets `aria-current` and its label is the `h1`.
    #[props(into)]
    active: String,
    #[props(default)] on_navigate: Callback<String>,
    /// Two letters for the account button.
    #[props(into, default = "ME".to_string())]
    initials: String,
    #[props(default)] on_sign_out: Callback<()>,
    children: Element,
) -> Element

/// A complete dashboard screen: [`DashboardShell`] with an overview page (key figures, two
/// charts, recent orders) and placeholders for the other pages. Replace the sample data with
/// your own.
#[component]
pub fn Dashboard01() -> Element
```

# Login 01

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add login_01` (also copies `alert`, `button`, `card`, `form`, `link`).
- Import: `use crate::blocks::login_01::*;` after copying, or `use ui::blocks::login_01::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate's `blocks` feature (internal).

A centred sign-in card: email, password, "remember me", a forgot-password link and a sign-up link. Built from `card`, `form`, `alert` and `link`.

```sh
rust-ui add login_01   # copies src/blocks/login_01 and the components it uses
```

```rust
let mut error = use_signal(|| None::<String>);
rsx! {
    Login01 {
        error: error(),
        on_submit: move |d: LoginDetails| {
            if d.password != "secret" {
                error.set(Some("Wrong email or password.".into()));
            }
        },
    }
}
```

## Props

- `on_submit: Callback<LoginDetails>`: called only with valid fields (`email`, `password`, `remember`).
- `error: Option<String>`: a server message shown in a destructive `Alert`.
- `busy: bool`: disables the button while you wait for the server.
- `forgot_href`, `sign_up_href`: where the two links go.

## Accessibility

- The block is the page's `main` landmark.
- The page heading is an `h1` ("Sign in"); the form is named "Sign in".
- Inputs carry `autocomplete="email"` and `"current-password"`, so password managers fill them.
- Errors are tied to their inputs with `aria-describedby`; a failed submit focuses the first one.
- The server error is a `role="alert"`, so it is announced when it appears.

## API

```rust
/// What the person typed into [`Login01`].
pub struct LoginDetails {
    pub email: String,
    pub password: String,
    pub remember: bool,
}

/// A centred sign-in card: email, password, "remember me", a forgot-password link and a link
/// to sign up. Fields are checked before `on_submit` runs; a failed submit moves focus to the
/// first field that needs fixing.
#[component]
pub fn Login01(
    /// Called with valid details. Check them on your server, then set `error` or move on.
    #[props(default)]
    on_submit: Callback<LoginDetails>,
    /// A message from your server, such as "Wrong email or password." Announced when it appears.
    #[props(into, default)]
    error: Option<String>,
    /// While true the button is disabled and says "Signing in…".
    #[props(default)]
    busy: bool,
    #[props(into, default = "#forgot-password".to_string())] forgot_href: String,
    #[props(into, default = "#sign-up".to_string())] sign_up_href: String,
) -> Element
```

# Settings 01

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add settings_01` (also copies `alert_dialog`, `button`, `card`, `form`, `label`, `switch`, `tabs`, `theme_customizer`).
- Import: `use crate::blocks::settings_01::*;` after copying, or `use ui::blocks::settings_01::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate's `blocks` feature (internal).

A settings page in four tabs: Profile (name, email, bio), Notifications (email switches), Appearance (the theme customizer) and Account (delete, behind a confirmation). Built from `tabs`, `card`, `form`, `switch`, `label`, `theme_customizer` and `alert_dialog`.

```sh
rust-ui add settings_01
```

It stands alone (its root is the page's `main`), or fits inside `DashboardShell` from `dashboard_01` with `embedded: true`, which makes the root a plain `div` because the shell already has a `main`:

```rust
rsx! {
    Settings01 {
        profile: Profile { name: "Ada".into(), email: "ada@example.com".into(), bio: String::new() },
        on_save_profile: move |p: Profile| save(p),
        on_email_prefs: move |e: EmailPrefs| save_prefs(e),
        on_delete_account: move |_| delete_account(),
    }
}
```

## Props

- `profile: Profile`: the values the form starts with.
- `on_save_profile: Callback<Profile>`: called only with valid fields.
- `email_prefs: EmailPrefs`, `on_email_prefs: Callback<EmailPrefs>`: called on every switch change.
- `on_delete_account: Callback<()>`: called after the person confirms.
- `embedded: bool`: set inside a layout that already has a `main` and an `h1` (the block then drops its own "Settings" `h1`).

## Accessibility

- The page title is an `h1` and each card title an `h2`; the tab list is named "Settings sections".
- Tabs use manual activation: arrow keys move, Enter or Space opens (docs/GUARDRAILS.md).
- "Saved." is a `role="status"` line, so it is announced without moving focus.
- Each switch is labelled by its row text; deleting asks first in an alert dialog, which traps focus and returns it on close.

## API

```rust
/// The profile fields of [`Settings01`].
pub struct Profile {
    pub name: String,
    pub email: String,
    pub bio: String,
}

/// Which emails the person wants, from the Notifications tab of [`Settings01`].
pub struct EmailPrefs {
    pub product: bool,
    pub security: bool,
    pub weekly: bool,
}

/// A settings page in four tabs: Profile (a form), Notifications (switches), Appearance
/// (the theme customizer) and Account (a danger zone behind a confirmation).
#[component]
pub fn Settings01(
    /// The values the profile form starts with.
    #[props(default)]
    profile: Profile,
    /// Called with a valid profile from "Save".
    #[props(default)]
    on_save_profile: Callback<Profile>,
    #[props(default)] email_prefs: EmailPrefs,
    /// Called on every switch change.
    #[props(default)]
    on_email_prefs: Callback<EmailPrefs>,
    /// Called once the person confirms "Delete account".
    #[props(default)]
    on_delete_account: Callback<()>,
    /// Set when the page already has a `<main>` and an `h1`, as inside `DashboardShell`;
```

---

# Sign-up 01

- Copy into your app: `rust-ui add signup_01` (also copies `alert`, `button`, `card`, `form`, `input_otp`, `link`).
- Import: `use crate::blocks::signup_01::*;` after copying, or `use ui::blocks::signup_01::*;` with the `rust-ui-kit` crate's `blocks` feature (internal).

A two-step sign-up card: name, email, password typed twice and a terms checkbox, then a 6-digit email code. Built from `card`, `form`, `input_otp`, `alert` and `link`.

```sh
rust-ui add signup_01
```

```rust
rsx! {
    Signup01 {
        on_submit: move |d: SignupDetails| send_code(&d.email),
        on_verify: move |code: String| check_code(&code),
        on_resend: move |_| resend(),
    }
}
```

## Props

- `on_submit: Callback<SignupDetails>`: called only with valid fields (`name`, `email`, `password`); the card then shows the code step.
- `on_verify: Option<Callback<String>>`: called with all 6 digits. Leave it out to stop after step one.
- `on_resend: Callback<()>`: the "Send a new code" button.
- `error: Option<String>`: a server message for the current step, shown in a destructive `Alert`.
- `terms_href`, `sign_in_href`: where the two links go.

## Accessibility

- The block is the page's `main` landmark.
- Each step has its own `h1`. Moving to the code step puts focus on its heading, so screen readers announce the new step.
- "Confirm password" checks that both passwords match; errors are tied to their inputs and a failed submit focuses the first one.
- Password inputs use `autocomplete="new-password"`, so password managers offer to generate one.
- The code boxes are one labelled group ("Verification code"); a short code is reported in a `role="alert"` line.

## API

```rust
/// What the person typed into [`Signup01`].
pub struct SignupDetails {
    pub name: String,
    pub email: String,
    pub password: String,
}

/// A two-step sign-up card. Step one asks for name, email, a password (typed twice) and
/// agreement to the terms. Step two asks for the 6-digit code you emailed; leave out
/// `on_verify` to skip it.
#[component]
pub fn Signup01(
    /// Called with valid details. Send the code here; the card then shows the code step.
    #[props(default)]
    on_submit: Callback<SignupDetails>,
    /// Called with the 6-digit code. Without it the card stops after step one.
    on_verify: Option<Callback<String>>,
    /// Called from "Send a new code".
    #[props(default)]
    on_resend: Callback<()>,
    /// A message from your server for the current step, such as "That code has expired."
    #[props(into, default)]
    error: Option<String>,
    #[props(into, default = "#terms".to_string())] terms_href: String,
    #[props(into, default = "#sign-in".to_string())] sign_in_href: String,
) -> Element
```
